The School of Public and Allied Health at Prairie View A&M University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor in the Division of Health Sciences. The successful candidate will join a growing and dynamic team dedicated to preparing students for careers in the health and health sciences fields. The role involves leadership and management of field education, student advising, and participation in department, college, university, and professional service.

***The salary is determined in accordance with the University’s compensation structure and will be commensurate with the candidates’ education and experience, within the assigned salary range for this position.***

**Responsibilities:**

  

* Teach graduate and undergraduate courses within the field of expertise.
* Develop new courses and instructional materials that align with program needs.
* Utilize innovative teaching strategies, including technology-enhanced and online learning.
* Supervise student projects, internships, and independent studies.
* Establish and maintain an active research agenda leading to peer-reviewed publications.
* Pursue internal and external funding opportunities to support scholarly activities.
* Engage in collaborative research within the School of Public and Allied Health and across disciplines.
* Advise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students in academic planning, research, and professional development.
* Support students in pursuing experiential learning, including research, community engagement, and study abroad opportunities.
* Participate in program assessment, accreditation activities, and curriculum development.
* Serve on division, school, and university committees.
* Engage in professional service through memberships, conference presentations, and editorial/reviewer roles.
* Contribute to community outreach
* and partnerships that promote health access and allied health initiatives.

**Required Education and Experience:**

  

* Ph.D, Ed.D., in Health Sciences, or a closely related discipline
* Two years of college or university teaching.

**Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

  

* Excellent communication, written and technology skills.
* Demonstrate proficiency in written and oral communication skills for all audiences.
* Demonstrate ability for effective teaching and scholarship.
* Demonstrate support of professional organizations in the discipline and have potential for obtaining external funding.

**Preferred Education and Experience:**

  

* Three years of college or university teaching.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Social Work
jobs.description:
### **Assistant Professor, Social Work**

* 497098

* Full-Time

* Social Work

**Department**: Social Work **Salary**: Commensurate with Experience/Education'

**Description**:

***This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.***

  

The University of Houston-Downtown Social Work Program is seeking candidates for one (1) position at the rank of Tenure-Track Assistant Professor. The successful candidate will teach a 4-3 course load over the two long semesters in a variety of modalities; demonstrate a theory-based and community-engaged teaching philosophy; engage in a research agenda that supports the knowledge base of social work practice; and engage in service to the institution, community, and profession.
  
  
**Required Qualifications**

The individual selected will have:

* Earned a doctoral degree (PhD/DSW) in Social Work or a closely related field, and a MSW from a Council of Social Work Education (CSWE)-accredited social work program
* At least two (2) years of full-time post-MSW practice experience with systems of various sizes
* Experience in teaching or demonstrated potential for excellence in teaching at the college level
* Experience in research and scholarship or demonstrated potential to conduct research and scholarship as part of a clearly articulated and evolving social work research agenda
* Demonstrated commitment to service to the university, community, and/or profession

Preferred Qualifications

* PhD/DSW in Social Work (or be ABD)
* LMSW or LCSW (or is licensure-eligible) issued in the State of Texas
* Experience with face-to-face, hybrid, and online instructional modalities at the undergraduate and/or graduate social work course level
* Ability to teach generalist social work courses at all system levels (micro, mezzo, and macro)
* Experience in developing and implementing service learning and experiential learning activities in curricular and co-curricular settings
* History of publishing peer-reviewed articles and/or publishing in peer-reviewed academic journals of high quality
* Demonstrated experience or commitment to fostering community engagement programs and activities
* Knowledge of and experience working with an array of social service, public health, criminal justice, and/or healthcare agencies in the Greater Houston or other urban areas

To be considered for this position, the candidate must submit:

* A cover letter detailing interest in the tenure-track Assistant Professor faculty position and potential for fit in the UHD Social Work Program
* An updated Curriculum Vitae (please include a list of courses previously taught along with the modality)
* Teaching philosophy statement
* Research/scholarly agenda statement
* Unofficial graduate transcripts showing completion of an MSW degree from a CSWE-accredited program and unofficial transcripts showing completion or progress toward the doctoral degree
* Names and contact information for three professional references (letters will be requested if candidates advance in consideration for the position)

**Review of applications will begin immediately and conclude when the position is filled.**
  
  
The University: Located in the heart of Harris County and the Houston metroplex, the University of Houston-Downtown is a public university that serves the fourth largest city and one of the most diverse student bodies in the nation. UHD offers bachelor's degrees in 44 areas of study and nine master's degrees. Current enrollment is approximately 15,000 students, making UHD the second largest member institution in the University of Houston System. UHD is a federally designated Hispanic and Minority Serving University.
  
  
The College: The College of Public Service (CPS) has two departments: Criminal Justice & Social Work and Urban Education. The college offers four bachelor's degrees and three master's degrees. The college is within walking distance of major police agencies, correctional facilities, and county, state, and federal courts. Additionally, the CPS maintains relationships with key social service providing organizations that serve the Greater Houston area.
  
  
The Department: The Department of Criminal Justice and Social Work offers degree plans leading to the Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice, the Bachelor of Applied Arts and Sciences in Criminal Justice, the Master of Science in Criminal Justice, the Bachelor of Social Work, and Master of Social Work degrees. The department recently added an innovative graduate-level Applied Corrections Certificate that draws on the combined strengths of the criminal justice and the social work faculty of the department.
  
  
The Program: The University of Houston-Downtown’s Social Work Program is accredited by the Council on Social Work Education (CSWE) and awards a Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) and Master of Social Work (MSW) degree.
  
  
To apply for this position, fill out the online application and submit a Curriculum Vitae, cover letter, teaching philosophy statement, research/scholarly agenda statement, unofficial graduate transcripts, and contact information for three professional references.

The search committee will begin screening applications as early as October 2026, although the system will remain open for applications until the position is filled. Ideally, we will complete the selection process by early Spring 2027.

All positions at the University of Houston-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check.

The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

jobs.description:
**Job Details**
The Assistant Professor and Director, Pre-Licensure Clinical Placements is a faculty leadership role that combines the academic responsibilities of an Assistant Professor with strategic and operational leadership for undergraduate clinical education and placement. The position assumes a leadership role in the planning, implementation, and evaluation of curriculum and student learning experiences in classroom, laboratory/simulation, and clinical settings while providing oversight of clinical placement processes, clinical partnerships, adjunct clinical instructors, and related systems. The Director serves as a primary liaison among JCN faculty, staff, students, clinical partners, and the broader Jefferson enterprise and supports an environment conducive to learning, strong academic-practice partnerships, and positive student/faculty relationships.
  
  
**Responsibilities Include**
Faculty Teaching, Scholarship and Service
  
  

* Provide theory and/or clinical instruction and utilize contemporary and

innovative teaching methodologies in classroom, laboratory/simulation, and
  
  
clinical settings.
  
  

* Serve as an academic advisor to assigned students, as applicable.
* Develop and implement a scholarly agenda and contribute to the nursing

profession through scholarly papers, presentations, publications,
  
  
grantsmanship, or other appropriate scholarly activity.
  
  

* Serve on College and/or University committees and demonstrate an emerging

leadership role.
  
  

* Represent the College in appropriate University activities and participate

actively in professional organizations at the local, state, or national level.
  
  

* Participate in College and University recruitment activities and activities that

support the quality of nursing care and the nursing profession.
  
  
Clinical Placement Leadership and Operations
  
  

* Communicate effectively and bi-directionally as a primary point of contact

between clinical site personnel and JCN faculty, staff, and students.
  
  

* Lead and coordinate undergraduate clinical placement processes, including

site relations, placement needs, site-specific requirements, and student and
  
  
adjunct clinical instructor compliance.
  
  

* Collaborate with Chairs and program leadership to determine the number and

type of clinical placements needed each semester by program and level.
  
  

* Deploy and support clinical placement request processes to route student

requests to appropriate faculty for review, vetting, and approval.
  
  

* Oversee undergraduate aspects of the clinical management system and

collaborate on implementation, maintenance, and evaluation of clinical
  
  
placement technology and software.
  
  
Clinical Partnerships and Academic-Practice Integration
  
  

* Identify, vet, cultivate, and maintain affiliated clinical education sites to expand

high-quality clinical learning opportunities that reflect sound patient/client
  
  
management, ethical and professional conduct, and contemporary nursing
  
  
practice.
  
  

* Actively cultivate relationships throughout the Jefferson enterprise to develop

and sustain a strategic pool of internal clinical placement opportunities.
  
  

* Build and strengthen community partnerships to meet clinical education needs

as part of the Academic Practice Integration team.
  
  

* Serve as a JCN representative to Jefferson regional nurse residency advisory

boards and other appropriate academic-practice forums.
  
  

* Collaborate with the clinical contracts coordinator to ensure affiliation

agreements remain current and new agreements are processed efficiently.
  
  

* Contribute to Academic Practice Integration strategic planning and

development of policies and procedures for clinical placement, management,
  
  
communication, and evaluation.
  
  
Clinical Quality and Adjunct Faculty Leadership
  
  

* Maintain clinical site rounding, preceptor, adjunct instructor, and clinical site

evaluation information to support strategic planning and quality improvement.
  
  

* Review clinical site evaluations and collaborate with Program Directors and

site contacts when sites do not meet established evaluation benchmarks.
  
  

* Lead the hiring, onboarding, evaluation/remediation, and professional

development of adjunct clinical instructors.
  
  

* Collaborate with appropriate JCN partners to maintain and update handbooks,

guidance, and resources for adjunct clinical instructors
  
  
Administrative and Professional Responsibilities
  
  

* Prepare internal and external correspondence, reports, and other materials

related to clinical education and academic-practice initiatives.
  
  

* Establish and maintain effective working relationships with faculty, staff,

students, clinical faculty, clinical preceptors, alumni, visitors, and internal and
  
  
external partners.
  
  

* Exercise judgment requiring broad interpretation of policies, procedures, and

instructions within the scope of assigned responsibilities.
  
  

* Interact with co-workers, visitors, students, faculty, and partners consistent

with the core values of the University.
  
  

* Perform related duties as assigned

Supervisory / Leadership Responsibilities
  
  
Provides leadership and direction to adjunct clinical instructors and others supporting clinical placement activities, including instructing, assigning and reviewing work, and participating in hiring, onboarding, evaluation, remediation, and professional development activities as appropriate.
  
  
**Qualifications**
**Job Description**
Earned doctorate in nursing or an appropriate discipline from an accredited institution.
  
  
Current license to practice as a registered nurse in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
  
  
State Board of Nursing licensure for states where clinical assignments are performed, as applicable.
  
  
Professional specialty certification as applicable to teaching assignment.
  
  
Evidence of continuing education and professional memberships relevant to areas of expertise.

Participation in College and/or University committees and professional organizations at the local, state, or national level.
  
  
Experience in clinical education, clinical placement coordination, academic-practice partnerships, or related nursing education operations strongly preferred.
  
  
Experience supporting, supervising, onboarding, developing, or evaluating adjunct clinical faculty preferred.
  
  
Computer literacy, including Microsoft Office. Experience with clinical placement, compliance, or clinical management systems preferred.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Al & Computational Photonics - PhD Program in Physics
jobs.description:
Assistant Professor - Al & Computational Photonics - PhD Program in Physics

**FACULTY VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT**

Performs teaching, research and guidance duties in area(s) of expertise. Shares responsibility for committee and department assignments including administrative, supervisory, and other functions.

CAMPUS SPECIFIC INFORMATION

The Graduate Center (GC) of the City University of New York (CUNY) is seeking a tenure-track Assistant Professor to join the Ph.D. Program in Physics in Fall 2027. This position is part of the CUNY Martin S. Spergel Initiative in the Computational Sciences supported by the Simons Foundation. The successful candidate will join the CUNY Photonics Initiative, a multi-campus research effort building on research excellence in optics and photonics, and leverage the computational resources of Empire AI in their research.

The Graduate Center, a Carnegie R1 Institution, is the focal point for advanced teaching and research at the nation's largest urban public university system. With over 35 doctoral and master's programs of the highest caliber, the CUNY GC fosters pioneering research and scholarship in the arts and sciences and prepares students for careers in universities and the private, nonprofit, and government sectors. The GC's commitment to research and scholarship for the public good is exemplified by its more than 30 centers, institutes, and initiatives, including its Advanced Science Research Center (CUNY ASRC), a 200,000 square-foot facility in upper Manhattan, designed to promote collaboration among scientists in five areas of global research and innovation: nanoscience (including a nanofabrication facility), photonics, structural biology, neuroscience, and environmental sciences.

We seek an outstanding scientist with a record of significant research promise and accomplishments in theoretical and computational photonics, with expertise in areas such as (but not limited to) modeling light-matter interactions, metamaterials and/or complex photonic systems, light-based computing, first-principles/DFT calculations of the optical and electronic properties of materials, and/or condensed matter theory for photonics. This faculty position is poised to enhance CUNY's research portfolio and leadership in photonics by integrating advanced theoretical and computational research activities within its experimentally focused research in photonics.

Building on the success of the GC’s Photonics Subprogram, and leveraging partnerships with the CUNY ASRC, and the world-class computational resources of Empire Al consortium, this effort will accelerate breakthroughs in quantum photonics, nanophotonics, metamaterials, and other fields broadly related to photonics and electromagnetics.

The successful candidate will engage in research, teaching and mentorship of students and group members; develop new educational and research initiatives at CUNY; and initiate new AI-relevant collaborative projects and activities across CUNY and other research institutions. The successful candidate will also be expected to develop an externally funded research program and pursue competitive federal and other extra- and intra-mural funding opportunities.

This position will begin in Fall 2027. The incumbent will report to the Executive Officer of the Ph.D. Program in Physics at GC CUNY and will require the incumbent to work in person.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

Ph.D. degree in area(s) of experience or equivalent. Also required are the ability to teach successfully, demonstrated scholarship or achievement, and ability to cooperate with others for the good of the institution.

A preferred candidate will have a Ph.D. degree in a photonics-related area, postdoctoral work or equivalent, a record of several years of productive research experience, and a willingness to perform research independently and collaborate on research projects. The incumbent will have demonstrated achievements in extra-mural funding, high-impact published scholarship, and conducting productive research using modeling or computational approaches. We encourage applications from candidates with a collaborative spirit, an innovative research plan that complements current GC CUNY and CUNY-wide Photonics efforts, and ability to base their research at GC CUNY (which does not have wet-lab facilities).

**COMPENSATION**

$102,460-$114,091 (9 month contract payable over 12 months). Salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development.

**HOW TO APPLY**

Please click on "Apply Now" which will bring you to the registration screen. If you are a new user, you must register to apply. If you already have a user ID, please use your existing ID to apply.

Applicants should upload, in a single file .pdf format:

* Academic Curriculum Vitae
* Cover Letter (2 page maximum)
* Research Statement (3 pages maximum)
* Teaching, Mentoring, and Service Statement (2 pages maximum)
* Contact information for three professional references (name, title, email, and organization)

**CLOSING DATE**

Open until filled with review of applications to begin on November 2, 2026

CUNY encourages people with disabilities, minorities, veterans and women to apply. At CUNY, Italian Americans are also included among our protected groups. The Department of Mechanical Engineering at Virginia Tech seeks applications for multiple tenure track faculty positions at the Assistant or Associate Professor level, depending on experience and qualifications, in the broad area of advanced manufacturing with an anticipated start date of August 2027.
  
  
We seek candidates who will establish an internationally recognized research program in advanced manufacturing. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, advanced materials and materials processing; additive, hybrid, and emerging manufacturing processes; manufacturing robotics and automation, including autonomous self-driving laboratories; data-driven, intelligent, and autonomous manufacturing; computational design and digital manufacturing; human–machine interaction; point-of-care and distributed biomanufacturing; and future-generation manufacturing systems. Candidates whose research bridges multiple areas, integrates advances across materials, processes, design, and systems, or establishes new directions in advanced manufacturing are particularly encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will benefit from and contribute to VT MADE (Virginia Tech Center for Advanced Manufacturing), which brings together interdisciplinary expertise and research capabilities in materials, manufacturing technologies, computational and data-driven design, robotics and autonomy, digital integration, and manufacturing systems, while fostering partnerships across Virginia Tech and with external organizations to advance manufacturing research, education, and innovation.
  
  
The successful candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate courses, including core mechanical engineering courses and specialized courses in their area of expertise. The development of new courses that address emerging directions in advanced manufacturing is encouraged. The successful candidate will also mentor undergraduate and graduate students and contribute to the continued growth of advanced manufacturing research and education within the department and VT MADE.

**Required Qualifications**

Applicants must hold a PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related discipline by the start of their appointment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

A history showing a strong record of academic accomplishments, a proven ability to work collaboratively, a commitment to interdisciplinary research and instruction, and a willingness to expand disciplinary boundaries to address complex technical and societal challenges.

**Overtime Status**

Exempt: Not eligible for overtime

**Appointment Type**

Regular

40

November 6, 2026

**Additional Information**

The successful candidate will be required to have a criminal conviction check.

**About Virginia Tech**

Dedicated to its motto, *Ut Prosim* (That I May Serve), Virginia Tech pushes the boundaries of knowledge by taking a hands-on, transdisciplinary approach to preparing scholars to be leaders and problem-solvers. A comprehensive land-grant institution that enhances the quality of life in Virginia and throughout the world, Virginia Tech is an inclusive community dedicated to knowledge, discovery, and creativity. The university offers more than 280 majors to a diverse enrollment of more than 36,000 undergraduate, graduate, and professional students in eight undergraduate colleges, a school of medicine, a veterinary medicine college, Graduate School, and Honors College. The university has a significant presence across Virginia, including Blacksburg, the greater Washington, D.C. area, the Health Sciences and Technology Campus in Roanoke, sites in Newport News and Richmond, and numerous Extension offices and research institutes. A leading global research institution, Virginia Tech conducts more than $650 million in research annually.

Virginia Tech endorses and encourages participation in professional development opportunities and university shared governance. These valuable contributions to university shared governance provide important representation and perspective, along with opportunities for unique and impactful professional development.

**FACULTY VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT**

The College of Staten Island, CUNY, seeks a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor, specializing in music technology. This position will develop and deliver a curriculum that integrates traditional and contemporary music technology methods, materials, and conceptual approaches.

The ideal candidate will teach electronic music composition, audio production, and sound design courses; have advanced knowledge of industry-standard software and languages, such as Pro Tools, Logic Pro, Ableton Live, Max/MSP, etc.; and have knowledge of traditional sound design principles, theory, and history. The ideal candidate will play a key role in shaping a progressive curriculum that spans technical mastery, creative artistry, and cultural context, encouraging interdisciplinary collaboration and fostering connections with related disciplines such as sound design, film scoring, interactive media, and live event production.

The ability to teach in a secondary area – such as music theory, musicianship, musicology, or applied music – would be welcome.

The College of Staten Island is a four-year public institution within the City University of New York system. Ranked #33 in Top Performers in Social Mobility by *U.S. News and World Report* , the College serves approximately 11,000 students, including undergraduates, graduates, and Ph.D.s, on a 200-acre campus. The Performing and Creative Arts Department, housed within the Division of Humanities and Social Sciences, includes Art History, Dance, Drama, Music, Photography, and Studio Art, serving approximately 200 majors, as well as delivering courses for General Education requirements. The department produces numerous performances and events for the campus and community each year, including a Festival of Electronic Music. Facilities consist of one large electronic-music studio with hardware and software for composition and sound design, and a recording studio. It is hoped that the successful candidate would work to secure funding for these facilities and oversee the renovation of the recording studio.

Qualifications for the position are: an earned doctorate (Ph.D. or D.M.A.) in music composition, music technology, or a related field (candidates at the ABD level with exceptional credentials may be considered, provided the degree is conferred before appointment)

Preferred qualifications include:

Substantial record of ongoing research and/or creative practice, including premieres, grants, residences, and/or similar activities within the field, at the national and/or international level; a minimum of three years teaching experience at the college level as the teacher of record, preferably in electronic music or music technology topics; expertise in contemporary approaches, concepts, and critical issues as they pertain to electronic music composition and sound design, as well as fluency in the history of the discipline; knowledge of principles and methods for curriculum design, teaching, and instruction for students; and advanced communication (verbal, written and interpersonal) and organizational skills.

The Philosophy & Religion program in the School of Humanities at the University of Southern Mississippi invites qualified applicants for a full-time, 9-month, non-tenure track, Assistant Teaching Professor in Philosophy to begin Fall 2027. The program has a new inter-disciplinary BA in Philosophy, Religion, and Law that offers three pathways of concentration: Ethics, Philosophy of Law, and Religion and World Cultures. We are seeking a candidate whose area of specialization is open, but we are looking for someone to fulfill our needs in applied ethics, particularly Environmental Ethics and Healthcare Ethics. PhD in Philosophy by the time of appointment  
  
**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

The Aeronautical Science Department in the College of Aviation (COA) at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University—Daytona Beach invites applications for a Tenure-Track 9-month appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor. The qualified candidate will teach courses held in the Department of Aeronautical Science for both the Aeronautical Science and Aeronautics undergraduate degree programs. jobs.description:
* Tuscaloosa, Alabama, United States

* Arts and Sciences

* Tenure/Tenure-Track Faculty

* Closing at: Aug 1 2027 - 22:55 CDT

**Department/Organization**  
204271 - Theatre and Dance

**Rank**  
Assistant Professor

**Position Summary**  
The Department of Theatre and Dance invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Dance.

**Detailed Position Information**  
The Department of Theatre and Dance invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Dance. The successful candidate will engage with students across the MFA and BA dance programs through teaching, mentoring, research and creative activity, and service. The faculty member will teach a combination of dance studies and studio courses, which may include dance pedagogy, graduate research methods, graduate dance seminars, and improvisation and composition, in addition to all levels of technique in the candidate’s area of expertise. While we are particularly seeking candidates with experience teaching all levels of jazz and/or ballet techniques, additional expertise in dance forms such as Hip Hop, House, Street Style, or Latin forms, and in dance technology and digital media, will be considered an asset. The position also offers opportunities to contribute to the reimagining of curricular initiatives and the development of new courses. The faculty member will mentor graduate and undergraduate students in teaching, choreography, and research.
  
Research and creative activity are integral components of the position. The faculty member is expected to develop and maintain a compelling creative research agenda with demonstrated potential to impact the field. This is an exciting time for creative work within the department, and in Fall 2027, we will open the Smith Family Center for the Performing Arts, a new performing arts center featuring four venues including the dedicated 450-seat Eliza P. Culverhouse Dance Theatre. Creative research opportunities on campus include choreographing for the pre-professional company Alabama Repertory Dance Theatre, contributing other departmental productions, and collaborative, interdisciplinary arts research opportunities through CARI, the Collaborative Arts Research Initiative, among others.  
Additional responsibilities include student recruitment, mentorship of student dance concerts, and service to the department, college, and university. The faculty member will also advise and mentor students at both the graduate and undergraduate levels, contributing to their artistic, academic, and professional development throughout their time in the program.

**Minimum Qualifications**  
Master of Fine Arts or PhD in Dance or related field. Record of successful teaching at the college and/or university level. Candidates should demonstrate a clear commitment to inclusive pedagogical approaches and a record of work using various and collaborative perspectives. Good communication and organizational skills are imperative.

**Preferred Qualifications**  
3-5 years of university teaching experience and evidence of potential to impact the field through creative activity and research.

**Instructions and Required Materials for Application**  
This position begins on August 16, 2027. To apply, go to careers.ua.edu/jobs/search/AS. Review will begin November 15 and remain open until filled. Submit a letter of application, specifically addressing how your qualifications, training, and experience meet the stated needs of the position, a detailed dance curriculum vitae, and the names and contact information for three current references. Please submit PDF including links of teaching samples and creative works/research as Additional Documents. Questions may be directed to Associate Professor Lyndell T. McDonald, ltmcdonald@ua.edu.

**About the Division/College/School**  
The J. Frank Barefield Jr. College of Arts and Sciences at The University of Alabama offers an exciting and dynamic environment for faculty seeking to make an impact in their field and in the lives of the innovators and changemakers of tomorrow.  
  
As the largest college at The University, we house over 9,000 students and 1,000 faculty and staff across our 22 departments.  
  
With nationally recognized programs and award-winning faculty, our College has positioned itself as a leader in higher education. Our facilities and resources include state-of-the-art laboratories, research centers, and performance venues, providing students with hands-on learning experiences and opportunities for research and creative expression.  
  
The College is committed to the liberal arts philosophy that fosters creative and critical thinking and a lifetime of learning.”

**About the University**  
The University of Alabama is located in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, named one of Travel + Leisure’s 25 Best College Towns and Cities in the U.S. As one of the nation’s premier universities, UA offers bachelor’s, master's and doctoral degrees in nearly 200 fields of study. With more than 1,400 acres of tree-lined academic core campus and over 300 state-of-the art facilities, UA has been ranked among the most beautiful and most impressive college campuses in the South, in the state of Alabama and in the nation.
  
  
In Fall 2023, the Capstone set a new enrollment record with more than 39,000 students, including more than 8,200 in the freshman class. The current enrollment includes students from every county in Alabama, every state in the nation and 92 countries around the world. More than 1,100 National Merit Scholars are currently enrolled, making UA one of the largest enrolling institutions of the scholars in the country.  
  
UA was recently recognized as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. students for the seventh time in nine years, as well as a Top Producing Institution of Fulbright U.S. Scholars for the first time. UA is one of only 12 universities in the nation to receive both honors.
  
  
For reasons like this, the University made Forbes list of America’s Top Colleges for 2023 and Time magazine’s list of Top 50 Best Colleges for Future Leaders. It also made Princeton Review’s list of Top Value Colleges.  
  
UA is also designated among the top doctoral research universities in the United States in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. One of the fastest growing major research institutions in the nation, UA saw a 21% increase in sponsored awards in the 2023 fiscal year.
  
  
Since 2015, UA has invested over $1.1 billion in the physical campus, adding more than 2.55 million gross square feet of space, over 150 new research-intensive faculty, signature research areas (e.g., “The Alabama Research Institutes”), and a growing number of partnerships with industry and with state and federal agencies.
  
  
The University employs nearly 2,100 faculty and over 4,500 staff, with 52 UA researchers included in the National Academy of Inventors. An additional 40 current faculty have received the NSF CAREER Award, the nation’s most prestigious recognition of top performing young scientists in disciplines ranging from nanoscience and engineering to biological sciences.

Background Investigation Statement: Prior to hiring, the final candidate(s) must successfully pass a pre-employment background investigation and information obtained from social media and other internet sources. A prior conviction reported as a result of the background investigation DOES NOT automatically disqualify a candidate from consideration for this position. A candidate with a prior conviction or negative behavioral red flags will receive an individualized review of the prior conviction or negative behavioral red flags before a hiring decision is made.  
  
Equal Employment Opportunity: The University of Alabama is an Equal Employment/Equal Educational Opportunity Institution. Mission
  
We are a community committed to preparing students to be educated and enlightened citizens who lead productive and meaningful lives.
  
  
Vision
  
To be the national model for the engaged university: engaged with ideas and the world.
  
  
Who We Are
  
Situated in the heart of Virginia’s beautiful Shenandoah Valley, the city of Harrisonburg is a vibrant community with a population of approximately 52,000. Harrisonburg is conveniently located approximately 120 miles from Washington, D.C. and Richmond, VA.
  
  
JMU is a selective, public institution with a growing national reputation for offering experiences that lead to an outstanding education and supportive environment for students, faculty and staff. The student body includes approximately 21,000 undergraduate and 1,800 graduate students, with over 1,000 full-time instructional faculty.
  
  
JMU offers thriving programs in the liberal arts, science and technology, and professional disciplines at the undergraduate, master’s and doctoral levels. JMU has achieved national recognition for the high quality of its academic programs, focus on maintaining strong student/faculty interaction, and innovative faculty research.

**General Information:**

The Department of Physics and Astronomy at James Madison University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Physics with expertise in data-intensive, computational, and/or AI-enabled approaches to physics, astronomy, or closely related fields. This is a full-time appointment beginning August 10, 2027.
  
  
The Department of Physics & Astronomy at James Madison University combines a strong commitment to undergraduate education with an active culture of scholarship and discovery. Through excellent teaching, close mentorship, and faculty-led research programs that engage undergraduate students, the department provides a rich educational experience for its majors. The department consists of 21 full-time faculty members, most of whom maintain active research agendas, and approximately 70 students enrolled in our multi-track baccalaureate-only programs.
  
  
Please visit our website at http://www.jmu.edu/physics for more information about the department.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

The successful candidate will contribute to the department's mission through outstanding teaching, active scholarship, and meaningful service. Teaching responsibilities include undergraduate physics and/or astronomy courses and laboratories at both introductory and advanced levels. The candidate will establish and maintain an active, externally visible research program that engages undergraduate students and enhances the scholarly reputation of the department, college, and university. The successful candidate will also contribute to the continuing development of an innovative curriculum, including courses related to data science, computation, artificial intelligence, and other emerging areas relevant to the discipline and university priorities. Faculty participate in departmental, college, and university service activities that support the academic community, including committee work, student mentoring, and professional service.

**Qualifications:**

Applicants must have a Ph.D. in Physics, Astronomy, or a closely related field by the time of appointment. Relevant Postdoctoral (or equivalent) experience is preferred.
  
  
Candidates will be evaluated based on their potential for excellence in undergraduate teaching and their ability to establish a productive research program that actively involves undergraduate students. Preference will be given to candidates whose teaching and research interests include data-intensive, computational, and/or AI-enabled approaches to physics, astronomy, or closely related fields. Areas of interest may include, but are not limited to, computational astrophysics, data-driven astronomy, biophysics, materials physics, computational physics, or other emerging interdisciplinary areas.
  
  
The department is particularly interested in candidates who have the potential to secure external funding and develop a sustained research program, as well as those interested in developing courses that integrate computing, data science, artificial intelligence, or other workforce-relevant skills. Interest in contributing to the university's General Education program, particularly the Science, Technology, and the Built Environment and/or Connections areas, and a commitment to mentoring undergraduate researchers are desirable.

* A cover letter addressing relevant qualifications
* Current curriculum vitae (CV)

* Effectively teach undergraduate students
* Promote a welcoming and supportive climate for students in teaching and research
* A statement of research (uploaded as "Other Document #1) plans involving students at JMU with:
* A 5-year plan that involves undergraduate students at JMU
* Plans to promote the growth and excellence of student researchers
* The names and contact information for three professional references

Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a criminal background check.

James Madison University is committed to creating and supporting a diverse and inclusive work and educational community that is free of all forms of discrimination. This institution does not tolerate discrimination or harassment on the basis of age, color, disability, gender identity or expression, genetic information, national origin, parental status, political affiliation, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation or veteran status.

Anyone having questions concerning discrimination should contact the Office for Equal Opportunity: (540) 568-6991.

If you are an individual with a disability and need assistance searching or applying for jobs please contact us at (540) 568-3597 or jobs@jmu.edu. You may also visit the JMU Human Resource Office, located at 752 Ott Street, Harrisonburg, VA 22807 and we will be happy to assist you.

We are New Mexico’s land-grant institution and a comprehensive research university dedicated to teaching, research public service and outreach at all levels. Established in 1958 to serve the needs of the airmen and families stationed at Holloman Air Force Base located only 10 miles west of Alamogordo, NMSUA is a community college with a long history of excellence that is supported by a caring community of hard-working students and dedicated faculty and staff. NMSU Grants was established as a branch of New Mexico State University in 1968 through the cooperative efforts of New Mexico State University and Grants Municipal Schools. jobs.title: Assistant Professor – Tenure Track
jobs.description:
**M****aster of Social Work Assistant Professor**

St. Ambrose University in Davenport, Iowa, invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty position in Social Work at the rank of Assistant Professor to start as soon as January 1st, 2027, and no later than July 1st, 2027.This individual hired for this position will have primary teaching responsibilities in the Master of Social Work Program. The faculty member holding this position will:

* Teach research methods courses, as well as other courses across the social work curriculum
* Teach in a variety of course delivery systems, i.e., in-person, online synchronous and asynchronous, and hybrid.
* Serve as a Practicum Liaison for social work students
* Be an active advisor to students
* Participate and provide leadership on university committees
* Engage in scholarly activity

One of eight disciplines within the College of Health and Human Services, the MSW program offers a supportive, collaborative environment with a strong focus on teaching, as well as support for scholarship. Multiple interprofessional learning events and numerous outreach services enhance the student experience. Additionally, the program and college value self-directed community involvement, inter-professional collaboration, and active professional development for faculty and staff. This MSW Program has a single concentration in Empowerment Social Work Practice. Program options include an in-person full-time MSW program, part-time online MSW program, and in-person and online Advanced Standing MSW programs.

The position requires an MSW from a CSWE-accredited program and a doctorate in social work or related field. Applications from ABDs will be considered. A minimum of two years of post-MSW experience is required, and evidence of effective teaching is essential. Salary will be commensurate with experience.People from under-represented populations are encouraged to apply.Priority will be given to applicants showing a strong history of teaching and practice experience with vulnerable populations.

St. Ambrose University and its affiliate campuses are an inclusive, Catholic, and diocesan community of learners empowering all their members to act courageously, to seek wisdom through faith and reason, to work for justice and mercy, and to lead lives of service. St. Ambrose is an equal opportunity employer. You can learn more about St. Ambrose at www.sau.edu.

Interested individuals should apply online at https://Stambroseuniv.applicantlist.com by submitting a cover letter addressing their knowledge and experience, a vitae, a statement of their teaching philosophy, and contact information for three professional references. Applications received by October 15, 2026, will be ensured of consideration and applications will continue to be reviewed until the position is filled. EOE. #HEJ

jobs.description:
* Tuscaloosa, Alabama, United States

* Arts and Sciences

* Tenure/Tenure-Track Faculty

* Closing at: Aug 1 2027 - 22:55 CDT

**Department/Organization**  
204211 - Art

**Rank**  
Assistant Professor

**Position Summary**  
The Department of Art and Art History at The University of Alabama invites applications for a full-time, nine-month, tenure-track, Assistant Professor position in Graphic Design beginning fall semester 2027.

**Detailed Position Information**  
The Department of Art and Art History at The University of Alabama invites applications for a full-time, nine-month, tenure-track, Assistant Professor position in Graphic Design beginning fall semester 2027. The ideal candidate will demonstrate commitment to creative activity, teaching excellence, scholarship, and university and community service.  
  
The successful candidate will teach courses at the undergraduate level and will serve on the graduate faculty. This position includes teaching and research responsibilities. The candidate's primary creative engagement should be within the graphic design field. While a broad range of skills is required, one or more of the following focus areas are sought, but not limited to: interactive design, motion design, print media, branding/identity, packaging design, graphic design history, and commercial/industry practices. The applicant should be well-versed in the theory of graphic design pertaining to contemporary practice, as both a fine art and applied discipline. The individual will work with other faculty members in the area on curriculum development, facilities management, coordination of instructors, and scheduling. Other responsibilities include: participation in departmental duties such as student advising and mentorship; program assessment and management; service to departmental, college, and university committees; and participation in community outreach and program recruitment.  
  
Importantly, the candidate should demonstrate an ability to conduct a sustained program of creative research and production. An established record of creative activities, awards, and/or industry recognition that demonstrates a high level of professional engagement with contemporary practice is essential.  
  
The Department of Art and Art History offers the BA and MA degrees in Art History and the BA, BFA, MA, and MFA degrees in Studio Art, and the BFA in Graphic Design. Important resources include the Sarah Moody Gallery of Art, the Sella-Granata Art Gallery, the Paul R. Jones  
Collection of American Art, and the UA Gallery at the Dinah Washington Cultural Arts Center. The University of Alabama, the state's flagship public research university, is located in Tuscaloosa, about 50 miles southwest of Birmingham. UA's enrollment is diverse, drawing from the state of Alabama, the Southeast region, and the nation, and increasingly from around the world. The total enrollment exceeds 39,000 students and continued growth is projected for the coming years. 60% of students come from outside the state of Alabama.  
  
Tuscaloosa supports a vibrant arts community with many venues that host exhibits and events. These include the Barna Theatre, the Dinah Washington Cultural Arts Center, the Tuscaloosa Amphitheatre, as well as many galleries both on campus and off. Across the Black Warrior River, Northport is home to the Kentuck Arts and Crafts Center. Each year, the Kentuck Arts Festival brings together over 270 nationally and internationally acclaimed folk artists. Throughout the year there are many festivals and events in the city which make Tuscaloosa a culturally vibrant location to live. Additionally, Tuscaloosa is in the middle of a busy interstate corridor, close to Birmingham, Nashville, New Orleans, and Atlanta.

**Minimum Qualifications**  

* Master of Fine Arts degree in graphic design or related field.
* Evidence of active professional engagement, exhibition record, and/or scholarship.
* Demonstrated excellence and recognition of dynamic ongoing creative research that can build towards tenure.
* Evidence of commitment to university level teaching.

**Preferred Qualifications**

  

**Instructions and Required Materials for Application**  
Candidates for this position must visit The University of Alabama website at: https://careers.ua.edu/jobs/search/AS to initiate an application with Human Resources and to upload materials saved as pdf's directly into the appropriate section: 1. Cover letter addressing qualifications 2. Curriculum vitae/resume 3. Teaching philosophy that addresses both your personal teaching approaches to graphic design, as well as what you feel is important for a contemporary graphic design program 4. Contact information for three professional references {letters of reference will only be requested from finalists) 5. 20 examples of professional work, please include size, date, and medium 6. 20 examples of student work 7. Links to pertinent websites are also welcome in lieu of, or in addition to a pdf document 8. Web-links to examples of time-based media can also be included PDFs should not exceed 15 MB Only fully completed applications will be reviewed. Review of applications will begin January 8, 2027, and continue until the position is filled.

Our facilities and resources include state-of-the-art laboratories, research centers, and performance venues, providing students with hands-on learning experiences and opportunities for research and creative expression.  
  
The College is committed to the liberal arts philosophy that fosters creative and critical thinking and a lifetime of learning.”

The University of Alabama is located in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, named one of Travel + Leisure’s 25 Best College Towns and Cities in the U.S. As one of the nation’s premier universities, UA offers bachelor’s, master's and doctoral degrees in nearly 200 fields of study. * Maintain an active scholarly profile

jobs.description:
* JR10015554
* On Site

* Madison, Wisconsin

* Faculty

  

**Job Category:**
-----------------

Faculty

**Employment Type:**
--------------------

Regular

**Job Profile:**
----------------

Professor

**Job Summary:**
----------------

The College of Computing & Artificial Intelligence (CAI) is UW–Madison’s first new college in more than 40 years, bringing together three established and highly regarded departments: Computer Sciences, Statistics, and the Information School. Building on their longstanding strengths in research and education, CAI advances interdisciplinary discovery spanning computing, data, information, and artificial intelligence and prepares students to shape how technology is designed, developed, and used for the public good. Supported by more than $400 million in philanthropic and institutional investment, CAI is expanding its faculty by 50 positions and significantly growing its research enterprise. Faculty joining CAI have the opportunity to contribute to established academic communities while helping shape a new college at a pivotal moment in its development. CAI is based in Morgridge Hall, a new, state-of-the-art facility designed to foster collaboration, learning, and discovery.

The Department of Statistics within the College of Computing & Artificial Intelligence at the University of Wisconsin-Madison is experiencing rapid expansion as part of the university's substantial investment in data science and artificial intelligence.

The department is also home to the Data Science major, which stands as the university's fastest-growing undergraduate program. Currently, the department features:

* 37 regular faculty members

* Over 80 PhD students

* Over 100 MS students

Approximately 1,800 undergraduate majors across statistics and data science  



The Department of Statistics is widely recognized for its strong interplay between statistical theory, methodology, and practice. You can learn more about CAI at cai.wisc.edu/about and the Department of Statistics at stat.wisc.edu.

**Position Summary:**

We are seeking excellent candidates for multiple tenured or tenure-track faculty positions in Statistics.

The successful candidates will engage in the intellectual life of the Department through scholarly research, teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels, graduate student mentoring and supervision, and university and professional service. They will proactively contribute to, support, and advance the college’s commitment to excellence among all aspects of their teaching, mentoring, research, and service; which includes making significant contributions to the department’s teaching mission through course development and delivery to undergraduate and graduate students in one or more fields of specialization.

UW-Madison ranks among the top universities in the country for research expenditures and provides exceptional support for faculty seeking external funding. Internal research support is also available via funds provided by the Wisconsin Alumni Research Foundation (WARF). Our field and department are growing rapidly, fueling our excitement for the future of our discipline and driving an eager desire among our faculty to attract candidates from various backgrounds and interests.

**About Madison:**

Madison is the state's capital city and is highly regarded for offering a small-town feel within a medium-sized city. It is an exceptional place to raise a family, offering an ideal combination of natural beauty, stimulating cultural events, outstanding schools, and year-round outdoor recreation.

**Key Job Responsibilities:**
-----------------------------

The successful candidates will be expected to:

* Engage in high-impact research addressing significant scientific and societal problems.

* Conduct scholarly research and publish results in premier academic journals or refereed conference proceedings across statistics, data science, and closely related fields.

* Present research findings at prominent national and international meetings.

* Teach undergraduate and graduate-level statistics courses.

* Mentor and advise students.

* Participate actively in professional, university, and community outreach service.

**Department:**
---------------

UW-Madison, College of Computing & Artificial Intelligence, Department of Statistics

  
  

**Compensation:**
-----------------

Negotiable – 9 months / ongoing / renewable

  
  

**Required Qualifications:**
----------------------------

* **Research:** Demonstrated excellence, or demonstrated potential for excellence, in statistical research (very broadly defined).

* **Teaching:** Proven interest and ability to teach effectively at both undergraduate and graduate levels.

* **Collaboration:** Strong ability to interact with an interdisciplinary, collaborative intellectual community.
  

  

**Education:**
--------------

PhD in Statistics or a closely related field is required by the appointment start date.

**How to Apply:**
-----------------

Apply online at Jobs at UW (jobs.wisc.edu) under job requisition number JR10015554.

Applications must be submitted through UW-Madison's online application system; submissions outside of this system will not be considered.

Please upload the following required documents:

* **Letter of Application** (Cover Letter)

* **Detailed Resume/CV** and copies of university transcripts

* **Teaching and Mentoring Statement**

* **Research Statement**

* **Letters of Reference:** All applicants will receive an email requesting the names and contact information for three references; each reference will each receive an electronic link through which they can upload a signed letter of reference.
  

  

**Important Application Notes:**

* For full consideration, all materials must be received no later than 11:59 PM on November 16, 2026. Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.

* Applicants will be evaluated strictly based on submitted materials. Your application should clearly demonstrate your dedication to excellence in student-centered teaching and mentoring.

* Materials must showcase your ability to purposefully plan teaching practices (evidenced through goals, action plans, reflection, and related documentation). This section must be created directly by you; while supporting letters may be included, it cannot consist solely of letters and testimony written by others.

------------------------

For questions regarding the position or application process, please contact:

  

**Matthias Katzfuss**  
Department of Statistics
  
1205 University Ave, Madison, WI 53706
  
**Phone:** 608-263-8531
  
**Email:** mkatzfuss@wisc.edu
  
  
Relay Access (WTRS): 7-1-1. See RELAY\_SERVICE for further information.

The candidate's primary creative engagement should be within the graphic design field. While a broad range of skills is required, one or more of the following focus areas are sought, but not limited to: interactive design, motion design, print media, branding/identity, packaging design, graphic design history, and commercial/industry practices. The applicant should be well-versed in the theory of graphic design pertaining to contemporary practice, as both a fine art and applied discipline. The individual will work with other faculty members in the area on curriculum development, facilities management, coordination of instructors, and scheduling. Other responsibilities include: participation in departmental duties such as student advising and mentorship; program assessment and management; service to departmental, college, and university committees; and participation in community outreach and program recruitment.

Ball State University’s Department of Architecture seeks faculty candidates for a tenure track position at the rank of Assistant Professor available starting in August 2027. Our faculty are expected to be innovative, adaptive, engaging teachers across modalities; producers of impactful creative and/or scholarly work; leaders in meaningful service activities to multiple communities. We are committed to student and faculty success, impact, and access, within an environment that prioritizes inclusive excellence. We inspire each other to be critical thinkers and responsible citizens, so that we can pursue fulfilling careers and meaningful lives. Ball State University lives the values of Beneficence. We invite you to be part of our community.  
  
Ball State University is located in Muncie, Indiana, on an attractive campus 45 miles northeast of Indianapolis. Approximately 20,000 graduate and undergraduate students enroll in one of eight academic colleges that offer 270+ undergraduate and graduate programs. Many of our master’s, doctoral, certificate, and specialist degrees rank among the best in the nation. We engage students in educational, research, and creative endeavors that empower our graduates to have fulfilling careers and meaningful lives enriched by lifelong learning and service, while we enhance the economic, environmental, and social vitality of our community, our state, and our world.

(Applications will continue to be accepted after the full consideration date, until a sufficient applicant pool has been achieved or the position if filled. **What you'll do and what you will bring:**

**Position Function:**

Ball State University’s Department of Architecture seeks faculty candidates for a tenure track position at the rank of Assistant Professor available starting in August 2027. Major responsibilities lie mainly within the area of design studio instruction at both the undergraduate and graduate levels as well as lecture/seminar courses in the candidate's areas of focus. Candidates should also be able to demonstrate a record of current and advanced design methods with the ability to teach—and speak to—contemporary design processes and effective visual communication and representation strategies.

The Estopinal College of Architecture and Planning (CAP) at Ball State University has a rich history in community engaged, professionally grounded, innovative, and impactful design education. The Department of Architecture offers undergraduate and graduate architecture programs that emphasize the education of architecture students through design studio, engagement with social and environmental issues, immersive and experiential learning, digital fluency and design computation, high performance building design, building systems and assemblies, historic preservation, digital fabrication, and critical practice in the pursuit of preparing the next generation of leaders in architecture.

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

This position carries a standard 12-credit academic workload per semester, structured as a 9-credit teaching load (typically one studio plus a 3-credit course) and a 3-credit research allocation dedicated to active scholarship and publication.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

1. Master of Architecture degree by time of appointment OR;

2. Bachelor of Architecture degree with post-professional master’s degree in architecture or allied discipline from an accredited college or university by time of appointment.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

Professional licensure in architecture OR; a PhD in architecture. Evidence of excellence in teaching within an architectural curriculum; evidence of productive scholarship (research/creative work) with an active research, grant solicitation, and publication agenda; a track record of excellence in professional practice and service; design studio teaching; excellence and experience in teaching a primary AND secondary topical area.

At Ball State University, we understand the importance of balancing professional responsibilities with personal well-being. That's why we offer 12 paid sick days and 10 holidays a year. Plus, our paid parental leave (6 weeks) is there for life's most significant moments. We offer affordable health and dental insurance, robust long-term disability and life insurance plans, as well a range of retirement benefits to provide financial security to you and your family. These benefits ensure that you can focus on your work and personal growth without worrying about the unexpected.

When you work for us, you are family. And to show our support of your family, we will cover 90 percent of your child's (or children's) undergraduate college tuition at Ball State. This offer is good from the very first day you start. It's just one way we do our part to uplift you.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor - Black Studies
jobs.description:
Assistant Professor - Black Studies

**FACULTY VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT**

The Black Studies Unit of the Humanities Department at Hostos Community College of the City University of New York seeks applicants for the position of Assistant Professor of Black Studies. Applicants are expected to have a strong record of Afrocentric thought and practice. The successful candidate will perform the following tasks:

* Teach various levels of Black Studies and interdisciplinary Humanities courses.
* Develop new courses and plan extracurricular activities.
* Engage in research and scholarly activities leading to professional growth.
* Mentor and cultivate students to prepare them for senior college, professional degrees, and their intellectual journey in general.
* Participate in the evaluation of institutional goals in the context of Middle States accreditation, and assist in assessing the progress of curricular goals, at the Department, Unit and individual course levels.
* Participate in departmental and college assignments.
* Perform other tasks normally associated with the responsibilities of a full-time faculty appointment.

This is a tenure-track position and is on-campus/ in-person.

The mission of the Black Studies Unit at Hostos Community College is comprised of five interlocking objectives. First, to teach the Black experience, spanning the African continent and the African diaspora, particularly in the Americas; second, to create an edifice of knowledge that generates mental, spiritual, and political emancipation from oppression; third, to cultivate conscious scholars dedicated to community service, activism, and the application of emancipatory knowledge to liberate the Black community; fourth, to expand campus and community relationships; and fifth, to sustain the position of Black Studies in the academy as a serious discipline essential to a quality education.

As a discipline, Black Studies insists on African centeredness, African agency and an African frame of reference in research methodology, pedagogy, and intellectual production.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

Ph.D. degree in Black Studies or equivalent. Also required are the ability to teach successfully, demonstrated scholarship or achievement, and ability to cooperate with others for the good of the institution.

Candidates will be evaluated on their demonstrated record of Afrocentric thought and practice, regardless of disciplinary background.

The successful applicant will be a scholar with demonstrated original research, pedagogical innovation, and professional community impact through specific contributions, as well as an ability to cooperate with others for the good of the institution.

The following qualifications are preferred:

* Experience teaching in Black Studies or a related area.

* Ability to teach and develop curriculum, as well as co-curricular activities.

* Demonstrated success teaching and mentoring students in an urban public higher-education setting, particularly multilingual, first-generation, and culturally diverse student populations.

* Familiarity with CUNY students and the educational mission of an urban public university is particularly valued.

* Strong interest in interdisciplinary collaboration with related scholarly areas such as, but not limited to, Latin American and Caribbean Studies, Film Studies, History, Art History, and / or Digital Humanities.

* Availability to teach evening and weekend courses.

**COMPENSATION**

$79,630 - $85,556; salary commensurate with education and experience.

CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development.

**HOW TO APPLY**

To apply, go to www.cuny.edu, access the employment page, log in or create a new user account, and search for this vacancy using the Job ID 32854 or Title. Select "Apply Now" and provide the requested information.

Please submit cover letter and statement of scholarly interest.

**CLOSING DATE**

Open until filled with review of applications to begin October 28, 2026

**JOB SEARCH CATEGORY**

CUNY Job Posting: Faculty

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY**

CUNY encourages people with disabilities, minorities, veterans and women to apply. At CUNY, Italian Americans are also included among our protected groups. Applicants and employees will not be discriminated against on the basis of any legally protected category, including sexual orientation or gender identity. EEO/AA/Vet/Disability Employer.

**Location:** Hostos Community College

**Job Type:** Full-Time

URI is Rhode Island's flagship public research university. In 2025, URI achieved Carnegie R1 status, placing it among the nation's highest research activity universities. URI was also ranked the No. 1 public university in New England by The Wall Street Journal/College Pulse. The Kingston campus is located near Narragansett Bay and the Atlantic coast, with access to Providence, Boston, New York, and the coastal communities of southern Rhode Island. Rhode Island is also an EPSCoR-eligible jurisdiction, providing faculty with access to targeted federal funding opportunities that support research capacity, collaboration, and innovation.

The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at the University of Rhode Island invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the assistant professor level in environmental engineering. The anticipated start date is August 2027.  
  
We seek an outstanding scholar and educator with the potential to build a nationally prominent, externally funded research program. This is a broad search, and candidates from all areas of environmental engineering are encouraged to apply.  
  
The department is interested in reviewing applications from candidates whose work touches on air pollution, indoor air quality, links between climate and air quality, atmospheric chemistry, and ocean-atmosphere interactions; however, candidates from all areas of environmental engineering are encouraged to apply and will receive full consideration.  
  
The successful candidate will contribute to the growth of environmental engineering research at URI and help advance the launch and long-term success of URI's new Bachelor of Science degree program in Environmental Engineering.  
  
**THE POSITION IS IN-PERSON**  
  
**POSITION SUMMARY:**  
  
The successful candidate will be expected to develop a nationally recognized and externally funded research program; publish high-impact scholarship; teach undergraduate and graduate courses; mentor undergraduate and graduate students; contribute to the new BS Environmental Engineering curriculum; and participate in service to the department, college, university, profession, and broader community.  
  
Applicants are expected to hold a terminal degree in environmental engineering, civil engineering, chemical engineering, environmental health engineering, or a closely related field by the time of appointment. Required qualifications include evidence of potential for excellence in research and teaching; a strong record of scholarly activity appropriate to career stage; effective written and oral communication skills; and the ability to work effectively with students, faculty, staff, and external partners. Preferred qualifications include evidence of potential for external research funding; experience advising or mentoring students; ability to teach core undergraduate or graduate environmental engineering courses; interest in program development; and Professional Engineering licensure or the ability to pursue licensure.  
  
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering is housed within URI's College of Engineering and is entering an exciting period of growth. The department offers undergraduate and graduate programs in civil and environmental engineering and is launching a new BS degree in Environmental Engineering. The successful candidate will join URI at a pivotal moment, with opportunities to help shape a new undergraduate degree program while expanding the department's research impact in environmental engineering.  
  
Faculty and students in the College of Engineering work in the Fascitelli Center for Advanced Engineering (FCAE), a 190,000-square-foot facility designed to support interdisciplinary engineering research and education. Research in the facility is organized around themes that include clean water, sensors and instrumentation, alternative energy, advanced materials, robotics, biomedical technology, and nanotechnology. FCAE also houses the Shimadzu Analytical Core, the RI Water Resources Center, and the RI Consortium for Nanoscience and Nanotechnology.
