To be the national model for the engaged university: engaged with ideas and the world.
  
  
Who We Are
  
Situated in the heart of Virginia’s beautiful Shenandoah Valley, the city of Harrisonburg is a vibrant community with a population of approximately 52,000. Harrisonburg is conveniently located approximately 120 miles from Washington, D.C. and Richmond, VA.
  
  
JMU is a selective, public institution with a growing national reputation for offering experiences that lead to an outstanding education and supportive environment for students, faculty and staff. The student body includes approximately 21,000 undergraduate and 1,800 graduate students, with over 1,000 full-time instructional faculty.

JMU has achieved national recognition for the high quality of its academic programs, focus on maintaining strong student/faculty interaction, and innovative faculty research.

**General Information:**

The Department of Physics and Astronomy at James Madison University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Physics with expertise in data-intensive, computational, and/or AI-enabled approaches to physics, astronomy, or closely related fields. This is a full-time appointment beginning August 10, 2027.
  
  
The Department of Physics & Astronomy at James Madison University combines a strong commitment to undergraduate education with an active culture of scholarship and discovery. Through excellent teaching, close mentorship, and faculty-led research programs that engage undergraduate students, the department provides a rich educational experience for its majors. The department consists of 21 full-time faculty members, most of whom maintain active research agendas, and approximately 70 students enrolled in our multi-track baccalaureate-only programs.

The successful candidate will contribute to the department's mission through outstanding teaching, active scholarship, and meaningful service. Teaching responsibilities include undergraduate physics and/or astronomy courses and laboratories at both introductory and advanced levels. The candidate will establish and maintain an active, externally visible research program that engages undergraduate students and enhances the scholarly reputation of the department, college, and university. Florida International University is a Top 50, preeminent public research university with 55,000 students from all 50 states and more than 140 countries, as well as an alumni network of more than 340,000. Located in the global city of Miami, the university offers more than 200 degree programs at the undergraduate, graduate and professional levels, including medicine and law. A Carnegie R1 institution, FIU drives impactful research in environmental resilience, health and technology and innovation. Home to the Wall of Wind and Institute of Environment, FIU stands at the forefront of discovery and innovation. With a focus on student success, economic mobility and community engagement, FIU is redefining what it means to be a public research university.

  
**Job Information**

**Assistant Teaching Professor in Sport and Recreation Management**

Position Description

The Department of Counseling, Recreation and School Psychology (CRSP) at Florida International University (FIU) invites applications for a full-time, 12-month, non-tenure track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Teaching Professor in Sport and Recreation Management, to commence in the Fall semester of 2027.

Responsibilities

The appointed faculty member will have an assignment in the areas of instruction (90%) and service (10%).

The instruction assignment during the first year will be a 4/4/3 teaching load (11 courses in the academic year) and involve the delivery of undergraduate and/or graduate courses for the Sport and Recreation Management program, in in-person and online modalities. The appointee will also be expected to participate in student mentorship activities.

Beyond instruction, the position encompasses service contributions to support the department's mission. These may include assisting with the accreditation process of the sport management program, actively participating in curriculum meetings, and representing the department's standards and goals. Additionally, the successful candidate will be expected to maintain active involvement with industry and relevant professional associations to enhance our students' educational experiences and raise the profile of the program in the professional community.

Minimum Qualifications

* Terminal degree in Sports Management or a closely related field.
* Demonstrated effectiveness in instruction in a variety of modalities, including in-person and fully online courses at an institution of higher education.

Preferred Qualifications:

* Evidence of excellence in teaching, industry and leadership experience
* Strong organizational and communication skills.
* Ten (10) or more years of industry experience in a leadership role in Sport and Recreation Management

Nationally competitive and commensurate with experience based on appropriate salary survey.

The Sport and Recreation Management Program is a vibrant and growing program with a healthy number of applicants and strong enrollment. The Department of Mechanical Engineering and Engineering Science (MEES) is the largest department in the William States Lee College of Engineering. Its 54 full-time faculty members and 16 staff members serve approximately 2,000 undergraduate and graduate students. The department currently has six active NSF CAREER awards, and several faculty members are Fellows of leading professional societies.

MEES has established research programs in advanced manufacturing, precision metrology, battery research, motorsports and automotive engineering, control systems, computational mechanics, hypersonics, transport phenomena, and autonomous vehicles.

The department is home to the Center for Precision Metrology, the Center for Additive Manufacturing of Advanced Ceramics, and the Battery Complexity, Autonomous Vehicle and Electrification Research Center. It has also recently launched an undergraduate concentration in Aerospace Engineering.

The College of Engineering leads initiatives in several strategic research areas, including Advanced Manufacturing and Metrology, Transformational Energy, and Transportation and Advanced Mobility. The College is also home to the newly established NSF Grid Modernization Engine in the Carolinas. Other University initiatives supporting robotics and unmanned systems include the Charlotte Aviation Innovation and Research Institute (AIR) and the National Defense and Intelligence Innovation Institute (NDI3).

  

**Vacancy Open to**

All Candidates

  

**Description of Work**

The University of North Carolina at Charlotte recognizes the differentiation of mission, goals, and objectives inherent in the diversity of disciplines represented by its colleges and departments. Thus, the Job Responsibilities and Essential Functions for Tenured and Tenure Track Faculty should be interpreted in the context of the related departmental and collegiate goals.
  
Teaching, Advising, Curriculum and Instructional Development – Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to teaching may include but are not limited to: subject matter competence, course design, course presentation, advising and consultation, directing student research, curriculum and instructional development, and grading student work.
  
Scholarly Research, Creative, and Other Professional Activities – All tenured and tenure-track faculty are expected to participate in expanding the knowledge base of their academic field by conducting research or engaging in other creative activities as appropriate to the faculty member’s discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to research may include but are not limited to: research/creative activity that generates new knowledge and/or synthesizes and/or integrates existing knowledge, publication, an on-going agenda for research, scholarly, and creative activity, and are expected to seek extramural support for their work.
  
Service to University, the Public, and the Profession – All tenured and tenure-track faculty are expected to engage in a program of service appropriate to their discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to service may include but are not limited to: service to the administration and governance of the University, public service, and service to the profession.
  
  
This position is subject to research-security screening. As part of the application, applicants must disclose, **either in their CV or in a separate document submitted with the application**, all current appointments or affiliations with foreign institutions or organizations, foreign research support, and ongoing research collaborations with foreign institutions, organizations, or their personnel. Before candidates advance to an on-campus interview, the university will review this information and other publicly available information for relationships involving institutions on the current Section 1286 list and any other applicable U.S. restricted-party lists. A disclosed or identified relationship does not automatically disqualify a candidate. As a condition of employment, a selected candidate must resolve any relationship the university determines would violate applicable law or sponsor requirements or materially impair the candidate’s or the university’s eligibility for federal funding.
  
  
To view the complete Job Responsibilities and Essential Functions for Tenured and Tenure-Track Faculty document visit our website: https://facultyhandbooks.charlotte.edu/full-time-faculty-handbook/

  

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

The Department of Mechanical Engineering and Engineering Science at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte invites applications for a nine-month, tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor in robotics, with an expected start date of August 2027.

We seek candidates conducting foundational research in robotics and autonomy with broad applications across manufacturing, aerospace, space, defense, and energy.

Areas of interest include, but are not limited to:

* Embodied AI, physical intelligence, and learning-enabled robotics;
* Robotic manipulation and locomotion;
* Mobile robotics and autonomous systems;
* Robotics and automation for advanced manufacturing; and
* Soft, continuum, and compliant robotic systems.
  

Research that complements and expands existing departmental strengths is particularly encouraged. Relevant faculty expertise includes digital twins and AI for manufacturing, human–robot interaction, assisted driving, traffic-flow automation, bio-inspired robotics, multi-robot systems and swarms, precision engineering, and path planning for unmanned aerial, marine, and space systems.

  
  

**Minimum Experience/Education**

UNC Charlotte gives primary consideration to the earned doctorate or terminal degree in the teaching discipline or a related discipline.

  

**Preferred Education, Skills and Experience**

Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics Engineering, or a closely related field by the time of appointment.
  
  
Priority will be given to candidates with strong research records, as demonstrated by peer-reviewed publications, relevant professional activities, evidence of or potential for securing external funding, and a research vision aligned with departmental and University priorities.

  

**Necessary Licenses/Certifications**

  

**Special Notes to Applicants**

The successful candidate will be expected to:

* Establish a strong, externally funded research program;
* Publish in leading research journals;
* Teach undergraduate and graduate courses;
* Advise graduate theses and dissertations;
* Supervise undergraduate capstone projects; and
* Develop collaborations with faculty, industry partners, and national laboratories

#### **About this Position**

**Open Rank Professor of Computer Science**

The Oklahoma State University (OSU) Department of Computer Science is seeking applications for an open-rank tenure-track position with a start date of August 2027. Preferred research and teaching interests are in cybersecurity with an emphasis on **digital** **forensics** **and** **cyber** **investigations**, **reverse** **engineering** **and** **malware** **analysis, and cybersecurity operations and incident management**, or related areas with a solid track record in the core Computer Science domains.

**Responsibilities:**

Our department’s mission is to pursue and to publicize research projects in computer science in order to extend the present state of knowledge in the computer field, educate students in all program levels in order to provide them with the knowledge, interest, and ethics to become productive members of the computing profession, and serve as an initial and continuing source of education in the field of computer science.

The successful candidate will demonstrate their alignment with this mission through a clear research record along with the potential for teaching, support of program growth, and commitment to excellence in service and extension. Faculty are expected to pursue research collaborations with other faculty, industry, and research institutions as well as to further the university’s land grant mission through excellence in teaching and outreach activities. All faculty members are also expected to support the department's efforts in developing and teaching courses for our online certificate and degree programs and may be assigned to either the Tulsa or Stillwater campus. Junior faculty members are expected to be heavily research focused and during their first three years are only required to teach one course per semester.

**About the Department of Computer Science**

The OSU Department of Computer Science (https://cs.okstate.edu) is strongly committed to excellence in research, teaching, and outreach. The Department offers B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. degrees in Computer Science, a B.S. degree in Applied Computer Programming, and two new interdisciplinary M.S. programs in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science. The Department also offers online courses to students at remote sites. Our recent student enrollment is approximately 420 undergraduate and 100 graduate students across all our majors with expected continued growth over the coming years.

**About Oklahoma State University**

Oklahoma State University is a Carnegie R1 research institution with a 130-year legacy as one of the nation’s model land-grant universities. Its beautiful Stillwater campus serves as the flagship of the OSU system, which enrolls more than 34,000 students. The College of Arts and Sciences offers exceptional strengths across the natural sciences, social sciences, and arts and humanities, complemented by institutional excellence in engineering, agriculture, and business. Together, these strengths support a collaborative intellectual environment and OSU’s longstanding commitment to research, teaching, and public engagement.

Home to approximately 50,000 residents, Stillwater offers the welcoming atmosphere and affordability of a college town within an hour’s drive of two major metropolitan areas, Tulsa and Oklahoma City. The city benefits from a vibrant, university-centered intellectual and cultural community, with lectures, performances, exhibitions, Cowboy athletics, and traditions such as OSU’s signature Homecoming and Walkaround traditions. The McKnight Center for the Performing Arts brings internationally renowned artists and ensembles, including the New York Philharmonic, to Stillwater, while the OSU Botanic Garden, Block 34 park and amphitheater, Main Street, locally owned restaurants and breweries, parks, trails, and abundant outdoor recreation contribute to the city’s quality of life. Stillwater Regional Airport’s new passenger terminal and multiple daily flights to Dallas–Fort Worth provide convenient connections to destinations across the world.

#### **Required Qualifications**

* Ph.D. in Computer Science or closely related discipline (degree must be conferred on or before agreed upon start date).
* Demonstrated research background as evidenced by conference and journal publications in high-quality venues commensurate with rank.
* Demonstrated ability to effectively mentor and collaborate with students and colleagues.
* Evidence of university-level teaching success commensurate with rank.

#### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Evidence of successful grantsmanship.
* Evidence of the ability to create and/or manage a successful research or teaching program.
* Demonstrated knowledge and experience in program accreditation, which may include ABET or NSA NCAE.

**Department of Physics - Open Rank Faculty Search** 
**Experimental Condensed Matter and Quantum Information Science**
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### **The Grainger College of Engineering** **University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign**

The Department of Physics in the Grainger College of Engineering at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign invites applications for one (1) open-rank (assistant, associate, or full professor level) tenure-track, full-time faculty position in experimental quantum physics, broadly defined, including quantum information science (QIS), condensed matter physics (CMP), and atomic, molecular, and optical (AMO) physics.

Successful candidates must be able to teach in these and other areas while also contributing to the excellence of our programs through research and service efforts. Candidates are expected to establish and maintain an active and independent research program, teach effectively at both the undergraduate and graduate levels, and provide service to the department, the university, and the profession.

Illinois Physics has broad and internationally recognized strengths in experimental and theoretical research spanning condensed matter physics (CMP), atomic, molecular, and optical (AMO) physics, and quantum information science (QIS). Current research encompasses a wide range of topics, including strongly correlated and topological quantum matter, superconductivity, bulk, thin films, and 2D quantum materials, magnetism, non-equilibrium quantum phenomena, quantum simulation and sensing, quantum algorithms and quantum error correction, superconducting and solid-state qubits, atomic and photonic quantum systems, quantum memories, hybrid quantum networks, quantum transduction, and the development and study of novel platforms for quantum information processing.

Faculty have access to a rich campus-wide research environment and extensive opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration, including close interactions with theorists at the Anthony J. Leggett Institute for Condensed Matter Theory and through the Illinois Quantum Information Science and Technology Center (IQUIST). IQUIST brings together QIS researchers from Physics and departments across the University, while the Illinois Seitz Materials Research Laboratory (MRL) provides a major hub for interdisciplinary materials research and state-of-the-art experimental facilities. Illinois researchers also participate in and lead major multi-institutional quantum initiatives, including the NSF Quantum Leap Challenge Institute for Hybrid Quantum Architectures and Networks (HQAN), Q-NEXT, the Chicago Quantum Exchange (CQE), the IBM-Illinois Discovery Accelerator Institute, and the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP).

A doctoral degree in Physics or a related field is required by the expected fall 2027 start date; however, starting date is negotiable. The budgeted salary range for the position is $115,000 to $135,000 at the Assistant Professor level, $135,000 to $160,000 at the Associate Professor level, and $160,000 to $220,000 at the Full Professor level, for a 9-month service basis paid over 12 months. Salary is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience, while also considering internal equity. Full consideration will be given to applications received by **November 2, 2026.** Applications may be reviewed as they are received. Those submitted after the stated deadline may still be considered until the position is filled. Applicants may be interviewed before the closing date; however, no hiring decision will be made until after that date. This position is eligible for work authorization sponsorship.  
  
  

To apply for this position, please create a candidate profile at https://jobs.illinois.edu. The application package should include the following materials uploaded as a single PDF file in the “Resume/CV” section: 1) cover letter, 2) curriculum vitae, 3) research statement, 4) teaching statement, 5) service statement, and 6) names and contact information for at least three professional references (no letters required at this time). The research, teaching, and service statements offer a chance to share your motivation, approach, experience, leadership, impact, and vision in each area, including how you would support the university’s land-grant mission (https://boldly.illinois.edu/), through campus, community, or professional engagement. For further information regarding application procedures, please address questions to Stephanie Swearingen and sswearin@illinois.edu.

Faculty and students at Illinois benefit from access to world-class experimental and computational facilities across campus, including: Advanced Materials Testing and Evaluation Laboratory, the Coordinated Science Laboratory, Materials Research Laboratory, Holonyak Micro & Nanotechnology Lab, the Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology, and the National Center for Supercomputing Applications.

We have an active and successful Dual Career Academic Couples Program and a strong commitment to work-life balance and family-friendly programs for faculty and staff (https://provost.illinois.edu/faculty-affairs/work-life-balance/).

Founded in 1867 as Illinois’s flagship public university, the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign empowers a global community of students, scholars, and alumni to change the world through bold, innovative research and transformative education. With a land-grant heritage rooted in progress, Illinois faculty drive paradigm-shifting discoveries, mentor future leaders, and collaborate across 15 colleges and instructional units and more than 20 research institutes. The university’s legacy of excellence includes **24 Nobel Prizes and 29 Pulitzer Prizes** awarded to its faculty and alumni, $755 million in sponsored research funding, and 94 academic programs ranked in the top 20 nationally. Illinois offers the resources, recognition, and reach to accelerate your career — along with a highly competitive benefits portfolio. Discover how the Illinois Value Proposition fosters professional longevity, personal fulfillment, and a deep sense of purpose in every role.

Successful candidates will have outstanding academic and research records and are expected to establish a vigorous, funded research program, teach at the undergraduate and graduate levels, and be involved in service to the University and the profession. An earned doctorate or equivalent foreign degree in an appropriate discipline is required at the time of appointment. It is anticipated that the appointment will begin Fall 2027. Completion of PhD required.  
  
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering is committed to fostering a community of research, teaching, and operational excellence that is culturally and academically diverse by attracting and retaining individuals with a variety of backgrounds, experiences, viewpoints, and identities. Candidates who will actively contribute to this commitment and community - both in identity and professional vision - are particularly encouraged to apply.

The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities invites applications in three areas: (i) Computer Engineering, (ii) Artificial Intelligence, and (iii) Optics and Photonics. This tenure-track faculty position will be filled at the Assistant Professor level; salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.

Computer Engineering:  
  
Expertise in chip design and verification, electronic design automation, computer architecture, and emerging computing platforms is of particular interest, including AI/ML hardware, heterogeneous integration, quantum and physics-inspired computing. Expertise in novel devices and microelectronics for quantum and physics-inspired computing will also be considered.  
  
Collaborative research and development in chip design, verification methods, electronic design automation, and computer architecture is of particular interest. Relevant applications include, but are not limited to, AI/ML accelerator design, AI/ML for chip design and verification, domain-specific computing, heterogeneous architectures, hardware-algorithm co-design, quantum computing, and physics-inspired computing.

Artificial Intelligence:  
  
Expertise in the algorithms, theory, and applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning.  
  
Collaboration in research and development in basic and applied research in artificial intelligence and machine learning. Theoretical areas of interest include, but are not limited to, optimization, neural networks, and reinforcement learning. Application areas of interest include, but are not limited to, robotics, foundation models, image / signal processing, optimization, and control.

Optics and Photonics:  
  
Expertise in the fields of optics, photonics, nanophotonics, quantum optics, optical materials, devices, instrumentation, and systems, including, but are not limited to, integrated and nano-scale photonics, metasurfaces, and plasmonics, micro/nanofabrication techniques, biophotonics and optical biosensing, optical imaging and spectroscopy, optical measurement and sensing science and instrumentation, quantum optics, optoelectronics and silicon photonics, optical communications and interconnects, and optical computing.  
  
Collaboration in research and development of one or more of the above listed fields of expertise is of particular interest. Candidates whose work bridges optics and photonics with emerging areas such as quantum technologies or computing, packaging, neuroengineering, biomedical diagnostics, high power devices or systems, or AI-enabled systems are particularly encouraged to apply. Demonstrated ability in micro- and/or nanofabrication is desirable; candidates are expected to make extensive use of the Minnesota Nano Center (MNC) cleanroom facilities.

Responsibilities  
  
Research

* Engage in research, publication, and creation of scientific and engineering knowledge.
* Develop research proposals for external funding opportunities and collaborate with researchers from academia, industry, and other organizations such as government labs on joint research projects.

Teaching

* Develop and teach undergraduate and graduate courses in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering.
* Advise students regarding specific coursework and broader academic or career goals. Service
* Provide service through participation in governance of the department and/or the University.
* Contribute to outreach activities that support the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering mission.
* Contribute to the development of the profession, keep current with the field, and broaden knowledge and expertise.

Service

* Provide service through participation in governance of the department and/or the University.
* Contribute to outreach activities that support the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering mission.

jobs.description:
The School of Psychology and Cognitive Science at the Rochester Institute of Technology invites applications for a full-time, 9-month tenure-track Assistant Professor of Computational Linguistics, beginning in August 2027. Candidates are expected to have an earned doctoral degree (in hand by August 2027) in Linguistics, Computational Linguistics, or a related field. The position additionally offers an affiliation with the Department of Modern Languages and Cultures in the School of Languages, Humanities, and Social Sciences.

Successful candidates should demonstrate computational expertise, strong research talent, and initiative in grant writing. Candidates should also have a plan for excellence in teaching and student mentoring at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Applicants must be able to teach our courses in language technology and large language models, natural language processing, and/or computational speech processing. In addition, applicants should be able to teach foundational linguistics from a cross-linguistic perspective, as well as courses in at least one additional linguistics, artificial intelligence, or cognitive science subfield. Proficiency in an additional language other than English is preferred, and we welcome research or teaching experience involving language learning. The position requires a commitment to teaching and mentoring, active research and publication, and a strong potential to attract external funding. Research and teaching are priorities for faculty at RIT, and all faculty are expected to mentor graduate and undergraduate students through advising, research, and in-class experiences.

The computational linguistics-related programs at RIT serve a rapidly expanding student population at a technical university. We are looking for a faculty colleague who can also contribute to the interdisciplinary M.S. program in Artificial Intelligence and the Ph.D. program in Cognitive Science. Our coursework is also offered to B.S. in Artificial Intelligence majors. In addition, RIT provides many opportunities for collaborative research across the institute in areas such as linguistics of sign languages and languages other than English, artificial intelligence, human-centered computing, and cybersecurity. RIT faculty have access to extensive research computing resources.

  

**REQUIRED MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Ph.D. (in hand by August 2027) in Linguistics, Computational Linguistics, or a related field.

* Have demonstrated ability to conduct independent research in computational linguistics.

* Demonstrate potential for external research grant attainment.

* Have consistently and recently published in computational linguistics.

* Demonstrate potential for excellence in teaching language technology, natural language processing, and/or computational speech processing.

* Demonstrate potential for excellence in teaching foundational linguistics from a cross-linguistic perspective, and courses in at least one more linguistics, artificial intelligence, or cognitive science subfield.

* Demonstrate potential for excellence in supervising graduate and undergraduate student research.

* Show a career trajectory that emphasizes a balance between research and teaching.

The Department enjoys productive relationships with other units housed within and beyond the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, including the Center for the Humanities and the Public Sphere. The University’s strong library holdings include the Baldwin Library of Historical Children’s Literature and the Harold and Mary Jean Hanson Rare Book Collection.

The University is a major comprehensive, land-grant, research-intensive university, ranked in recent years as among the nation’s top public universities. Gainesville, Florida is a city of approximately 150,000 residents in Alachua County. It sits 50 miles from the Gulf of Mexico, 67 miles from the Atlantic Ocean, and within a 2-hour drive to the major cities of Orlando, Tampa, and Jacksonville. Its many nearby parks, springs, and recreational areas offer year-round outdoor activities such as hiking, biking, diving, and nature photography. Cultural activities abound and local schools are highly rated. Learn more about what Gainesville has to offer at Visit Gainesville

Salary is competitive, commensurate with qualifications and experience and includes a full benefits package.

Leave: UF staff enjoy a generous paid leave plan as well as access to a sick-leave pool, parental leave, and leave payouts.

  

**Required Qualifications:**

PhD, and record of research/publication and teaching experience in British Romanticism and/or early Victorian literature.

We are especially interested in candidates with expertise in British Romanticism *and* early Victorian literature. **Job Description**

The Department of Mathematics at the University of Massachusetts Boston (UMass Boston) invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professorship in Mathematics beginning September 1, 2027. The research area of interest is in applied mathematics with a preferred emphasis in scientific and mathematical Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Applied Statistics, and related areas at the intersection of mathematics, statistics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and data science. We are especially interested in candidates whose research combines rigorous mathematical and computational methodologies with impactful applications, preferably in biotechnology, biomedicine, neuroscience, or related scientific domains. Exceptional candidates from other areas of applied mathematics are encouraged to apply.

The Mathematics Department at UMass Boston is a vibrant and collegial group of faculty with research interests spanning the spectrum of pure and applied mathematics including Geometry and Symplectic Topology; Representation Theory; and Applied Mathematics, Data Science, and Mathematical Biology, and it pursues an important teaching mission. The College of Science and Mathematics is committed to inclusive excellence in research and education. We are a highly collaborative college of STEM including departments of Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics and Physics, and strong interdisciplinary Ph.D. programs. State-of-the-art research computing facilities, including high-performance computing clusters, are available to UMass Boston researchers. Partnerships and collaborations with academic institutions and industry research laboratories in the Greater Boston area offer substantial opportunities for collaboration.

The successful candidate must possess a PhD degree in mathematics, statistics or related fields and must have a robust research program and strong potential to secure extramural funding. The successful candidate will have an opportunity to expand and strengthen the research within the department and college. All candidates must exhibit a clear commitment to advancing the university's teaching mission through their participation in on-going student success initiatives in the department and the university. The successful candidate will also have the capacity to contribute to broad departmental and college service. A teaching load reduction to root a strong research program will be provided. For more information about the department see https://www.umb.edu/science-mathematics/academic-departments/mathematics/.

UMass Boston is an urban public research university with a teaching soul, whose impact is both local and global. We are the third most diverse university in the country - more than 60% of our undergraduate students come from minoritized communities and groups and more than half of our students are the first in their families to attend a college or university. Thus, our students come to us from richly diverse life experiences and backgrounds; they bring to our classrooms and research settings the robust range of perspectives growing out of the socio-cultural, economic, and historical contexts in which they have lived, along with the challenges they encounter, engage, and strive to overcome. We invite applications from candidates who engage the diverse life experiences of our student body, who appreciate that students bring their holistic selves into the academic setting, and who recognize and articulate how their own life experiences and backgrounds have shaped their journeys, practices, and commitments as researchers, scholars, and educators.

**Application instructions:**

Please submit (i) a cover letter, and (ii) a curriculum vitae via the application portal. Additionally, applicants are strongly encouraged to submit supplemental materials to MathJobs.org at the following link: https://www.mathjobs.org/jobs/list/29136. These materials should consist of the following: (i) a cover letter; (ii) a curriculum vitae; (iii) a standard AMS cover sheet; (iv) a statement of current research, vision, and future research plans; (v) a description of teaching philosophy and experience. In addition, you should arrange for four (4) writers to submit letters of recommendation to MathJobs.org, with one of these letters addressing teaching. Please note that applications are considered incomplete (and will not be considered) unless the cover letter and curriculum vitae are submitted to https://employmentopportunities.umb.edu/boston/en-us/job/530146/assistant-professor-mathematics. For full consideration, applications should be received by December 18, 2026. For inquiries, email: math@umb.edu.

The specific pay for this position will be determined by the University based on the consideration of all relevant factors when and if it decides to extend an offer of employment.

UMass Boston is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, we will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations for the hiring process. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please contact HR@umb.edu or 617-287-5150.

Position Description

**Department**: Civil and Environmental Engineering **Salary**: Commensurate with experience

**Description**:

The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at the University of Houston seeks an exceptional scholar to expand its research and educational programs in environmental engineering at the rank of Assistant Professor. Areas of particular research interest include, but are not limited to, air quality engineering; environmental sensing and monitoring; indoor air quality and the built environment; emerging environmental pollutants; resource recovery and reuse; and environmental and community health.
  
  
Candidates whose research integrates advanced sensing technologies, artificial intelligence, data analytics, or data-driven modeling with experimental or field-based environmental engineering are especially encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will have opportunities to develop collaborations with researchers across the University in environmental engineering, atmospheric sciences, public health, data science, energy, materials, and related areas and to utilize shared Departmental, College, and University research facilities.
  
  
The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate education in environmental engineering, including instruction in areas that complement the Department's existing strengths in water and advanced treatment systems and that engage emerging research directions.
  
  
This position advances the University of Houston Research Priorities in Energy, Security and Sustainability through research addressing environmental sustainability, water and resource security, pollution prevention, and resource recovery, and in Health and Well-being through research linking environmental quality, the built environment, and community health. Research incorporating advanced sensing, artificial intelligence, and environmental data science also aligns with the Digital Futures and the Human Experience priority.
  
  
**Qualifications**
  
Applicants must have an earned Ph.D. in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or a closely related field by the time of appointment. Candidates are expected to develop and maintain an internationally recognized and externally funded research program; publish high-impact scholarship; mentor graduate and undergraduate researchers; contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching; and participate in professional and University service.
  
  
Candidates whose scholarship creates collaborations across traditional disciplinary boundaries and complements existing research strengths within the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department, the Cullen College of Engineering, and the broader University of Houston research enterprise are particularly encouraged to apply.
  
  
**University, College, and Department**
  
The University of Houston is a Carnegie-designated Tier One public research university recognized with a Phi Beta Kappa chapter for excellence in undergraduate education. UH serves the globally competitive Houston and Gulf Coast region by providing world-class faculty, experiential learning and strategic industry partnerships. Located in the nation's fourth-largest city and one of the most vibrant regions in the country, UH enrolls nearly 49,000 students.
  
  
The Cullen College of Engineering is a major center for engineering research and education, with more than $58 million in annual research expenditures, more than 200 tenured and tenure-track faculty, and extensive research infrastructure supporting interdisciplinary scholarship. Cullen is ranked among the Top 50 public graduate engineering schools in the United States. Located within one of the nation’s largest engineering and technology economies, the College has strong connections with Houston’s energy, aerospace, health care, and technology sectors, creating exceptional opportunities for industry partnership, technology translation, and research impact.
  
  
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering conducts interdisciplinary research aimed at advancing the sustainability and resilience of natural and built environments. Its approximately 20 tenure-track faculty members work across environmental engineering, hydrosystems, geosensing, geotechnical and structural engineering, and mechanics, using advanced sensing, computational modeling, and other emerging technologies. Houston and the Gulf Coast provide a distinctive living laboratory for research on water systems, flooding and coastal hazards, infrastructure, environmental quality, and urban resilience, with substantial opportunities for collaboration with public agencies, industry, and other research institutions.
  
  
**How to Apply**
  
Applications should include:
  

* a cover letter identifying the position for which the candidate wishes to be considered (Hydrology/Water Resources or Environmental Engineering or both);
* a curriculum vitae;
* a research statement describing past accomplishments and future research plans, not exceeding two pages;
* a teaching statement describing teaching philosophy, expertise, and interests, not exceeding two pages; and
* names and complete contact information for four professional references.

  
Applications should be submitted through the University of Houston Careers website at https://www.uh.edu/human-resources/careers/.
  
  
The anticipated start date is Fall 2027. Review of applications will continue until the position is filled.

Employees are expected to have a home address in the state of Texas for the duration of their appointments.
  
  
Official transcripts are required for a faculty appointment and will be requested upon selection of the final candidates.
  
  
All positions at the University of Houston-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check. Individuals conducting research in critical infrastructure areas (i.e., communication infrastructure systems, cybersecurity systems, electric grid, hazardous waste treatment systems, and/or water treatment facilities) are subject to regular review to ensure the security and integrity of the research is maintained.
  
  
The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

jobs.description:
The Department of History at Thiel College invites applications for a tenure-track position in United States History. Teaching responsibilities will include American surveys and upper-division courses in United States History. Areas of specialization are open, but preference will be given to candidates whose teaching and professional interests support the preparation of future history educators and the use of technology to enhance history instruction, historical research, and student learning.

Candidates should have an interest in joining an undergraduate department where teaching in a small classroom environment is emphasized. Expectations include a 4/4 teaching load, developing engaging pedagogy, openness to interdisciplinary courses, advising, and active involvement in the campus community. Candidates must have a Doctorate in History; candidates currently completing doctoral work will also be considered.

A dedicated passion for helping students reach their full potential in a supportive and inclusive, diverse environment is essential to this position. Responsibilities include teaching, advising, student supervision, and professional development. While Thiel College gives highest priority to teaching effectiveness, faculty are expected to remain current in the field through professional development opportunities such as attendance at related conferences, research, or other scholarly activities. A comprehensive employee benefit package, including research support and a sabbatical program, is provided.

Thiel College welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. Please note, however, that we are unable to provide employment visa sponsorship (e.g., H-1B) for this position. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship.

**To Apply:**

Thiel College welcomes applications from all qualified candidates. Please note, however, that we are unable to provide employment visa sponsorship (e.g., H-1B) for this position. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship.

Applicants should:

* Submit a letter of interest, curriculum vitae and list of references (all these materials should be attached in a single PDF document using candidate’s name as the document title) by clicking here.
* Additional required materials, including transcripts, sample syllabi for both a survey and an upper-division U.S. history course, and summaries of recent teaching evaluations, if available, should be sent in PDF format to employment@thiel.edu (preferred option). These items may also be mailed to Jennifer Clark, Director of Human Resources, Thiel College, 75 College Avenue, Greenville, PA. 16125.

Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled.

Thiel College is committed to attracting culturally and professionally diverse faculty and staff who engage our students by providing a rich and fulfilling curricular and co-curricular experience.

**About Thiel College**

Thiel College is an independent liberal arts college rooted in the Lutheran tradition. Thiel College empowers individuals to reach their full potential by creating a diverse and inclusive learning environment that ensures educational excellence, stimulates global awareness, and promotes ethical leadership. In doing so, Thiel prepares students for careers and lives of meaning and purpose.

Greenville is in northwestern Pennsylvania, a 90-minute drive from both Pittsburgh and Cleveland and a 40-minute drive from Youngstown, Ohio. Greenville and the surrounding areas have scenic parks, trails, and waterways for relaxing, hiking, camping, and boating. The area has a low cost of living, making it a desirable location for young professionals and growing families.

This is a full-time, 9-month, faculty appointment with employment starting in August 2027. Rank, tenure, and salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.

Marian University is located in Indianapolis, Indiana, which is known as the ‘Sports Capital of the World.’ By joining our team, you will benefit from a city that integrates professional growth with an exceptional quality of life, with affordable living, top-ranked communities, and an area built for an active lifestyle.

Position Description

**Department**: Civil and Environmental Engineering **Salary**: Commensurate with experience

**Description**:

The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at the University of Houston (UH) invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty positions at the Assistant or Associate Professor rank. The Department seeks outstanding candidates who will establish internationally recognized, externally funded research programs, contribute to undergraduate and graduate education, and collaborate across disciplinary boundaries within the Department, Cullen College of Engineering, and University.
  
  
The Department seeks an exceptional scholar to strengthen its research and educational programs in hydrology, hydraulics, earth system modeling, watershed science, and water resources. Areas of research interest include, but are not limited to, floods, droughts, hydraulics, hydrodynamics, sediment transport, hurricanes, coastal engineering, water security, weather extremes, infrastructure resilience to hydrologic hazards, and coupled natural-human infrastructure systems.
  
  
Candidates employing advanced computational, observational, and data-driven research approaches are especially encouraged to apply. Relevant approaches may include hydrologic and earth system modeling, experimental research, remote sensing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. The successful candidate will have opportunities to collaborate with faculty working in environmental fluid mechanics, water resources, hydrology, natural disasters, hydrodynamics, remote sensing, earth system modeling, and the use of machine learning and high-performance computing to understand extreme weather events such as hurricanes, compound flooding, and coastal resilience.
  
  
The position will contribute to undergraduate and graduate instruction in hydrology and water resources and may develop courses in related areas such as watershed processes, flood prediction, urban and coastal flooding, water infrastructure, and hydrologic extremes. Houston, Texas, and the Gulf Coast provide a compelling setting for research addressing compound floods, hurricanes, coastal processes, water security, and the resilience of natural and engineered water systems.
  
  
This position advances the University of Houston Research Priorities in Energy, Security and Sustainability through research addressing water security, hydrologic extremes, infrastructure resilience, and the impacts of floods, droughts, and hurricanes on natural and engineered systems, and in Aerospace and Earth and Planetary Sciences through research on hydrology, earth system processes, watershed science, and coastal change. Research incorporating remote sensing, advanced modeling, artificial intelligence, and machine learning also aligns with the Digital Futures and the Human Experience priority.
  
  
**Qualifications**
  
Applicants must have an earned Ph.D. in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or a closely related field by the time of appointment. Candidates are expected to develop and maintain an internationally recognized and externally funded research program; publish high-impact scholarship; mentor graduate and undergraduate researchers; contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching; and participate in professional and University service.
  
  
Applicants at the Associate Professor level should demonstrate a strong record of scholarly achievement, externally funded research, graduate student mentorship, and national or international recognition appropriate to the rank.
  
  
Candidates whose scholarship creates collaborations across traditional disciplinary boundaries and complements existing research strengths within the Civil and Environmental Engineering Department, the Cullen College of Engineering, and the broader University of Houston research enterprise are particularly encouraged to apply.
  
  
Salary and rank will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.
  
  
**University, College, and Department**
  
The University of Houston is a Carnegie-designated Tier One public research university recognized with a Phi Beta Kappa chapter for excellence in undergraduate education. UH serves the globally competitive Houston and Gulf Coast region by providing world-class faculty, experiential learning and strategic industry partnerships. Located in the nation's fourth-largest city and one of the most vibrant regions in the country, UH enrolls nearly 49,000 students.
  
  
The Cullen College of Engineering is a major center for engineering research and education, with more than $58 million in annual research expenditures, more than 200 tenured and tenure-track faculty, and extensive research infrastructure supporting interdisciplinary scholarship. Cullen is ranked among the Top 50 public graduate engineering schools in the United States. Located within one of the nation’s largest engineering and technology economies, the College has strong connections with Houston’s energy, aerospace, health care, and technology sectors, creating exceptional opportunities for industry partnership, technology translation, and research impact.
  
  
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering conducts interdisciplinary research aimed at advancing the sustainability and resilience of natural and built environments. Its approximately 20 tenure-track faculty members work across environmental engineering, hydrosystems, geosensing, geotechnical and structural engineering, and mechanics, using advanced sensing, computational modeling, and other emerging technologies. Houston and the Gulf Coast provide a distinctive living laboratory for research on water systems, flooding and coastal hazards, infrastructure, environmental quality, and urban resilience, with substantial opportunities for collaboration with public agencies, industry, and other research institutions.
  
  
**How to Apply**
  
Applications should include:
  

* a cover letter identifying the position for which the candidate wishes to be considered (Hydrology/Water Resources or Environmental Engineering or both);
* a curriculum vitae;
* a research statement describing past accomplishments and future research plans, not exceeding two pages;
* a teaching statement describing teaching philosophy, expertise, and interests, not exceeding two pages; and
* names and complete contact information for four professional references.

  
Applications should be submitted through the University of Houston Careers website at https://www.uh.edu/human-resources/careers/.
  
  
The anticipated start date is Fall 2027. Review of applications will continue until the positions are filled.

Employees are expected to have a home address in the state of Texas for the duration of their appointments.
  
  
Official transcripts are required for a faculty appointment and will be requested upon selection of the final candidates.
  
  
All positions at the University of Houston-System are security sensitive and will require a criminal history check. Individuals conducting research in critical infrastructure areas (i.e., communication infrastructure systems, cybersecurity systems, electric grid, hazardous waste treatment systems, and/or water treatment facilities) are subject to regular review to ensure the security and integrity of the research is maintained.
  
  
The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Faculty position, Chief of Nuclear Medicine, Department of Radiology
jobs.description:
SJCRH
  
  
St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital invites applications for the role of Chief of Nuclear Medicine in the Department of Radiology.We seek an ABNM- or ABR-certified nuclear medicine physician or radiologist with subspecialty training in Nuclear Medicine, Molecular Imaging, and Theranostics to lead a dynamic program central to St. Jude’s mission of advancing cures for children with cancer and other catastrophic diseases.
  
  
The Chief will shape a world-class clinical and research program built around our new extended field-of-view PET/CT, molecular imaging core (cyclotron and radiochemistry lab), expanding molecular imaging research section, and image quantification and artificial intelligence (IQAI) collaboratory.
  
  
**Our Mission and Vision**
:
  
  
The mission of St. Jude Radiology is to advance cures and understanding of pediatric cancer and catastrophic diseases through excellence in radiology research, innovation, clinical practice, education, and administration. Our vision is to lead the world in radiology for pediatric cancer and catastrophic diseases.
  
  
**Department Overview:**
The Department of Radiology is composed of seven sections: Nuclear Medicine, Neuroradiology, Body Radiology, Interventional Radiology, Intelligent Imaging Informatics (I3), Research, and Physics. Our patients include children with cancer, hematologic, infectious, and rare neurologic diseases, as well as research participants that are cancer survivors. Most of our patients are on clinical trials, providing rich opportunities for collaboration and for developing and validating imaging biomarkers and developing interventions that include theranostics.
  
  
**Clinician Scientists:**
Clinician–scientists at St. Jude are provided with exceptional support to build and sustain productive academic careers. Faculty on this track typically receive 50% protected research effort, along with dedicated full-time research staff (one, two, or three permanent staff members for assistant, associate, and full members, respectively). Each clinician scientist is also provided with a recurring research cost center that is renewed annually in perpetuity, ensuring long-term stability for program development. Start-up packages, including equipment and laboratory resources, are available to launch new research programs.
  
  
These resources are complemented by robust institutional infrastructure, including access to biostatistics, image processing, data science, software engineering, wet lab space, and grant-writing expertise. Clinician scientists are expected to pursue extramural funding, and St. Jude’s research environment is intentionally designed to promote success through mentorship, collaboration, and strong administrative and technical support.
  
  
**Clinical:**
Clinical responsibilities are designed to be balanced and sustainable, supporting excellence in both patient care and academic productivity. The Nuclear Medicine service is staffed by one faculty member on weekdays and carries no after-hours or weekend call, providing an optimal environment for integration of clinical, research, and educational activities. Nuclear Medicine clinical faculty interpret PET/CT, SPECT/CT, and nuclear scintigraphy studies, primarily serving pediatric oncology patients, while also contributing to innovative research applications for cancer and other catastrophic diseases, including first-in-human imaging agents. The section is equipped with state-of-the-art technology, including a 148 cm extended field-of-view PET/CT scanner (the first of this caliber installed in North America and the first in a dedicated pediatric hospital) which enables whole-body imaging with exceptional sensitivity and efficiency. The department will also replace its SPECT/CT system within the next year, further strengthening our advanced imaging capabilities and commitment to continuous innovation in pediatric molecular imaging.
  
  
**Molecular Imaging Core**
The Molecular Imaging Core (MIC) is a departmental resource that serves investigators across St. Jude by translating cutting-edge radiochemistry into impactful clinical and preclinical research. The MIC supports the production of multiple IND-approved PET tracers, facilitates first-in-human imaging studies, and collaborates closely with molecular imaging research faculty to develop and automate synthesis of novel tracers for infection, inflammation, and oncology. Equipped with a dedicated cyclotron facility, advanced radiosynthesis systems, and exceptional engineering expertise, the MIC enables the seamless transition of discovery science into FDA-compliant production for clinical trials. Recent achievements include the translation of the first-in-human [¹⁸F]fluoromannitol infection tracer and organization of national radiochemistry symposia that position St. Jude as a leader in pediatric molecular imaging innovation.
  
  
**Research:**
Research is central to the St. Jude mission, and the Department of Radiology provides an exceptional environment for innovation in molecular imaging, theranostics, and translational science. The molecular imaging section has one NIH-funded PhD faculty member, with two additional faculty hires planned to advance radiopharmaceutical development and translational molecular imaging. Faculty benefit from direct access to departmental resources including the Molecular Imaging Core, the Radiology Data Center, and Image Quantification and Artificial Intelligence (IQAI) collaboratory. Dedicated staff assist with grant writing, IRB management, clinical research coordination, image processing, and biostatistics, ensuring seamless integration of research and clinical activity. Partnerships across Oncology, Surgery, Pathology, the Molecular Imaging Core, and Data Science create fertile ground for developing novel PET tracers, radiopharmaceuticals, and image-guided treatment paradigms. Faculty are encouraged and supported in pursuing extramural funding from the NIH, foundations, and industry partners, building upon strong institutional mentorship and infrastructure.
  
  
**Artificial Intelligence:**
The department is deeply engaged in advancing artificial intelligence (AI) and quantitative imaging to improve both patient care and research. Some clinician scientists are also members of Intelligent Imaging Informatics (I3), an expanding section that harnesses the power of imaging informatics and AI to accelerate research, clinical care, and translational efforts in pediatric radiology, advancing the St. Jude Mission. The Image Quantification and Artificial Intelligence (IQAI) Co-Laboratory is a dedicated research and development team for biomedical informatics and AI. This interdisciplinary team serves the Department of Radiology by building and maintaining the advanced data infrastructure that fuels faculty-led research, performing collaborative projects with clinicians and scientists and conducting core biomedical informatics research. The IQAI team recently developed a Radiology Data Center (RDC) for data science that supports de-identified radiologic and pathology data, electronic medical records, and other institutional datasets. These resources collectively position St. Jude as a leader in the ethical and impactful application of AI in pediatric imaging and provide a strong foundation for developing and validating AI-driven molecular imaging and theranostic tools.
  
  
**Education:**
Education is an important component of our mission. Faculty have the opportunity to teach and mentor radiology fellows, radiology residents, medical students, graduate students, and postdoctoral fellows. St. Jude supports professional development by providing travel funds for faculty presentations at national and international conferences. The department hosts an annual international educational conference and a separate scientific symposium, including dedicated courses for molecular imaging and therapeutics. In February 2026, St. Jude will co-host a Pediatric Oncologic Imaging Course with the Society for Pediatric Radiology (SPR), including a session for nuclear medicine. Faculty actively participate in institutional and national educational initiatives.
  
  
**Compensation and Environment:**
St. Jude offers competitive compensation determined by faculty rank and fair market value, as well as comprehensive benefits and programs that support wellness, work–life balance, and career growth. The department fosters a culture of impact, excellence, collaboration, innovation, and mutual respect, where faculty elevate one another to achieve their maximum potential.
  
  
St. Jude is an Equal Opportunity Employer. St. Jude does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, sex, genetic information, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, transgender status, veteran’s status or disabled veteran’s status with respect to employment opportunities. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment.
  
  
We value different perspectives and intellectual discourse. We are committed to building an intellectually diverse community.
  
  
Academic rank and institutional resources will be commensurate with experience and qualification.
  
  
Requirements:
  
  
**Candidates must have an MD, DO or equivalent degree, be board certified by the American Board of Radiology and/or American Board of Nuclear Medicine and have experience in nuclear medicine, molecular imaging and theranostics. Applicants must qualify for medical licensure in the State of Tennessee.**
**To apply:**
Interested candidates should
**submit a CV**
**directly online**
.

Andrew D. Smith, MD PhD
  
  
Chair of the Department Radiology and Body Radiologist
  
  
Endowed Chair of Diagnostic Imaging
  
  
St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital
  
  
andrew.smith@stjude.org

jobs.description:
**Location:** El Paso, TX **Category:** Engineering **Job Type:** Full-time **Posted On:** Fri Oct 2 2026 **Job Description:**  
  

The Department of Civil Engineering has 22 full-time faculty and 700 students enrolled in accredited BS in Civil Engineering, BS in Construction Engineering & Management, MS in Civil Engineering, MS in Construction Management, MS in Environmental Engineering, ME in Civil & Environmental Engineering, and PhD in Civil Engineering degree programs. The Department organizes and actively encourages its students to participate in its international programs, including the faculty-led study abroad programs to Brazil, Czech Republic, Mexico, Peru, as well as the Dual Master Degrees Program in Smart Cities with Czech Technical University.

The civil engineering faculty members participate in research activities through the following centers affiliated with the Department: Center for Transportation Infrastructure Systems (CTIS); Center for Environmental Resource Management (CERM); NSF-Funded Engineering Research Center for Advancing Sustainability through Powered Infrastructure for Roadway Electrification (ASPIRE); USDOT-Funded Southern Plains Transportation Center (SPTC); USDOT-Funded Center for Efficient Mobility (CEM).

The Department of Civil, Environmental and Construction Engineering (CECE) at the University of Texas at El Paso (UTEP) invites applications for a Professor of Practice in Geotechnical Engineering beginning January 2027.

We seek an experienced geotechnical engineer with an M.S. or Ph.D. in civil engineering or a closely related field and at least 10 years of substantial professional experience. The successful candidate will connect professional geotechnical practice with graduate teaching and mentoring.

**Position Overview**

This position presents a unique opportunity to help shape the future of professional graduate education in geotechnical engineering. The successful candidate will play a leading role in the development and delivery of a practice-oriented online geotechnical engineering graduate program designed for working professionals. Responsibilities include developing and teaching in person and online graduate courses, integrating real-world engineering applications and case studies into the curriculum, mentoring students, and strengthening partnerships with industry and government agencies.

The department seeks a candidate who can bridge industry practice and academic instruction while helping position CECE as a regional and national leader in professional education for geotechnical engineering. The candidate should be able to translate field investigation, analysis, design, and construction experience into clear, rigorous instruction.

**Program Vision and Strategic Importance**

Geotechnical engineering is fundamental to the planning, design, and construction of infrastructure systems, including shallow and deep foundations, retaining structures, embankments, slopes, ground improvement systems, tunnels, and transportation infrastructure. Demand for engineers with advanced geotechnical expertise especially in the area of reliability-based design, continues to grow as federal, state, and local investments in infrastructure expand.

Many practicing engineers need graduate education compatible with full-time work. CECE aims to combine flexible course delivery with technically rigorous, practice-based instruction.

CECE's fully online Master of Science in Construction Management program provides an existing model for graduate instruction designed for working professionals. Building on this model, CECE envisions an online master's degree in geotechnical engineering. The Professor of Practice will help develop the curriculum, teach courses, and support the program if approved.

**This initiative aligns with the College of Engineering's strategic priorities of:**

Expanding professional graduate education;  
Strengthening engagement with industry partners;  
Supporting regional and national workforce development needs; and  
Advancing excellence in infrastructure engineering education.

**Responsibilities**

The successful candidate will be expected to:

* Develop and teach graduate courses in geotechnical engineering in person and online, including courses designed for working professionals;
* Help develop and assess the proposed online graduate curriculum in geotechnical engineering;
* Use geotechnical design projects, field investigation data, case studies, and current engineering practice in instruction;
* Mentor graduate students, including practicing engineers pursuing advanced education;
* Build partnerships with geotechnical consulting firms, contractors, transportation agencies, and other infrastructure stakeholders;
* Support student recruitment, professional outreach, and workforce development initiatives; and
* Evaluate course outcomes and contribute to program growth and the department's educational mission.

  
**Job Requirements:**

Applicants must possess:

* An M.S. or Ph.D. in civil engineering or a closely related field with graduate coursework or professional specialization in geotechnical engineering;
* At least 10 years of substantial professional experience in geotechnical engineering, including responsibility for geotechnical investigation, analysis, design, or construction support;
* Evidence of effective teaching, technical training, or mentoring, or clear potential to teach at the graduate level; and
* Ability to explain technical material clearly and collaborate with students, faculty, and professional partners.

Preference will be given to candidates with:

* Experience teaching at the university level or providing technical instruction to practicing engineers;
* Professional Engineer (PE) licensure, or eligibility and willingness to obtain licensure within three years of appointment;
* Experience leading geotechnical engineering work on transportation or other infrastructure projects;
* Experience in designing or teaching online courses;
* Established professional relationships with geotechnical consulting firms, public agencies, contractors, or infrastructure owners; and
* Experience developing graduate curricula or continuing education programs for practicing engineers.

  
**Additional Information:**

Appointment and Salary

This is a 9-month, non-tenure-track Professor of Practice appointment with a competitive salary commensurate with candidate's qualifications and experience.
