jobs.description:
Hiring Department
  
  
**UNIVERSITY of MISSOURI-KANSAS CITY**
**School of Dentistry**
**Department of Oral Pathology, Radiology & Medicine**
The UMKC School of Dentistry, founded in 1881, is the only public dental school in Missouri and Kansas, offering eight fully accredited programs. The School provides outstanding education, extensive hands-on clinical training, and real-world community service. Each year, students and faculty deliver care to more than 56,000 patients, while shaping the future of oral health through innovation in teaching, research, and clinical practice.
  
  
**UMKC is rated R1**
by the Carnegie Research Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. The UMKC Dental School is a partner of the UMKC Health Sciences District. The District strives to be a premier academic health district, engaging in cutting-edge biomedical research and entrepreneurship, delivering state-of-the-science health care, and educating the next generation of health care professionals. UMKC provides unique opportunities for research and health care collaboration across its Schools of: Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing & Health Studies, and Pharmacy as well as University Health physicians, regional health care institutions, and the University of Missouri System’s NextGen Data Science and Analytics Innovation Center.
  
  
Our School of Dentistry provides a primary oral health workforce pipeline for the region, with alumni comprising roughly half of all practicing dentists in the state. Serving Missouri, Kansas, and surrounding states, the School offers comprehensive predoctoral education alongside advanced education residency programs in General Dentistry, Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Periodontics, Orthodontics and Dentofacial Orthopedics, and Endodontics. About Us - UMKC School of Dentistry | UMKC
  
  
As part of the School, the Division of Dental Hygiene delivers the state’s only baccalaureate dental hygiene program, preparing graduates for clinical practice, public health, and community-based care. Dental Hygiene - Academic Programs - UMKC School of Dentistry | UMKC
  
  
**Job Description**
The UMKC School of Dentistry Section of Oral and Maxillofacial seeks to fill the position of Assistant/Associate Clinical Professor or Assistant/Associate Professor within the Oral Pathology, Radiology and Medicine Department. Position will be a ranked non-tenure track clinical faculty member or tenured/tenure-track faculty member commensurate with applicant qualifications.
  
  
with rank, track, and salary commensurate with qualifications and experience. Consideration for tenure requires the inclusion of evidence of sustained scholarly/research activity within the application materials.
  
  
The successful candidate will provide didactic and clinical instruction in oral and maxillofacial radiology for predoctoral dental (DDS) students and dental hygiene students. Responsibilities include teaching principles of radiology, radiographic interpretation, and supervising students in clinical settings to provide technique assessment, consultative services, and to ensure patient safety and compliance with accreditation standards. Additionally, this position provides graduate level didactic instruction for advanced education residency programs.
  
  
Opportunities for faculty practice participation (up to one day per week) may be available, consistent with School policy.
  
  
**Qualifications**
**Required Qualifications**
**DDS**
or
**DMD degree**
, or a foreign equivalent professional dental degree
  
  

* Completion of a CODA-accredited postgraduate training program in Oral and Maxillofacial Radiology (minimum 24 months in the U.S.)
* Eligibility for licensure in the State of Missouri, including successful completion of required clinical licensure examinations

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior teaching experience in predoctoral dental and/or dental hygiene programs

***To be eligible for a tenure-eligible faculty position, applicants must present:***

* an active research schema and demonstrated success or potential for success in obtaining external funding as a Principal Investigator or Co-Investigator
* prior experience or demonstrated ability to teach didactic and clinical courses in an advanced dental education program, and
* evidence of service to and/or participation in organizations which work to advance dental education and research

Anticipated Hiring Range
  
  
Rank and salary are commensurate with qualifications, experience and evidence of success in externally funded research. This is a 12-month, benefit-eligible, full-time (1.0) faculty appointment eligible for ranked promotion. Our academic schedules and workload provide for a positive work/life balance.
  
  
UMKC offers full benefits that start day one, paid time off, paid winter break, tuition discounts at all 4 UM System campuses for full-time employees and qualifying dependents, and continuing education benefits. Visit our Total Rewards page to learn more about our benefits package we offer to acknowledge our employees as the university's most important resource.
  
  
Application Materials
  
  
For consideration, you must apply online at
**Careers - Human Resources | University of Missouri-Kansas City**
, click Academic Positions/Prospective Employees (Job Opening ID
**61208**
).
  
  

* Complete the job application including Legal Name, US employment eligibility, questionnaire, and current contact information.
* Application materials

+ Letter of interest which provides your qualifications and experience for a ranked clinical faculty position or tenure-eligible faculty position

- For a tenure eligible position: description of research interests, any external funding, and goals

+ Curriculum vitae
+ Names, complete and current contact information for professional references

- These references can remain confidential for most of the application process.

Please combine all application materials into one PDF or Microsoft Word document and upload as your resume attachments. Limit document name to 50 characters and do not include any special characters (e.g., /, &, %, etc.).
  
  

* If you are experiencing technical problems during application, please email umpshrsupport@umsystem.edu .
* For questions and correspondence about the position, please contact umkcfacultysearch@umkc.edu including the Job Identification number including job identification number 61208.
* Reasonable accommodations may be requested during the application and recruitment process. If you need an accommodation, please contact the Office of Equity and Title IX at (816) 235-6910.

Official higher education transcripts will be required for candidates advancing as finalists. We will contact references for finalists; candidates will receive prior notification if references will be contacted. Selected candidate will be required to pass a criminal background check prior to employment.
  
  
**Handling of Application Materials**
After initial review by the committee all uploaded materials may be shared with all faculty in the prospective home department and faculty in all departments involved.
  
  
Application Deadline
  
  
Review of applications begins upon receipt; the position remains open until a qualified candidate is hired.
  
  
Sponsorship Information
  
  
Employment visa sponsorship may be available for candidates currently in the United States in H-1B status or other work-authorized status.
  
  
Other Information
  
  
**UMKC**
is a public, urban, research university with more than 16,000 undergraduate, graduate, and professional students. It is part of the larger University of Missouri System. Our university is committed to being a model urban university that is recognized for our partnerships with multifarious communities to effectively foster a healthy, safe, more economically secure, and socially just quality of life. About - Home Suite | UMKC

**A City on the Rise:**
Big City Life and Midwest Charm, Kansas City offers the best of both worlds - a vibrant, urban community with midwestern appeal and an affordable cost of living. The university is located in a Kansas City metropolitan area that is among the most entrepreneurial cities in America with a population of more than 2.4 million. Our UMKC campuses are centered in the hubs of business activity, cultural arts, (some great barbeque and ethnic cuisine!) and health science research engagement for both the Volker and Health Sciences campuses. Our community boasts championship professional athletic teams, NASCAR racing, a new international airport and a rich history of music and performing arts. Our beautiful state provides rivers, lakes, biking/hiking trails and mountains for outdoor enthusiasts all within an easy drive.
  
  
Visit Kansas City: Find Events, Things to Do & More
  
  
Benefit Eligibility
  
  
This position is eligible for University benefits. As part of your total compensation, the University offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental and vision plans, retirement, and educational fee discounts for all four UM System campuses. For additional information on University benefits, please visit the Faculty & Staff Benefits website at https://www.umsystem.edu/departments-staff/human-resources/benefits-retirement

The University of Missouri is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
  
  
To request ADA accommodations, please call the Office of Equity & Title IX at 816-235-6910.

The Department of Communication Studies in the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB) invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor in Media Studies to begin August 2027. Areas of specialization may include Digital Media, Advertising, Visual Storytelling, Interactive Digital Narrative, and related emerging media fields. Versatility in teaching media courses is desirable, as the successful candidate will support multiple concentrations within the media curriculum. Instruction may include both in-person and online delivery formats.

Our 19 departments — home to over 300 full-time faculty and more than 58 baccalaureate, master’s, and doctoral degrees — make us the largest academic entity in the UAB academic enterprise. **Department**
College of Medicine, COM Residency Program Administration
  
  
**Responsibilities**
The Program Director oversees the Internal Medicine Residency Program (“IM Program” or “Program”) under the guidance of the Designated Institutional Official (DIO). The Program Director handles the general management, curriculum development, hiring, and teaching and mentoring of the Program. The Program Director sets the strategic vision of the Program and ensures its standards, quality, and reputation. The Program Director is expected to support the collaboration of the IM Program with physician practices and hospital clinical services in a way that improves value and quality, and that fosters a positive environment for professional practice and medical education. The Program Director will also work in collaboration with the program leadership to ensure outstanding educational offerings within Ascension Sacred Heart Bay Hospital.
  
  

* Clinical Teaching and Supervision of Residents
* Core Program Clinical Teaching
* Clinical Practice in Internal Medicine or applicable Subspecialty
* General Administration
* Graduate Medical Education (GME) Committees/Meetings
* GME Lecturing/Teaching Conferences
* GME Recruiting/Interviewing
* GME Research/Scholarly Activity
* Resident Evaluation/Monitoring
* Program Evaluation

* Doctoral degree from an accredited institution or the highest degree appropriate in the field of specialization with a demonstrated record of achievement in teaching, academic research, and service.
* Valid FL medical license, or licensed in another state with the ability to obtain FL licensure.
* Must be board certified in Internal Medicine by the American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM).
* Must have a minimum of three years of faculty and administrative experience in an ACGME accredited internal medicine residency program.

* The 47-million-dollar renovation of Bay Medical after Hurricane Michael is in process and aims to create a facility with 200 private rooms. The improvements include major upgrades to information technology and creation of new space for physician offices and other services, including the laboratory, imaging and pharmacy.
* Bay offers an accredited Stroke Center, a Level II Trauma Center, which provides 24-hour emergency care for life-threatening injuries and illnesses, and emergency services located at the main hospital as well as a freestanding emergency center on Panama City Beach.

Helpful
  
  

* The successful candidate will have the opportunity to shape the program in their vision and recruit core faculty.
* Candidates with recent scholarly activity such as peer reviewed funding, publication of original research or review articles in peer-reviewed journals, chapters in textbooks, publication or presentation of case reports or clinical series at scientific society meetings, or participation in national committees or educational organizations are highly encouraged to apply.

Contact Info
  
  
Jessee Graham: jjgraham@fsu.edu

One of the nation's elite research universities, Florida State University preserves, expands, and disseminates knowledge in the sciences, technology, arts, humanities, and professions, while embracing a philosophy of learning strongly rooted in the traditions of the liberal arts and critical thinking. Founded in 1851, Florida State University is the oldest continuous site of higher education in Florida. FSU is a community steeped in tradition that fosters research and encourages creativity. At FSU, there’s the excitement of being part of a vibrant academic and professional community, surrounded by people whose ideas are shaping tomorrow’s news!
  
  
Learn more about our university and campuses.

jobs.title: Full-Time Clinical Faculty: School of Nursing
jobs.description:
**Overview**
Quinnipiac University's School of Nursing invites applicants who are dynamic educators and clinicians for a full-time, 12-month clinical track faculty position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor.
  
  
We are particularly interested in doctorally-prepared candidates with clinical practice and teaching experiences teaching across the lifespan with prelicensure BSN students. The position supports the School’s competency-based curriculum aligned with the AACN 2026 Essentials, emphasizing learner-centered approaches, clinical judgment, and integration of evidence-based practice. Faculty members in the School of Nursing contribute to the development of practice ready nurses through innovative teaching strategies and mentoring.
  
  
Successful candidates will have experience teaching concepts such as person-centered care, population health, interprofessional practice, scholarship and inquiry, and informatics and healthcare technology with patients across the lifespan. Successful candidates are also able to contribute to the university’s strategic initiatives including empowering academic success, cultivating a community of learners, leading through innovation, designing distinctive experiences, redefining health and human potential, and extending our partnership.
  
  
**About The School/Program**
The Quinnipiac University (QU) School of Nursing has been educating nurses for more than 50 years. Our mission is to develop exceptional, practice-ready nurses as leaders in science-based, holistic care through innovation and inclusive education. The School of Nursing was recently designated as a National League for Nursing (NLN) Center of Excellence. The School of Nursing’s strategic priorities are aligned with innovative programs, student success, thriving community, and sustainable resources. The School of Nursing serves approximately 1200 graduate and undergraduate students. We offer CCNE accredited programs leading to BSN, MSN, and DNP degrees that prepare graduates for successful careers in hospitals, clinics, schools, communities, and many other settings. The QU School of Nursing partners with Hartford HealthCare (HHC) with a New Careers in Nursing (NCN) work-compatible program for mid-career professionals interested in a future nursing career. As one of 17 schools in the nation with holistically endorsed programs, we emphasize the social, emotional, spiritual, and psychological aspects of care, as well as the physical, throughout our nursing curriculum.
  
  
School of Nursing graduates become leaders at each level of their careers and facilitate positive changes within healthcare. Faculty and staff work with colleagues in our Center for Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences and all schools across campus to create innovative interprofessional educational experiences that prepare students for today's health care challenges. The Center is located at our North Haven, CT campus and encompasses 325,000 square feet designed for collaborative learning including 48 pro-section stations, 16 standardized patient rooms, an exceptional health sciences library, 7 high-fidelity simulation rooms including 2 ORs and a PACU, health assessment and skills labs, advanced diagnostic imaging equipment and classrooms outfitted with the latest technology. The NCN Program is offered at the Center for Education, Simulation and Innovation (CESI) at Hartford HealthCare.
  
  
**Education**
We are a highly collaborative and supportive community that is committed to high quality educational experience, advancing diversity in all areas. Successful candidates will share the School of Nursing values of belonging, compassion, collaboration, curiosity, and integrity. The School provides faculty members with:
  
  

* A structured orientation and mentoring
* An assigned faculty affiliate
* Regular workshops by Quinnipiac Innovations in Learning and Teaching (QILT)
* Opportunities to work with nationally recognized faculty and staff
* Generous support for conference attendance and professional development
* Support with grant applications for faculty research or curricular innovations
* A culture of community, teamwork, and professionalism
* A climate that values diversity and inclusion
* Values of belonging, collaboration, compassion, curiosity and integrity

Faculty are provided with one day a week as a practice and/or scholarship day. On-ground in person presence is expected on the campus 3 days per week.
  
  
**About Quinnipiac**
Quinnipiac University is a private, coeducational institution located 90 minutes north of New York City and two hours from Boston. The university currently has an enrollment of 9,700 students in more than 100-degree programs through its Schools of Business, Communications, Computing & Engineering, Education, Health Sciences, Law, Medicine, Nursing and the College of Arts & Sciences. Our 20 Division I teams have achieved remarkable success, boasting national and conference titles — including a 2023 NCAA national championship win in men’s ice hockey, a trip to the Sweet 16 for our women's basketball team and NCAA Tournament appearances by many of our programs. The Quinnipiac University Poll is nationally recognized as a leader in public opinion research, and the university is consistently recognized by U.S. News & World Report and Princeton Review. The Wall Street Journal ranked Quinnipiac #51 among the best colleges in the nation, and second in Connecticut, for our exceptional graduation rate, salary impact, learning facilities, career preparation and learning opportunities.
  
  
The university is in the midst of program expansion and renewal for both traditional and adult learners, the development of innovative strategic partnerships, and recently opened South Quad with three state-of-the-art buildings.
  
  
As Quinnipiac grows, the university remains guided by the core values that define our community and shapes the experience of every student and employee.
  
  

* We are fiercely committed to ensuring every Bobcat thrives. We are a lifelong partner for every learner.
* We passionately care about our community. Everyone should feel welcome and valued.
* We boldly shape our university's future. We will forge a path of impact together.

These values are the foundation of who we are and reflect the Quinnipiac spirit found across our campuses. For more information, please visit qu.edu. Connect with Quinnipiac on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and X.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Teaching intensive, clinical track nursing faculty position, with primary responsibility teaching in the New Careers in Nursing (NCN) work compatible program for mid-career professionals transitioning into nursing at the Center for Education, Simulation and Innovation (CESI) at Hartford HealthCare in Hartford, CT; faculty will also have teaching responsibilities on the North Haven campus
* Collaborate with colleagues to ensure high-quality programs that demonstrate academic excellence and success
* Participate in competency-based curriculum development, assessment, and continuous quality improvement aligned with the AACN 2026 Essentials
* Advise and mentor students to support academic success and professional growth
* Contribute to School and University service, including committee participation and professional engagement within the community
* Engage in scholarly activities and maintain currency in nursing practice and education
* Participate in faculty development
* Engage in the School of Nursing’s strategic plan
* Actively participate in the School of Nursing community

**Education Requirements**

* Required: unencumbered RN license in Connecticut
* Required: doctoral degree (PhD, EdD, DNP) in nursing or related field

**Qualifications**

* Recent clinical practice experience
* Experience with competency-based education and curriculum development
* Evidence of effective teaching
* Service to profession or community
* Commitment to contribute to the excellence of the academic community

**To Apply**
**Special Instructions to Applicants:**
Applications must be submitted electronically and include a resume, a cover letter detailing how your experience aligns with the position requirements, demonstrated commitment to intentional leadership that values individuals of all backgrounds and experiences, and contact information for three references.
  
  
We offer a comprehensive benefits package for full-time faculty and staff which includes tuition remission and a culture that is inclusive and driven by excellence.
  
  
**Quinnipiac University is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from individuals of all backgrounds and experiences. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and respectful community.**

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor - Finance
jobs.description:
**Assistant/Associate Professor - Finance**

The Department of Business and Communication and the Finance program at Briar Cliff University seek to fill an Assistant or Associate Professor of Finance position to begin in Spring 2027 (preferred) or Fall 2027. This is a 9-month, tenure-eligible position focused on advancing knowledge through teaching, professional development, and service within the university community.

The successful candidate will teach courses in beginning and advanced finance, general business, and other courses that serve the University’s general education curriculum, known as the Core Values Curriculum. The typical faculty teaching load is 24 credits over the normal academic year. Collaboration with colleagues across departments and programs, and participation in curriculum development are essential to ensure the academic program remains current and rigorous. Additionally, faculty engage in professional development, complete institutional and departmental service, and advise students regarding experiential learning opportunities in addition to their coursework, supporting their professional growth and contributing to the broader educational mission.

The successful candidate should have at minimum a Masters in Finance or related field, with additional licensure; a terminal degree in finance or related field is preferred. The successful candidate should have demonstrated excellence in teaching at the university level, a strong record of successfully advising and mentoring students, interest in maintaining their own intellectual creativity, and an ability to contribute to curriculum development and academic service.

Founded in 1930 and rooted in the Catholic Franciscan tradition, Briar Cliff University is a vibrant, values-based community dedicated to academic excellence and personal growth. Located on the scenic Loess Hills overlooking the Missouri River, "The Cliff" maintains a tight-knit learning environment with an institutional 13:1 student-to-faculty ratio. Academically, the university offers over 30 undergraduate programs and several respected graduate degrees, including regionally recognized programs in Nursing, Physical Therapy, and Sport Management. Our commitment to the student-athlete experience is equally robust; as members of the NAIA and Great Plains Athletic Conference, the Briar Cliff Chargers have earned 19 conference championships and were recently honored as an NAIA Champions of Character Gold Level Institution.

A city of 85,000 stretching across the corners of Iowa, South Dakota, and Nebraska (referred to as “Siouxland”), Sioux City is nestled along the Sioux River approximately 80 miles from both Omaha, NE, and Sioux Falls, SD. The city offers a vibrant, friendly community with a cost of living that is attractive for families and individuals alike. Sioux City possesses a bustling riverfront, a lively downtown arts and entertainment scene, numerous parks, and rich cultural opportunities, combining small-town charm with the amenities of a larger metropolitan area. As a regional hub for business and culture, the city features over 50 parks, the historic Orpheum Theatre, Tyson Events Center, and a mix of national retailers and award-winning local favorites. Sioux City has twice been named an “All-America City,” highlighting its strong community and significant quality of life.

Interested candidates should visit the Briar Cliff University employment website for more information and to apply. Candidates should submit:

* A letter of interest describing the alignment of the candidate's qualifications with the position requirements
* Current curriculum vita
* A statement of teaching philosophy that addresses ways in which the candidate creates and sustains a culture of belonging, fairness and appreciation for different perspectives in the classroom
* Graduate and undergraduate transcripts (unofficial copies are fine at this point)
* Contact information (only) for three professional references

For full consideration, candidates should submit their applications no later than August 31, although review of applications will continue until the position is filled. Any final offer is contingent on a successful background check. If you have any questions about this position, contact Provost@briarcliff.edu. A competitive salary is commensurate with teaching experience and academic credentials. This position is subject to final budget approval.

==============================================================

### **Position Overview**

**School / Campus / College:** College of Engineering

**Organization:** Mechanical Engineering

**Title:** Assistant Professor, Tenure Track - Mechanical Engineering

### **Position Details**

#### **Position Description**

The Department of Mechanical Engineering within the College of Engineering at the University of Washington invites applications for two faculty positions at the rank of Assistant Professor, Tenure Track, with an anticipated start date of September 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in research, teaching, and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community. The successful candidates will join our faculty as tenure-track Assistant Professor, on a full-time basis for a nine-month academic appointment. Initial appointment is on a 3-year term, renewable while on the tenure-track, which is traditionally 6 years. Starting date is expected on September 2027, but an earlier or later starting date can be arranged.

The base salary range for this position will be $12,000-$17,900 per month, commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination.

We seek candidates in any area of Mechanical Engineering. The Department of Mechanical Engineering has internationally recognized strengths in additive and advanced manufacturing, including composite materials manufacturing, robotics, biomechanics and biomedical engineering sciences, physics-based machine learning and artificial intelligence modeling and controls, energy storage and electrification, renewable energy and thermal and fluid sciences. Successful candidates will be expected to develop a strong research program in one or many of the areas of impact for which Mechanical Engineering is well-known. Candidates whose research complements or expands these areas are encouraged to apply.

The successful candidates will be expected to develop an internationally recognized extramurally funded research program and to provide innovative, high-quality teaching. The candidates will also be expected to contribute to a learning environment that welcomes and values all lived experiences and points of view, collaborate with members of the department, as well as other researchers within the University and affiliated institutions, participate in the department’s teaching in the Bachelor’s, Master’s and PhD programs, and contribute to the mentoring and training of students in the department’s graduate programs. They will be expected to propose and implement new initiatives in the undergraduate curriculum, and graduate courses in their areas of expertise, as well as activities to involve students from all backgrounds in research. In addition, all University of Washington faculty are expected to engage in teaching, research, and service.

The Mechanical Engineering department’s research and teaching portfolio covers all aspects in the broad field of mechanical engineering. The department currently has 45 tenured, tenure track, research and teaching faculty, over 700 undergraduates, 250 Master’s students, 160 PhD students and 30 postdoctoral researchers, and continues to grow. More information about the ME department is available at http://www.me.washington.edu.

The University of Washington, located in Seattle, Washington, the heart of the high-tech Pacific Northwest, is one of the world’s leading universities, ranking No. 12 in Best Global Universities in 2026 by U.S. News & World Report (https://www.usnews.com/education/best-global-universities/rankings). The College of Engineering and the ME Department foster a highly collegial and collaborative culture. The University of Washington is committed to fostering an inclusive, respectful and welcoming community for all.

#### **Qualifications**

Applicants for this position must meet the following minimum qualifications:

* A Ph.D. (or foreign equivalent) degree in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related discipline by the date of appointment.
* Demonstrated potential for excellence in scholarly research and teaching as demonstrated by publications, presentations, teaching evaluations, or other comparable evidence.
* Ability to develop an internationally recognized research program and contribute effectively to undergraduate and graduate education. Evidence may include a record of scholarly publications, competitive research funding, invited presentations, and professional recognition, as well as successful teaching, student mentoring, graduate supervision, and curriculum development.

#### **Instructions**

To ensure full consideration of your application, please submit all materials no later than **December 15, 2026**. Priority will be given to those applications received by December 15, 2026. Applications will only be accepted via Interfolio: https://apply.interfolio.com/190130. The position will remain open until filled. Additional questions may be addressed to MEChair@uw.edu.

Applications should include the following materials:

* a cover letter detailing interest in the position, relevant qualifications, and experience;
* a curriculum vitae;
* a statement on research plans;
* a statement on educational experience and teaching philosophy;
* names and contact information for at least three references prepared to provide letters of recommendation upon request; and
* copies of the applicant's three most significant publications.

Applicants should articulate how their past experiences and/or future plans in research, teaching, mentoring, and service promote a sense of belonging and foster a welcoming and inclusive environment.

jobs.description:
**Position Announcement**
-------------------------

The Culinary Arts Institute (www.uvu.edu/culinary/) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position to begin January 2027.
  
  
The culinary arts faculty member develops and teaches a wide range of undergraduate courses. These courses may include, but are not limited to, culinary skill development, baking skill development, advanced pastry, and restaurant management to meet the changing needs of the culinary arts industry. The faculty member is involved in catering operations on and off campus. The faculty member engages in scholarship and creative works activities that contribute to the mission of the university, department, and profession. In addition, the faculty member provides service at the department, college, and university levels.
  
  
Utah Valley University places a strong emphasis on teaching. Faculty members are expected to develop a learning environment and activities that help students achieve their learning objectives. UVU encourages applicants with a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and expertise to apply.
  
  
The Culinary Arts Institute offers an AAS Culinary Arts degree. The Culinary Arts program is accredited through the American Culinary Federation.
  
  
By joining our team, you'll have the opportunity to influence and guide the minds of future chefs. The satisfaction of knowing that you're playing a vital role in developing future culinary professionals is one of the many rewards of this position. Moreover, you'll have access to cutting-edge resources and a collaborative community of experts dedicated to staying at the forefront of the culinary industry. You will guide the students in the techniques of not only baking and cooking, but also catering aspects as well. The UVU Culinary Arts Institute participates in the production and serving of many catering events, including the Presidential Scholarship Ball, Christmas events for local businesses, and our own Gala that earns funds to help our students and the program. Utah Valley University offers a comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance and retirement contributions.

* Certified or certifiable in 1 year as a Certified Executive Pastry Chef, Certified Executive Chef, Certified Chef d’ Cuisine, or Certified Culinary Educator through the American Culinary Federation's certification guidelines.

Job Title: Assistant/Associate Professor in Biomedical Robotics - Engineering (Indianapolis)

City: Indianapolis

**Job Summary**
---------------

Purdue University College of Engineering invites applications for **multiple tenured/tenure track positions at the Assistant or Associate Professor level in biomedical-related robotics** to strengthen its growing leadership at the intersection of robotics, engineering, and human health in our Indianapolis location. The candidate’s research focus should target areas where robotics, controls and autonomy impact the biomedical, medicine, and heath fields such as surgical robotics, active prostheses, self-driving labs for diagnostics, surgery and therapies, or rehabilitative systems. Tenured or tenure-track positions are expected to collaborate with an interdisciplinary group spanning Biomedical Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Industrial Engineering, and/or Mechanical Engineering with active degree programs based in Indianapolis. Successful candidates must hold a Ph.D. degree in **Biomedical Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Computer Science** or a related discipline by the employment start date. Early-career applicants should show evidence of initiating independent research, while mid-career applicants should demonstrate a sustained record of independent research within academic or industrial organizations, and contributions to education and/or mentoring. The successful candidate will conduct original research, advise graduate students, teach undergraduate and graduate level courses, and perform service at the School, College, and University levels. The position would also enhance Purdue’s ability to attract major federal and industry-sponsored research, train students in a rapidly expanding field, and translate fundamental advances in robotics into technologies that address important biomedical and healthcare challenges. Applicants interested in a position in any of Purdue’s engineering schools are welcome to apply.

**College of Engineering**
--------------------------

Purdue Engineering is renowned for top-notch faculty and students, unique research facilities and innovations, and a culture of collegiality and persistent pursuit of preeminence. As one of the top ranked and largest engineering colleges in the nation, we are the first among U.S. engineering colleges in annual graduates and market demand, and have 8 degree programs ranked in the top 10 nationally. Purdue Engineering is a top-ranked college for patents and translation of our research activities to practice in the state, nation, and world. More than 70 Purdue Engineering faculty and alumni are National Academy of Engineering members, and we look to continue bringing outstanding faculty to campus, remaining the leader in affordable excellence at scale by guiding strategic growth through investment in people, exciting initiatives , and facilities .

Req Id: 44333

Job Title: Assistant/Associate Professor in Electrical and Computer Engineering (Indianapolis)

City: Indianapolis

**Job Summary**
---------------

Purdue has begun a major growth effort at our new location in Indianapolis—a dynamic, affordable city offering a vibrant urban lifestyle, rich cultural scene, and strong connections to industry and healthcare innovation. As part of this initiative, the **Elmore Family School of Electrical and Computer Engineering** at Purdue University invites applications for a tenure-track/tenured Assistant/Associate Professor to be **based in Indianapolis** . Purdue University seeks to attract exceptional candidates in Electrical and Computer Engineering. Particular areas of interest include **Autonomy and Controls, Software Engineering and Systems, and Computer Vision** , but exceptional candidates in other areas, especially those who have application interests in medicine and healthcare, are welcome. Successful candidates must hold a Ph.D. degree in **Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science** , or a related discipline by the start of employment. Early-career applicants should show evidence of initiating independent research, while mid-career applicants should demonstrate a sustained record of independent research within academic or industrial organizations, and contributions to education and/or mentoring. The successful candidate will conduct original research, advise graduate students, teach undergraduate and graduate-level courses, and perform service at the School, College, and University levels.

**School and College**
----------------------

The Elmore Family School of Electrical and Computer Engineering is the largest academic unit at Purdue University and one of the largest in the nation with more than 130 faculty members (7 NAE members, more than 40 Fellows in multiple societies), 2,500 undergraduate students (sophomores-seniors), and 1,700 graduate students. In Indianapolis, ECE is home to the **Transportation and Autonomous Systems Institute (TASI)** which collaborates closely with industry partners in developing and testing cutting-edge vehicle autonomy systems, as well as the newly-launched **Intelligent Software & Systems Center** , which is re-envisioning the software lifecycle in the age of agentic AI and the impact on AI-native systems. These institutions will provide a strong foundation to new faculty joining in Indianapolis. ECE’s undergraduate programs in Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering are ranked 10th and 9th, respectively. Its graduate programs are ranked 8th and 9th. And its online MS in ECE is ranked 1st in the nation.

  

Faculty in ECE collaborate closely with industry. The Purdue West Lafayette–Indianapolis Hard Tech Corridor is strategically established to drive transformative industry engagement across a 60-mile innovation corridor, unified by a seamlessly integrated campus that serves as a catalyst for economic growth, technological advancement, and global leadership in hard tech development.

  

The School is an integral part of Purdue Engineering. Purdue Engineering is renowned for top-notch faculty and students, unique research facilities and innovations, and a culture of collegiality and persistent pursuit of preeminence. As one of the top ranked and largest engineering colleges in the nation, we are the first among U.S. engineering colleges in annual graduates and market demand, and have 8 degree programs ranked in the top 10 nationally. Purdue Engineering is a top-ranked college for patents and translation of our research activities to practice in the state, nation, and world. More than 70 Purdue Engineering faculty and alumni are National Academy of Engineering members, and we look to continue bringing outstanding faculty to campus, remaining the leader in affordable excellence at scale by guiding strategic growth through investment in people, exciting initiatives , and facilities .

jobs.description:
Req Id: 44262

Job Title: Assistant Professor, Artificial Intelligence for Agriculture/Forestry/Natural Systems

City: West Lafayette

**Job Summary**
---------------

The Purdue University College of Agriculture seeks applicants for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position. This is a full-time (9-months) position with an appointment in research and teaching. The candidate for this position could have a home department in Agronomy, Agricultural & Biological Engineering and/or Forestry & Natural Resources. Within the context of natural, forestry, and/or cropping systems, we are looking for candidates with experience and potential integration of two or more of the following topic areas:

* artificial intelligence (AI) including machine learning (ML), deep learning, knowledge-guided AI, and/or translational applied AI models
* digital agriculture including crop modeling and/or digital twins of assorted scales
* remote-, proximal- and near-proximal- sensing, and/or Internet of Things (IoT)
* data science, geo-spatial analysis, GeoAI, and/or integration of data pipelines
* agroecosystem (crop-soil-environmental) and/or ecosystem modeling
* applications of robotics and/or autonomous systems

  

Applications of the work could relate to productivity improvement, resource optimization, systems efficiency, and/or operational strategies and logistics. We expect the candidate to build a nationally and internationally recognized research program that advances discovery and innovation across these areas at the intersection of agricultural, environmental, and data sciences. Demonstrated experience and interest in working with multi-disciplinary teams is beneficial. The selected candidate will develop and teach undergraduate and/or graduate level courses. Course modality is generally in person. The potential may exist for teaching online/distance courses during the academic year.

**The College**
---------------

The College of Agriculture is one of the world’s leading colleges of agricultural, food, life, and natural resource sciences. The College is ranked third in the U.S. and sixth in the world in the 2026 QS World University Rankings. The College is deeply committed to the three land-grant missions (teaching, research, and extension), to international activities and perspectives that span all missions, and to excellence in all we do. The College has 10 academic departments, 294 faculty, 2842 undergraduate students, and 694 graduate students.

**Qualifications**
------------------

Applicants must possess a Ph.D. degree in forestry and natural resources, agronomy, soil science, agricultural and biological engineering, or a related discipline at the start of appointment. A record of research excellence and productivity commensurate with rank is required as well as demonstrated record or potential of interdisciplinary collaboration and impactful scholarship. Applicants must have demonstrated commitment to teaching and student mentorship. Ideal qualifications would include cross-discipline training among degrees earned with at least one degree in an agricultural or natural resources field.

**Application Process**
-----------------------

Interested applicants must submit a cover letter, CV, research statement, teaching statement, and contact information for at least three references. Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Applications should be submitted at: https://careers.purdue.edu/job/Assistant-Professor%2C-Artificial-Intelligence-for-AgricultureForestryNatural-Systems/44262-en\_US/ . Application materials must be combined into a single pdf and submitted electronically in the CV field on the application site. Contact Ignacio Ciampitti ( iciampit@purdue.edu ) if questions. A background check is required for employment in this position.

  

Purdue University is an equal opportunity/equal access university.

jobs.description:
The mission of the University of St. Augustine for Health Sciences is the development of professional health care practitioners through innovation, individualized, and quality classroom, clinical, and distance education.
  
  
**General Summary**
The University of St. Augustine for Health Sciences (USAHS) seeks a dynamic, innovative faculty member for a full-time Core Faculty position in the nursing programs. Responsibilities will include teaching activities primarily in one or more of the following: Master of Science in Nursing program, the Family Nurse Practice role specialty courses, Psych Mental Health specialty courses and the Doctor of Nurse Practice program.
  
  
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**
**Teaching**

* Effectively and proficiently using online technology and resources including providing informed feedback and critique in a thoughtful, well-written and timely manner.
* Optimizing the online environment to be conducive to student learning by developing creative, challenging, and evidence-based learning opportunities.
* Uses learning assessment information to improve teaching and curriculum; participates in quality improvement initiatives to meet program and institutional goals.
* Adheres to all USAHS faculty expectations, which are clearly set forth to the faculty member at the start of his/her employment with the University.
* Upholds the expectations of masters/doctoral level work with respect to the program and course learning outcomes.
* Participates in a culture of assessment of academic integrity, effectiveness and doctoral quality teaching and learning.
* Teaches three to four assigned courses/sections per trimester in accordance with the faculty expectations and as outlined in the USAHS employee handbook.
* Effectively supervises scholarly projects and practicum experiences
* Participate in residency experiences as assigned (may require travel).

**Scholarship**

* Establishes and implements an approved scholarship plan/faculty development plan as required by accreditation and university standards.
* Stays current with clinical practice and evidence that support content area expertise, professional growth, and professional certification and licensure requirements.
* Disseminates scholarly work consistent with University policies and accreditation expectations.
* Demonstrates commitment to scholarly advancement through research, written artifacts, scholarly inquiry and presentations at state, national and international professional events (minimum one per year).

**Service**

* Serves on programmatic and university committees as assigned.
* Actively participates in his/her professional association(s).
* Serves as university liaison in community and/or professional activities.
* Uses release time that enhances the program (e.g., clinical practice, consultation, advanced degree attainment, research, service) as approved by the program director.
* Participates in university governance, curriculum planning, and functions to support development and growth of the institution.
* Participates in a minimum of two to three committees (depending on requirements) and attends all university functions as assigned.

**Administration: supports efficient and consistent practices across all programs**

* Performs course coordinator and lead instructor roles as assigned; works collaboratively with members of the team.
* Advises students on academic, professional and/or personal issues while providing referrals when appropriate.
* Provides other administrative duties as assigned.
* Completes annual self-evaluation of faculty performance and sets goals for the next year in collaboration with the program director and is actively engaged in faculty development opportunities to meet performance goals.

**Professionalism: displays the behaviors of a professional academician and follows expected discipline specific Code of Ethics**

* Promotes professionalism by modeling and encouraging such behaviors inside and outside the classroom setting.
* Supports and exemplifies the University’s core values.
* Actively engages in interprofessional collaboration activities.
* Upholds and enforces student and faculty handbook policies and University policies/procedures.

**Other Responsibilities As Assigned By The Program Director**
**BUSINESS COMPETENCIES**
To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies:
  
  

* Committed to Mission and Values - Has a clear understanding of institution’s mission and values. Has a passion for facilitating learning and for enabling students to navigate their own learning journey.
* Contribute Knowledge to the Discipline - Compelled by the opportunity to contribute through research, scholarship professional practice or creativity.
* Accountable -Takes personal responsibility for own goals and outcomes to ensure student success. Establishes clear expectations, follows through on commitments to students and holds them accountable for assignments and performance
* Collaborative - Works cooperatively with others across the institution and beyond, including the community and through partnerships. Represents own interests while being inclusive and fair to others.
* Communicates Effectively - Adapts oral and written communication approach and style to the audience and based on the message. Also listens attentively to others.
* Drives Engagement - Makes students feel welcome, understood and valued. Creates a learning environment that is compelling, challenging and productive.
* Academic Discipline Expertise - Has sufficient credentials, industry expertise and/or experience in the discipline to teach according to the standards and qualifications required.
* Education Design - Designs learning experiences closely linked to learning outcomes including lesson planning, design of project, work integrated, group learning experiences, or interactive learning objects. Has depth of expertise in pedagogy, andragogy and overall learning effectiveness.
* Teaching Delivery/Learning Facilitation Skills - Manages small, large, blended, hybrid and/or online classrooms, monitoring and ensuring participation, managing oneï¿½s own and studentsï¿½ time and attention effectively.

**Additional Competencies**

* Utilizes an engaged, proactive and responsive style in communicating with students and colleagues as well as participation in research and university service.
* Demonstrates the ability to encourage critical thinking, helping students see multiple viewpoints, encouraging them along a path of continual improvement, and keeps up to date with developments in teaching and learning.
* Responds in a constructive, detailed and timely manner. Provides open-minded and receptive responses to student inquiry.
* Sets expectations with students about assignments and evaluates work products against stated expectations. Assesses students' critical thinking skills and writing skills in addition to content mastery.
* Utilizes clarity and specificity about how students' scholarly work will be evaluated. Informs students of their academic progress in meeting course expectations by regularly providing grades and feedback. Provides timely and substantive feedback in the gradebook and other appropriate places. Grades assignments consistently using rubrics.
* Adheres to the highest ethical standards and scholarly codes in practicing academic freedom. Respects the privacy of students and protecting the intellectual property of others that might be infringed upon through copyright violation or plagiarism.
* Effectively directs instruction and mentoring roles toward preparing students as agents of social change.
* Integrates various forms of scholarship into professional activities enabling creation of create new knowledge through research, interpretation of knowledge across disciplines, examination of teaching models to achieve optimal learning, and progress toward solution of problems within the profession and across society.
* Maintains an inter-professional focus, demonstrating respect and collaboration for all members of the healthcare team.
* Considers cultural and ethical aspects of teaching, learning and administrative duties.
* Supports a healthy organization by developing trust, mutual respect and honesty during all interactions.
* Exhibits excellent organization and time management skills.
* Follows through on commitments and is accountable for actions and outcomes.
* Maintains a working knowledge of educational theory and methodology.
* Establishes and maintains computer literacy including all features of Microsoft Office.

**LICENSING / CERTIFICATION**
Faculty members must be appropriately credentialed, possess an earned degree from an accredited institution, and expected to be licensed as a Registered Nurse and/or Advanced Practice Registered Nurse (if applicable). Faculty members must maintain their license(s) and any appropriate certifications in order to continue to teach at University of Saint Augustine for Health Sciences. Faculty members may be asked to seek additional state licenses if required. Faculty members are also expected to maintain currency with nursing practice and education by reviewing articles, journals, and presentations. If participating in research, the Faculty member may publish and acknowledge University of Saint Augustine for Health Sciences.
  
  
**TRAVEL**
Some travel may be required for residencies, faculty meetings or immersions.
  
  
**EDUCATION And/or EXPERIENCE**

* A terminal degree in nursing (PhD or DNP)
* Active and unencumbered RN license in home state and eligible for licensure in all 50 states
* Current national certification as a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP)
* APRN license in home state as well as states where students live, if required.
* A significant record of intellectual and professional contributions to the field of nursing, including experience in the practice of education and nursing.
* Teaching experience is required; teaching at doctoral level of the program is preferred. Rank is determined at point of hire based on years of teaching experience, publications, scholarship, and committee work.
* Experience in teaching advanced practice nursing, especially in PMHNP role, is required if assigned to PMHNP coursework.
* Experience with distance learning preferred.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**
Work is performed primarily in a standard office environment but may involve exposure to moderate noise levels. Work involves operation of personal computer equipment for six to eight hours daily and includes physical demands associated with a traditional office setting, e.g., walking, standing, communicating, and other physical functions as necessary.
  
  
Hiring ranges:
  
  

* Affiliated/Instructor rank: $59,758 - $100,394
* Assistant Professor rank: $68,722 – $115,400
* Associate Professor rank: $79,030 - $132,710
* Professor rank: $88,923 - $152,617

Join the dynamic and growing Nurse Anesthesia Program at Midwestern University as it expands to our Downers Grove, Illinois campus. Our program provides students with a solid foundation in the basic sciences, doctoral-level leadership and professional training, and comprehensive instruction in all aspects of anesthesia management, supported by an advanced, state-of-the-art simulation learning center.
  
  
Our mission is to educate nurses through rigorous academic and clinical experiences, producing safe, professional, and competent Certified Registered Nurse Anesthesiologists (CRNAs) / nurse anesthetists who meet the anesthesia healthcare needs of society.
  
  
The successful candidate will be expected to teach within the entry-into-practice DNAP program. Examples of courses include Principles and Pathophysiology, Pharmacology for Anesthesia, and Scholarly Projects.
  
  
**In-Person Requirements**
Weekly on-campus work is required and depends on teaching assignments, simulation activities, student needs, meetings, and program responsibilities. Full-time faculty may work remotely up to 2 days per week based on academic activities. However, their primary role is to provide in-person lectures, simulation lab training, and participation in faculty meetings, student advising, and other program activities that require an in-person presence. The nurse anesthesia program maintains flexibility in the work schedule to accommodate the needs of the program and students.
  
  
**Required Qualifications**
To align with standard accreditation guidelines for didactic and clinical faculty, candidates must possess:
  
  

* Active certification or recertification as a CRNA by the NBCRNA.
* An unencumbered RN and/or APRN license (eligible for licensure in Illinois).
* A doctoral degree (DNAP, DNP, Ph.D., Ed.D., or equivalent).
* A minimum of 3 years of clinical experience as a CRNA.

**Preferred Qualifications And Experience**

* Previous didactic teaching or clinical precepting experience.
* POCUS and regional ultrasound experience
* AANA Didactic Educator Micro-credential (or equivalent training in Didactic Instruction, Curriculum Writing, and Evaluation).

**Position Details & Compensation**
We offer a competitive salary with a comprehensive benefits package. This is full-time position (1.0 FTE) and is eligible for tenure track. We may also consider a part-time position (0.5 to 0.7 FTE).

Over 500 full-time faculty members and 400 staff members are dedicated to the education and development of our students in an environment that encourages learning, respect for all members of the health care team, service, interdisciplinary scholarly activity, and personal growth.

**Teaching Post-Doctoral Fellow**

#### **POSITION OVERVIEW**

##### **JOB SUMMARY:**

The Center for Environmental Diagnostics and Bioremediation (CEDB) at the University of West Florida (UWF) in Pensacola, Florida pursues modern research addressing local and regional environmental issues with basic and applied research approaches (uwf.edu/cedb). We invite applications for a faculty position to serve as Center Director, with an anticipated start date of August 2027. This position is a full-time, 12-month tenured appointment with rank of Associate Professor or Professor. CEDB is a collaborative interdisciplinary research center at UWF with an emphasis on water quality and habitat issues. Candidates from a broad range of disciplines will be considered. The successful candidate will be expected to bring an established research program that complements existing expertise and programs on campus. Candidates with established records of research leadership, including recruitment and expansion of a multidisciplinary research team are especially encouraged to apply. The Director is a member of the Hal Marcus College of Science and Engineering leadership team, working collaboratively to align and advance the strategic goals of the Center with those of the College and University. The Director manages infrastructure and operating budgets of the research labs as well as of the Wetlands Research Laboratory (WRL), the analytical arm of CEDB, including maintaining and expanding the appropriate analytical certifications.
  
  
We seek a collaborative, dynamic, and visionary leader who will integrate cutting-edge science using available resources as well as seeking extramural support. Preferred qualifications also include evidence of fostering strategic partnerships with regional, state, federal, and non-governmental organizations for extramural research support. Documentation of success in serving as a key liaison between research scientists and external stakeholders is also a plus.
  
  
CEDB appointments are generally 75% research with 25% teaching (one course per semester). The successful candidate will apply for tenure and promotion through the relevant academic department, depending on expertise. Salary will be commensurate with experience and qualifications. Mentoring of undergraduate and graduate students is a critical component of the university’s objectives and evaluation of candidates will include prior teaching and mentoring successes. The position offers an excellent opportunity to contribute to and complement existing expertise on campus. UWF is a student-centered public university where faculty and students collaborate on meaningful research across all disciplines. Known for strong graduation rates and personalized attention to strengthen workforce development, UWF emphasizes experiential learning that prepares students for the next step in their career path. Our location in northwest Florida provides easy access to coastal and terrestrial field sites. Engineering programs are rapidly growing, Chemistry is a highly regarded undergraduate research department, and the Biology and Earth and Environmental Sciences Departments continue to grow and increase research productivity.
  
  
Applicants must submit the following documents: Curriculum Vitae (CV) · Letter of application addressing interest in and qualifications for the position at their desired rank · Statement of strategic future research vision for the Center and of personal research interests, including how the research will engage undergraduate and graduate students · Statement of Teaching philosophy

##### **MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

Holds the highest degree appropriate to the field or possesses professional qualifications in the field above those that would be equivalent to the highest degree. Normally, an associate professor will have produced creative work, professional writing, or research; and have had successful teaching or professional experience in the field of specialization. The appointee engages in teaching, scholarship and creative projects, and/or service and other related activities.

##### **POSITION QUALIFICATIONS:**

Ph.D. in appropriate subject matter from an accredited University and minimum of five (5) years post graduate experience. Established research program with expertise in subject area complementary to current expertise in CEDB and UWF. Administrative experience and a record of successful student mentorship.

##### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

Ten (10) years post graduate experience with administrative experience

**About Us**
------------

  

As a comprehensive institution of the University System of Georgia, Valdosta State University (VSU) is a welcoming, aware, and vibrant community founded on and dedicated to serving our communities' rich and diverse heritages. Through excellence in teaching, basic and applied research, and service, VSU provides rigorous programs and opportunities that enrich our students, our university, and our region. As such, the VSU mission consists of three interrelated parts that includes a student mission, university mission and regional mission. The university is equally dedicated to the core values of community, including a commitment to practice civility, integrity and citizenship. As members of this community and proud Blazers we strive to uphold these core values for the advancement of the University, as stated in the Blazer Creed and reflected in our commitment to the University System of Georgia's Core Values.

**Blazer Creed**

Valdosta State University is a learning environment based on trust and mutual respect in which open dialogue, vigorous debate, and the free exchange of ideas are welcome. The University is equally dedicated to the core values of community, including a commitment to practice **civility, integrity,** and **citizenship.** As members of this community, and proud Blazers, we will strive to uphold these core values for the advancement of the University.

**Civility** - A Blazer shows courtesy and compassion as well as respect for the dignity of every human being.

**Integrity** - Each Blazer is responsible for his or her own actions, and our community is stronger when we contemplate the context of our decisions and uphold the principles of trust and honesty.

**Citizenship** - Every Blazer has an interest in the well-being of the community, and, therefore, a duty to stay informed, to make positive contributions, and to offer support to those who need help.

As a Blazer, we pledge to uphold the core principles of **Civility, Integrity,** and **Citizenship**.

**Job Summary**
---------------

  

The Department of Theatre, Dance, & Media seeks applicants for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Theatre History position beginning August 1, 2027. The selected candidate will be responsible for teaching courses in Theatre History and related areas of Theatre Studies, contributing to the department's production and educational programs, and providing service to the department, college, and University.

The successful candidate will demonstrate expertise in theatre history, dramatic literature, critical theory, performance analysis, or a related field, as well as a commitment to undergraduate teaching and student mentorship. The position offers opportunities to contribute to the department's interdisciplinary curriculum and to engage students in the historical, cultural, theoretical, and analytical dimensions of theatre and performance.

  

**APPLICATION PROCESS**

Review of completed applications will begin November 15, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Applicants will be required to attach the following to their online application:

* CV

* Letter of interest

* Unofficial Transcripts (Official Transcripts and Official International Course-by-Course Evaluations Due Upon Hire)

* List of three professional references with contact information (including email)

For additional information, please contact Ian Andersen, Interim Department Head, Theatre, Dance, & Media, via email igandersen@valdosta.edu or phone 229-333-7330.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

  

This position will be responsible for teaching a full 4/4 course load in Theatre, including courses in Theatre History I, Theatre History II, Play Analysis, and TheatreAppreciation. The successful candidate will contribute to the department's Theatre Studies curriculum through instruction that connects historical, theoretical, literary, and performance-based approaches to the study of theatre.

Additional teaching assignments may include courses such as Voice and Diction, Acting I, Stage Movement, and Stage Management, depending on the candidate's qualifications, expertise, and departmental instructional needs.

The successful candidate will be expected to:

* Teach undergraduate courses in Theatre History and related areas of Theatre Studies.

* Develop and deliver engaging, rigorous instruction appropriate to a diverse undergraduate student population.

* Incorporate appropriate historical, theoretical, literary, and performance-based perspectives into coursework.

* Advise and mentor students in areas related to theatre studies and the candidates area(s) of expertise.

* Contribute to the development and assessment of the department's curriculum.

* Participate in the department's production and performance activities as appropriate to the candidate's expertise and departmental needs.

* Provide service to the Department, College, University, profession, and/or community.

* Maintain an active program of scholarship, creative activity, or other professional engagement appropriate to the candidates field and the expectations of a tenure-track faculty appointment.

* Work collaboratively with faculty and staff across Theatre, Dance, & Media and the broader College of the Arts.

**Typical Allocation of Duties:**

**Teaching and scholarship - 80%**
  
Teaches classes and conducts/presents research in the employee's academic discipline.
  
  
**Service - 20%**
  
Participates in service at the department, college, and university levels.

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

  

* A terminal degree in Theatre History, Critical Theory, Dramatic Literature, Performance Analysis, Performance Studies or a related field by the time of appointment.

* Demonstrated expertise in theatre history, dramatic literature, critical theory, performance analysis, or a closely related area.

* Demonstrated ability to teach undergraduate students effectively.

* Ability to teach Theatre History I and II, Play Analysis, and Theatre Appreciation.

* Ability to work effectively and collaboratively in an academic and production-oriented environment.

* Commitment to student mentorship and undergraduate education.

* Ability to contribute to the department, college, university, and/or professional community through service.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

  

* A record of effective teaching appropriate to the applicant's career stage.

* College-level teaching experience in Theatre History, Dramatic Literature, Play Analysis, Theatre Appreciation, or related courses.

* Expertise in one or more areas of theatre history, performance studies, critical theory, dramatic literature, or related fields.

* Demonstrated ability to teach additional theatre courses such as Voice and Diction, Acting I, Stage Movement, or Stage Management.

* Experience mentoring students from diverse backgrounds and educational experiences.

* Evidence of scholarly or creative activity appropriate to the applicant's field and career stage.

* Experience contributing to theatre production, direction, performance, or other professional activities.

**Proposed Salary**
-------------------

  

Commensurate with experience

**USG Core Values**
-------------------

  

The University System of Georgia is comprised of our 26 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and can be found on-line at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18\_personnel\_conduct.

Employment is contingent upon:

Employment may also be contingent upon the job-based requirements if applicable for your position:

The University of Southern Mississippi is currently accepting applications for the position of Assistant Professor of Polymer Science and Engineering.

Brief statement of teaching philosophy that includes interest in specific core courses in the polymer science and engineering graduate and undergraduate curricula, particularly courses in polymer physics and polymer engineering

Review of applications will begin **November 13, 2026** and continue until the position is filled. Applications received after this date may be considered at the discretion of the committee and/or hiring authority.  
  
For inquiries, contact Dr. Derek Patton, Director, School of Polymer Science and Engineering at derek.patton@usm.edu.  
  
Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for visa sponsorship. The University will not sponsor applicants for work visas (e.g., H-1B).  
  
**Job Summary**  
The School of Polymer Science and Engineering (SPSE) at The University of Southern Mississippi invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position beginning August 2027. We seek candidates whose research and teaching will complement and expand the School’s strengths in polymer science and engineering. We are particularly interested in candidates developing research programs broadly within polymer physics, physical polymer chemistry, or polymer engineering, with the disciplinary expertise to contribute to core undergraduate and graduate teaching in these areas. Outstanding candidates in other contemporary areas of polymer science and engineering are also encouraged to apply.  
  
**Primary Duties and Responsibilities**

* Develop and sustain an externally funded, internationally recognized research program.
* Deliver high-impact instruction in undergraduate and graduate courses in polymer science and engineering, fostering a dynamic and experiential learning environment.
* Mentor and supervise graduate and undergraduate researchers, emphasizing scholarly excellence and professional development.
* Contribute to the mission of the school, college, university, and broader scientific community through professional service.
* Perform other duties as assigned

  

**Minimum Qualifications**  
Earned Ph.D. by the start date in polymer science and engineering or a closely related discipline.  
Demonstrated record of research productivity, as evidenced by peer-reviewed publications, professional presentations, and/or grant submissions.  
  
**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Ability to work effectively, collaboratively, and collegially with students, staff, and faculty
* Commitment to fostering a world-class research and learning environment in which faculty, staff, and students can thrive
* Exceptional written and oral communication skills
* Knowledge associated with use and application of common instrumentation and methodologies in polymer science and engineering

**Preferred Qualifications**  
Postdoctoral research experience with clear potential to build collaborative research programs within SPSE and across disciplines  
  
**About the School:** The School of Polymer Science and Engineering (SPSE) is one of the nation's few academic units devoted entirely to polymer science and engineering. SPSE comprises 13 faculty members, including multiple early-career awardees. Research in the School spans polymer composites and materials for extreme environments, including fire-retardant and carbon–carbon systems; biomaterials and polymers for human health, including tissue repair, regeneration, and therapeutic delivery; materials for energy and sustainability; optoelectronic materials; and advanced coatings. SPSE maintains a robust, well-funded research portfolio supported by federal agencies, industry, and private foundations. The Thames Polymer Science Research Center provides state-of-the-art facilities for polymer research, including NMR (400/600 MHz), TEM, SAXS/WAXS, XPS/UPS, polymer processing (extrusion/injection molding), composite fabrication, and advanced thermal, rheological, and mechanical characterization tools.  
  
SPSE sustains one of the largest polymer-focused graduate programs in the country alongside a growing ABET-accredited undergraduate program, and offers B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. degrees in polymer science and engineering. For more information about SPSE, visit usm.edu/polymer-science-engineering.

**About The University of Southern Mississippi**
  
Since our founding in 1910, The University of Southern Mississippi has remained dedicated to preparing students for success. We deliver programs to more than 13,000 students in Hattiesburg and Long Beach, at teaching and research sites across the Mississippi Gulf Coast, as well as online. We are a community-engaged Carnegie R1 university, earning distinction as one of the nation's leading research institutions.  
  
Southern Miss is known for pioneering work in polymer science, ocean science, spectator sports safety and security, and bringing language to children with communication disorders. We are also a national leader in a broad range of disciplines, including cybersecurity, hydrography, nutrition, aquaculture, kinesiology, and economic development, among others.
  
  
We produce graduates ready to enter fields that are leading the way in emerging technologies through programs such as computer engineering, information technology, and ocean engineering. We’re developing the next generation of business leaders, while also responding to critical workforce shortages by producing skilled professionals in education and nursing. With a tradition of excellence in the arts, we are one of only 36 public institutions in the nation accredited in four major areas of the arts. Home to the Golden Eagles, our student-athletes compete in 17 NCAA Division I sports. With a culture marked by passion and persistence, Southern Miss is delivering graduates who are ready for life. For more information, visit www.usm.edu.

The University of Southern Mississippi is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment. EOE/VETS/DISABILITY.

---------------------------

**Teaching:**

* The successful candidate will develop and teach undergraduate and graduate courses in Criminal Justice, with particular emphasis on homeland security and emergency management.
* Teaching responsibilities may also include courses in criminal justice policy, security studies, law enforcement, corrections, cybersecurity, research methods, or other areas consistent with the candidate’s expertise and departmental needs.
