The ISE program offers a dynamic undergraduate experience grounded in analytics, optimization, systems design and real-world problem solving, capped with hands-on industry projects. High-achieving students can accelerate their path through Early Entry graduate coursework. At the graduate level, flexible master’s options, including Engineering Management, prepare professionals to lead technical teams, improve processes and drive data-informed decisions across industries.

  

**Vacancy Open to**

All Candidates

  

**Description of Work**

The University of North Carolina at Charlotte recognizes the differentiation of mission, goals, and objectives inherent in the diversity of disciplines represented by its colleges and departments. Thus, the Job Responsibilities and Essential Functions for Tenured and Tenure Track Faculty should be interpreted in the context of the related departmental and collegiate goals.
  
Teaching, Advising, Curriculum and Instructional Development – Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to teaching may include but are not limited to: subject matter competence, course design, course presentation, advising and consultation, directing student research, curriculum and instructional development, and grading student work.
  
Scholarly Research, Creative, and Other Professional Activities – All tenured and tenure-track faculty are expected to participate in expanding the knowledge base of their academic field by conducting research or engaging in other creative activities as appropriate to the faculty member’s discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to research may include but are not limited to: research/creative activity that generates new knowledge and/or synthesizes and/or integrates existing knowledge, publication, an on-going agenda for research, scholarly, and creative activity, and are expected to seek extramural support for their work.
  
Service to University, the Public, and the Profession – All tenured and tenure-track faculty are expected to engage in a program of service appropriate to their discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to service may include but are not limited to: service to the administration and governance of the University, public service, and service to the profession.
  
  
This position is subject to research-security screening. As part of the application, applicants must disclose, **either in their CV or in a separate document submitted with the application**, all current appointments or affiliations with foreign institutions or organizations, foreign research support, and ongoing research collaborations with foreign institutions, organizations, or their personnel. Before candidates advance to an on-campus interview, the university will review this information and other publicly available information for relationships involving institutions on the current Section 1286 list and any other applicable U.S. restricted-party lists. A disclosed or identified relationship does not automatically disqualify a candidate. As a condition of employment, a selected candidate must resolve any relationship the university determines would violate applicable law or sponsor requirements or materially impair the candidate’s or the university’s eligibility for federal funding.
  
  
To view the complete Job Responsibilities and Essential Functions for Tenured and Tenure-Track Faculty document visit our website: https://facultyhandbooks.charlotte.edu/full-time-faculty-handbook/

  

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

The Industrial and Systems Engineering Department (ISE) at UNC Charlotte is seeking candidates for an 9-month tenure-track Assistant Professor (Pos 4416) with an expected start date of August 2027. A successful candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate courses in engineering management (e.g., project management, supply chain management), systems engineering, operations research, data analytics, and artificial intelligence applications; contribute to curriculum development; and mentor undergraduate and graduate students. The candidate is expected to establish and maintain an active, high-impact, and externally funded research program that complements and supports multidisciplinary research efforts in healthcare, manufacturing and supply chains, energy, and transportation and advanced mobility.

  

Research expertise may include systems modeling and decision analysis, forecasting, machine learning, optimization, reliability, simulation, and related analytical and computational methods. The department is particularly interested in candidates who leverage artificial intelligence, machine learning, big data, cloud/edge computing, cybersecurity, and related emerging technologies to address contemporary engineering management and systems challenges. Potential application areas include transformational energy systems and digital twins for energy applications; intelligent vehicles, electrification, and large-scale transportation systems; healthcare systems and technologies; digital manufacturing, smart manufacturing, and resilient supply chains; and smart and sustainable cities and infrastructure. Candidates may also develop research that bridges multiple application areas, such as intelligent transportation and energy systems, digital twins for manufacturing and healthcare, or data-driven optimization of interconnected infrastructure.

The candidate will be expected to disseminate research through peer-reviewed journal publications and national and international conferences and to pursue external funding to develop and sustain a productive research program. The candidate is also expected to contribute to multidisciplinary research collaborations within the department, college, university, and external organizations. The candidate will participate in service activities within the department, college, and university, as well as in relevant professional engineering organizations. Engagement with industry partners and regional stakeholders is expected to strengthen collaborative research, support educational and workforce.

  

**Minimum Experience/Education**

UNC Charlotte gives primary consideration to the earned doctorate or terminal degree in the teaching discipline or a related discipline.

  

**Preferred Education, Skills and Experience**

Applicants must hold a Ph.D. degree in Engineering or another closely related field, such as Operations Research and Applied Mathematics. Preferred applicants will have a background in systems analytics and its applications in one or more of the following areas: supply chain, health care, transportation, energy, and manufacturing, and can teach R and Python.

  
  

In addition, they must demonstrate significant accomplishments or outstanding potential in scholarship, teaching, and research, depending on the rank of appointment. Successful candidates are expected to: 1) develop and sustain nationally and internationally recognized, externally funded research programs as evidenced by high-quality publications and successful mentoring of students; 2) contribute to teaching and curriculum development at both the graduate and undergraduate levels; and 3) contribute to the mission of the department.

  
  

**Necessary Licenses/Certifications**

N/A

  

**Special Notes to Applicants**

Complete applications must include

* a current resume;
* a letter of interest;
* one page statement of research; one page statement of teaching;
* and the names, addresses, telephone numbers, and e-mail addresses for three professional references.
  

Review of applications will begin 11/16/2026.

The University of North Carolina at Charlotte is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against employees or applicants for employment based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, physical or mental disability, veteran status, or any other protected status. In keeping with this commitment, UNC Charlotte ensures that persons of any background are invited, included, and treated equally in the terms and conditions of employment.
  
  
The candidate chosen for this position will be required to provide an official transcript of their highest earned degree and submit to a criminal background check.

**Job Purpose:**

The Department of Psychology and Neuroscience at Gonzaga University in Spokane, WA invites applicants for a full-time Assistant Professor position (tenure-track) in Neuroscience beginning August 16, 2027. We are seeking a neuroscientist whose research investigates the neural mechanisms underlying human cognition, perception, and/or behavior. We welcome candidates from a range of areas within human neuroscience, with particular interest in researchers whose work could utilize our existing electroencephalography (EEG) and/or transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) facilities and provide meaningful research opportunities for undergraduate students. Gonzaga University is committed to pursuing excellence in teaching by creating engaging, inclusive learning environments for undergraduate students, and we are seeking a colleague who shares that commitment. Courses will include a mixture of introductory-level Psychology and Neuroscience courses and upper-division Neuroscience courses. We seek candidates who demonstrate an active program of research in neuroscience and who can mentor undergraduate students in their research.
  
  
Ideal candidates will have a record of teaching undergraduates from a variety of backgrounds and identities, including those historically marginalized in the sciences (e.g., first-generation students, students from low-income families, BIPOC students, LGBTQ+ students, and students with disabilities).
  
  
**About Gonzaga University and Spokane, Washington:**
  
The Psychology and Neuroscience Department and the College of Arts and Sciences are committed to inclusive excellence, and the success of a diverse population of undergraduate students, staff, and faculty. Gonzaga University is a Jesuit, Catholic, humanistic institution, and is therefore interested in candidates who will contribute to its distinctive mission of educating students “for lives of leadership and service for the common good.” The University is committed to fostering “a mature commitment to dignity of the human person, social justice, diversity, intercultural competence, global engagement, solidarity with the poor and vulnerable, and care for the planet.” Successful applicants will have read the mission statement and engaged with it throughout their application. The University is a committed EEO/AA employer seeking to increase the diversity of its faculty, staff, and students. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to their disability status and/or protected veteran status.
  
  
Gonzaga’s campus sits adjacent to downtown Spokane, WA, along the Spokane River. We exist on the historical and current lands of Salish speaking tribes in the Inland Northwest’s most metropolitan region. Spokane is Washington’s second largest city and boasts a vibrant restaurant, entertainment, and arts community; it is also home to a diverse array of neighborhoods and popular outdoor recreational areas.

For more information on our mission, please visit: https://www.gonzaga.edu/about/our-mission-jesuit-values/mission-statement

**Essential Functions:**

* Teach an equivalent to 9 credits each semester, typically three lecture sections (3 credits each) per semester. Teaching areas will be matched to candidates’ preparation and interests according to program and department needs, but will include a mixture of introductory-level Neuroscience courses, such as NEUR 201: Introduction to Neuroscience, and upper-division courses that support both the Neuroscience and Psychology majors. These may include BIOL 376: Cellular Neurophysiology, HPHY 451: Systems Neurophysiology, NEUR 399: Scientific Communication, NEUR 499: Neuroscience and Society, PSYC 300: Biological Psychology, PSYC 381: Affective Neuroscience, and PSYC 404: Psychology of Addiction, as well as advanced seminar courses in the candidate’s area of scholarly expertise.
* Develop a successful neuroscience research program providing quality research experiences to undergraduates. A successful researcher will publish in peer reviewed journals and seek external research funding.
* Provide academic and career advising and mentoring to 15 – 25 undergraduate students per year in the associated Neuroscience major, starting in the second year.
* Support the Psychology and Neuroscience department, the College of Arts and Sciences, and university through service and other forms of academic citizenship while maintaining close relationships with departments collaborating with the Neuroscience Program such as Biology and Human Physiology.
* Engage in professional activities that inform teaching, enhance student experience, and help the faculty member to remain current in their field.
* Maintain standards of professionalism.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* A Ph.D. in Neuroscience, Psychology, or a closely related field.
* At least one year experience teaching undergraduate students in relevant courses.
* Evidence of a research program focused on the neural mechanisms underlying human cognition, perception, and/or behavior that utilizes, or could be advanced through, methods such as electroencephalography (EEG) and/or transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS).

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* At least one year of postdoctoral work or a similar experience.
* Evidence of engaging, inclusive teaching at the undergraduate level.
* Evidence of effectiveness in teaching and mentoring undergraduate students.
* Evidence of peer-reviewed scholarship.

Terminal Degree

**Attention to Detail - Ability to focus on detailed tasks for extended periods:** Daily (>75% of time)

**Problem-Solving - Ability to identify and resolve issues effectively:** Daily (>75% of time)

  

**Required Application Materials:**

We welcome candidates working across rhetoric and composition, writing studies, technical and professional communication, digital rhetoric, literacy studies, or related fields.

Candidates should demonstrate how their work develops and applies questions about authorship, creativity, expertise, communication, labor, literacy, ethics, publishing, and/or the future of humanistic inquiry.
  
  
Candidates should also demonstrate a record of research, publication, and practical and pedagogical engagement with emerging technologies. Candidates should demonstrate the ability to work across disciplinary boundaries through expertise in multiple areas of study and the creative integration of diverse approaches.
  
  
We also seek candidates with a commitment to collaborative scholarship, which may be demonstrated through leadership and participation in academic programs, research initiatives, or public-facing projects. City: West Lafayette

**Job Summary**
---------------

As part of Purdue University’s strategic investment in One Health – Healthy and Resilient Living Systems, the Department of Philosophy within the College of Liberal Arts invites applications for a tenure-track or tenured faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor level. The Department of Philosophy seeks faculty who can contribute to the Department’s mission while working collaboratively with One Health researchers.

  

**Area of Specialization**  

* Bioethics (broadly construed)

  

**Area of Competence**  

* One of (1) Philosophy of Science, (2) Philosophy, Politics, and Economics, and (3) Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence

Applicants are expected to demonstrate a track record of securing external funding, or the promise of creating one.

  

**Purdue’s One Health Initiative**

  

This strategic recruitment will help advance Purdue’s One Health initiative ( https://www.purdue.edu/onehealth/) which seeks to tackle complex challenges with real-world impact at the intersection of human, animal, and plant health. This recruitment initiative builds on previous strategic faculty recruitment initiatives in: (1) Integrated Health; (2) AI-Driven Biomolecular Design, and (3) Advanced Chemistry. In addition, a parallel strategic faculty recruitment initiative in Intelligent Medicines is ongoing. Through academic programs, research, facility infrastructure and industry partnerships, Purdue’s One Health efforts are making giant leaps in improving health outcomes for all living things and driving economic growth regionally and globally. This strategic faculty recruitment initiative focused on Healthy and Resilient Living Systems is expected to build on prior recruitment initiatives and existing Purdue research and academic strengths, to transform research and impact human, animal and environmental health by bridging silos and fostering collaboration across disciplines.

  

The health and prosperity of society depend upon resilient living systems that connect ecosystems, plants, animals, insects, microbes, and people. Emerging and chronic diseases, food insecurity, environmental degradation, climate change, nutrient deficiencies, invasive species, and ecosystem disruption are increasingly interconnected challenges that require integrated approaches across biological scales and disciplinary boundaries. This strategic recruitment initiative will help establish Purdue as a national leader in predicting, designing, and improving living systems that support health, sustainability, and economic vitality. Working with existing campus experts, this cluster would develop innovative solutions that enhance health resilience from genes and microbiomes to organisms, food systems, populations, and ecosystems. By integrating strengths in agriculture, engineering, artificial intelligence, data science, and health sciences, Purdue aims to create a globally distinctive platform for addressing complex challenges at the intersection of food systems, environmental stewardship, animal and human health, and economic prosperity.

**Qualifications**

  

* A Ph.D. in Philosophy or a related discipline
* A record of research excellence and productivity commensurate with rank
* Demonstrated potential or record of interdisciplinary collaboration and impactful scholarship
* Commitment to teaching and student mentorship

  

**Faculty Responsibilities**

  

* Establish a vigorous, externally funded research program
* Teach and develop undergraduate and graduate courses with the Philosophy program, and mentor and supervise students as needed
* Collaborate across disciplines to solve complex global one health challenges

**Job Summary Continued**
-------------------------

**Integration within the Purdue One Health Community**

Collectively, the strategic faculty recruitment initiatives represent a forward-thinking investment in Purdue’s research infrastructure and academic excellence. Faculty hired as part of these One Health strategic faculty recruitment initiatives will be supported as part of the overall One Health community. Together, these faculty members are expected to work across diverse disciplines, enhance Purdue’s external funding potential, and drive innovation at the intersection of health, environment, food, and economics. In addition to joining an academic unit, faculty hired under this initiative will have the opportunity to join a vibrant ecosystem of interdisciplinary centers and institutes, that span the hard tech corridor between Indianapolis and West Lafayette including:

* Cognition, Agency, and Intelligence Center (CAIC)
* Center for Aging and the Life Course (CALC)
* Center for Rural and Migrant Health
* Center for Health Analytics and Therapeutic Intelligence
* Institute for a Sustainable Future

  

The integrated, cross-disciplinary nature of One Health is essential for addressing today’s most urgent One Health challenges and ensuring Purdue’s continued leadership in research, education, and community impact.

  

**Application Process**

  

To apply, please submit a cover letter, CV, research statement, teaching statement, and contact information for at least three references. Review of applications will begin on November 6, 2026 and continue until positions are filled. Applications should be submitted at: https://careers.purdue.edu/job/Assistant-Associate-Professor-of-Philosophy/44309-en\_US/ . A background check is required for employment in this position.

  

Purdue University is an equal opportunity/equal access university.

The **Department of Philosophy at the University of Washington, Seattle** invites applications for a full-time (100% FTE) faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor Tenure-Track, with an anticipated start date of September 2027. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in research, teaching and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community.

The successful candidate will be expected to develop a robust research program that addresses philosophical issues in relation to artificial intelligence and complements existing scholarship in the department; teach at the undergraduate and graduate levels; serve on dissertation committees and mentor graduate and undergraduate students; actively participate in service to the university, profession, and broader communities; and promote a diverse and inclusive community of faculty, staff, and students. jobs.title: Peter Roth Internship 2027
jobs.description:
***The Peter Roth Internship Program*** **is made possible by generous support from Ava DuVernay’s ARRAY Alliance, The Berlanti Family Foundation, The Chuck Lorre Family Foundation, and The Katie McGrath & J.J. Abrams Family Foundation.**

**Scope**

*The Peter Roth Internship Program,* named in honor of the legendary television executive, offers 20 talented undergraduate students whose perspectives and experiences are not widely represented in the media and entertainment industry an unrivaled paid apprenticeship experience for those interested in a career in television. This prestigious internship has been created to inspire the next generation of television professionals to embody Peter Roth’s visionary ideals including his commitment to innovative storytelling, his love for writers, and his passion for the art form of television. The program will also underscore the critical importance of nurturing an array of creative voices and portrayals on television—a hallmark of Peter Roth’s career.

**Program**

The Paley Center will offer students a comprehensive, paid internship that expands upon the institution’s long-running accredited internship programs. Using the renowned Paley Archive and its unmatched collection of television programming, the Paley Center will offer an extensive course to help students better understand the importance of a cross-section of voices and portrayals on television. Interns will also attend guest lectures, meet-and-greets, and Q&A sessions with television executives, talent, showrunners, writers, and other members of a creative team to gain an appreciation for the art of storytelling. The program will also include first-hand experience working at the Paley Center, along with site visits to networks and sets to provide a valuable understanding of the business side of television.

The Peter Roth Internship program runs from June 1st, 2027, through July 8th, 2027.

The breakdown is as follows:

From June 1st, 2027 through July 8th, 2027:

The program will be conducted Tuesday through Thursday: 10:00 am to 5:00 pm ET, unless time is shifted to allow participation in a Paley program that is in the early morning, evening, or on the weekend.

The internship will be held in-person at the Paley Center in New York City.

Peter Roth Interns will be paid $17 per hour. The advertised pay rate reflects this role's good faith maximum hourly rate. The advertised pay rate is not a promise of a particular wage for any specific employee.

**Application**

The application process will open on Thursday, October 1, 2026.

  

**There is an Early Bird Deadline which will offer applicants priority consideration in the process. The Early Bird Deadline closes Wednesday, December 2, 2026, at 11:59 pm ET.**

**The Final Deadline closes Wednesday, January 13, 2027, at 11:59 pm ET. Only fully complete applications will be considered.**

Applicants must be undergraduate students who are currently enrolled in a college degree program at an accredited college/university with a **GPA of 3.2 or higher** and **who will be a junior or senior in the fall of 2027.** The selection is highly competitive and based on a combination of criteria including evidence of exemplary academic achievement and exceptional leadership skills. Students from all backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.

For a complete application, please provide:

* Resume and cover letter
* Answers to the 3 essay questions
* 2 letters of recommendation from either a professor, a school advisor, or a current/former supervisor who can speak about your education work or background, character or professional competence, and interest in the entertainment, media, and television field (please provide contact information such as email address and phone number for references to be reached for follow-up)
* 1 writing sample for collegiate coursework (at most 3 pages) related to media and/or the media industry are encouraged but not required
* Transcript (while an unofficial transcript is acceptable for the initial application process, all Finalists will be required to submit an official school transcript. Finalists only will be reimbursed if there is a cost from the school to obtain an official transcript)

  

**Questions**

For more details about the program and FAQs to apply, go to www.paleycenter.org/rothinternship.

If you have additional questions, please email peterrothinternshipprogram@paleycenter.org and we will respond to you shortly.

**About Peter Roth**

  

Peter Roth’s inspiring and visionary leadership has earned the respect and admiration of his colleagues, as well as actors, writers, directors, and the millions of viewers the world over who have benefitted from his enduring body of work. Peter’s acumen for mentoring young talent and developing widely successful programming made him a vital part of the success behind iconic series that have resonated with audiences everywhere, including hits such as *All American*, *Arrow*, *Cherish**the Day*, *Fringe*, *George Lopez*, *Gilmore Girls*, *Nip/Tuck*, *One Tree Hill*, *Pretty Little Liars*, *Queen Sugar*, *Shameless*, *Smallville*, *Supernatural*, *The Big Bang Theory*, *The Closer*, *The Flash*, *The Mentalist*, *The Middle*, *The Vampire Diaries*, *The West Wing*, *Two and a Half Men*, *Westworld*, and countless others. During his twenty-two-year tenure at Warner Bros. Television Group, as President and then Chairman, thirty-two scripted primetime television series have reached the coveted hundred-episode milestone.

  

Previously, Peter Roth served as President, Fox Entertainment, President of Production at Twentieth Network Television, and President of Stephen J. Cannell Productions, where during a six-year tenure, he was involved with the creation and sale of many critically acclaimed series. He spent ten years at the ABC Television Network, where he began his television career in 1976 as Manager of Children’s Programs. He was promoted that same year to Director and was responsible for ABC’s number-one-rated Saturday morning schedule. In June 1979, he was named Director of Current Primetime Programs and was promoted to Vice President, Current Primetime Series, in November 1981.

  

**About T****he Paley Center** **for Media**

The Paley Center for Media is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that leads the discussion about the cultural, creative, and social significance of television, radio, and emerging platforms, drawing upon its curatorial expertise, an international collection, and close relationships with the media community. The general public can participate in Paley programs in both New York and Los Angeles that explore and celebrate the creativity, the innovations, the personalities, and the leaders who are shaping media. They can also access the Paley Center’s permanent media collection, which contains over 160,000 television and radio programs and advertisements. Through the global programs of its Media Council and International Council, the Paley Center also serves as a neutral setting where media professionals can engage in discussion and debate about the evolving media landscape. Previously known as The Museum of Television & Radio, the Paley Center was founded in 1975 by William S. Paley, a pioneering innovator in the industry. For more information, please visit paleycenter.org.

Overview:

The Department of History at Utah State University (USU) invites applications for a tenure-track, nine-month position at the rank of Assistant Professor in Philosophy. We are looking for a generalist with a specialization in Early Modern Philosophy, and experience in teaching Introduction to Philosophy, Ethics or applied ethics courses, and introductory courses in philosophy of religion or political philosophy. The successful applicant will teach in our general education program, which offers pre-disciplinary courses focused on big questions in the humanities with a focus on seminal texts and intensive instruction in writing. The department seeks a highly motivated teacher and researcher to join a vibrant community of scholars at our Logan campus. Teaching is the primary focus of this position, and the faculty member will be responsible for teaching six courses per year. The anticipated start date is August 2027.

Responsibilities:

**The successful candidate will be expected to:**

* Demonstrate excellence in teaching and effectiveness in research
* Teach in our general education program
* Contribute to the Philosophy Program’s lower-division and upper-division curricula
* Mentor undergraduates in their studies in the philosophy program
* Demonstrate commitment to high-quality teaching, mentoring, and meaningful educational opportunities
* Contribute to service in the Program, Department, College, and University

Qualifications:

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* A PhD in Philosophy by July 2027
* Evidence of teaching excellence
* Evidence of scholarly productivity

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Evidence of teaching excellence, particularly in Early Modern Philosophy, Introduction to Philosophy, and courses in ethics or applied ethics

Required Documents:

Review of applications begins 26 October 2026, and continues until the position is filled. Along with the online application, please attach:

* Curriculum Vitae to be uploaded at the beginning of your application in the Candidate Profile under “Resume/CV”
* The names and email addresses of three references to be typed at the beginning of the application (your references will be asked to upload a letter of recommendation if your candidacy advances to the next level).

Along with the online application, please attach the following documents under "Documents 1-10":

* A cover letter that speaks to your experience as a teacher and researcher in the field of Philosophy.
* Teaching statement addressing your approach to teaching, noting how your teaching approach is particularly suited to supporting the success of a wide range of students.
* A sample syllabus for an Introduction to Philosophy course.
* Evidence of teaching excellence.

Additional materials may be requested of candidates who advance to the next level.

\*\*Document size may not exceed 10 MB.\*\*

Advertised Salary: Commensurate with qualifications and experience, plus excellent benefits ADA:

College/Department Highlights:

The Department of History at Utah State includes dynamic undergraduate programs in Folklore, History, Philosophy, Religious Studies, and Classics as well as master's programs in Folklore, History, and Ancient Languages and Cultures. The faculty values advanced research in keeping with USU’s research mission, and it places the highest importance on accessible and quality teaching. All faculty are part of the College of Arts and Sciences, which plays an instrumental role in teaching critical thinking, knowledge-building skills and the ability to pose meaningful questions that advance understanding and knowledge. Students in our college confront the great questions and controversies, learn about the forces that have shaped our world, and develop the skills to tackle its most pressing challenges. Our graduates are creative problem-solvers with a passion for making a difference. The education they receive here prepares them to address the problems of today and to succeed wherever their career path takes them tomorrow.

Founded in 1888, Utah State University is Utah’s premier land-grant, public service university. As an R1 research institution, Utah State is dedicated to advancing knowledge and serving the public good through innovative research and scholarly activities that are grounded in reciprocal engagement with local, regional, and global communities. USU prepares students to be active, civically engaged leaders who are prepared to address critical societal challenges. Dedicated to providing a high-quality and affordable education, USU remains a leader in research, discovery, and public impact.

USU enrolls over 29,800 students, both online and in person at locations throughout the state. Utah State’s 30 locations include a main campus in Logan, Utah, residential campuses in Price and Blanding, and six additional statewide campuses, along with education centers serving every county. USU educates students from all 50 states and more than 80 countries. For over 100 years, USU Extension has served and engaged Utahns, serving every county in the state.

Competing at the NCAA Division I level in 16 sports, USU is a proud member of the Pac-12 Conference, officially joining on July 1, 2026. The Aggies capped a historic final season in the Mountain West by capturing nine combined regular-season and tournament titles in 2025–26, with five teams advancing to postseason play. This tradition of excellence extends to the classroom, where 232 student-athletes earned academic honors, and to the community, where USU ranked second nationally in Division I service hours, with nine teams placing in the top 10 for community service.

Utah State is dedicated to fostering a community where all individuals feel respected, valued, and supported and where diversity of thought and culture are cultivated. jobs.title: Open Rank Professor - Plant Metabolism
jobs.description:
The Department of Biochemistry and the Center for Plant Science Innovation at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln (UNL) invite applications for a tenure-track nine-month (academic year) faculty position of open rank (assistant/associate/full professor). This appointment is apportioned as 80% research and 20% teaching. Applicants are sought who will develop a vigorous, internationally recognized research program that seeks to identify novel metabolic pathways, regulatory mechanisms and/or biological processes with the goal of translating findings into strategies for crop improvement and/or bio-based products that support sustainable agriculture and biotechnology to enhance human health. Researchers will be able to leverage UNL’s extensive research infrastructure that includes the Plant Transformation Core Research Facility (PTCRF), multi-location biotech fields, and advanced field and greenhouse phenotyping platforms, to validate and scale their discoveries.
  
  
The Department of Biochemistry provides a robust environment for molecular research, offering access to state-of-the-art resources through shared equipment and the Nebraska Center for Biotechnology. Candidates will have the opportunity to utilize the UNL Cryo-EM facility for structural biology, mass spectrometry for metabolomics and proteomics, and bioinformatics and systems biology computational resources.
  
  
The university offers a highly collaborative environment to develop plant-focused research programs with affiliated resources provided by the University Research Centers (Center for Plant Science Innovation, Center for Integrated Biomolecular Communication, Redox Biology Center, Center for Virology), Holland Computing Center, the Quantitative Life Sciences Initiative, Nebraska Innovation Campus and the Center for Biological Chemistry and Complex Biosystems graduate training programs. The University Research Centers and UNL provide cutting-edge research facilities that support multiple-omics, bioinformatics, supercomputing, flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, TEM, SEM, and metabolic engineering. A competitive start-up package and appropriate laboratory and office space will be offered.
  
  
About Us
  
To learn about UNL benefits and your total compensation, please see: **https://go.unl.edu/aboutus**.
  
To learn more about Lincoln, NE at **About Lincoln | Nebraska**.

Minimum Required Qualifications

* Ph.D. or equivalent degree in biochemistry, plant science, or a related field.
* Two or more years of postdoctoral experience.
* Strong record of original research in plant biochemistry as evidenced by peer-reviewed publications.

Preferred Qualifications

* Experience in grant writing.
* Experience teaching in biochemistry or related fields.
* Experience with mentoring students.
* Excellent communication skills.
* Expertise in integrated biochemical, structural, and molecular genetic approaches in plant metabolism.
* Demonstrated potential for collaborative research.

  
Posted Salary
  

How to Apply

Click “Apply for this Job” and then “Faculty Application.” Complete the application and attach the following documents:

* A letter of interest that describes your qualifications for the job and anticipated contributions.

* Your curriculum vitae.

* Contact information for three professional references.

* Statements that describe your philosophy and approach to teaching and research.

* A statement describing your experience working in teams or groups and your anticipated contributions to creating environments in which every person and every interaction matters (2 page maximum). See **https://go.unl.edu/ianrguide** for guidance in writing this statement.

Please combine the statements (items 4 and 5) into a single document and attach as “Other Document.”

jobs.description:
**FACULTY VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT**
The Department of Nursing at Lehman College, City University of New York, invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Adult Health/Medical-Surgical Nursing beginning Spring 2027. Candidates must demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in nursing education at the undergraduate and graduate levels and an active or developing program of research and scholarship consistent with their area of expertise.
  
  

* Teach undergraduate and graduate nursing courses in multiple modalities, including in-person, hybrid, and online formats.
* Teaching assignments may include daytime, evening, weekend and online courses based on departmental needs.
* Advise and mentor undergraduate, master's, and doctoral students.
* Maintain an active program of scholarship and dissemination appropriate to a tenure-track faculty appointment.
* Participate in curriculum development, program evaluation, and continuous quality improvement.
* Provide service to the Department, College, University, profession, and community.

The Department of Nursing and is currently housed in the School of Health Sciences, Human Services and Nursing (HS2N). The School of Health Sciences, Human Services and Nursing currently includes six departments: Exercise Science and Recreation; Health Promotion and Nutrition Sciences; Health Equity, Administration & Technology; Social Work; Speech, Language and Hearing Sciences, and Nursing. The school is also home to the CUNY Institute for Health Equity. Departments in the School actively engage with community and government partners to support evidence-based practices and health equity, with a special emphasis on urban populations. The faculty are also strongly committed to high-quality teaching and preparation of ethical and skilled health and human service professionals.
  
  
CAMPUS SPECIFIC POSITION DETAILS
  
  
The Lehman College campus is located in the Bronx, New York and is a Senior College within the City University of New York (CUNY) system. Lehman is the only four-year public college in the Bronx and is recognized as a Hispanic-serving Institution. The college serves mainly undergraduate students preparing them for employment, the professions and further study. The Department of Nursing provides education for nursing students at the undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral levels. The teaching load is 18 credit hours over a 9-month appointment. Student advisement is required, (minimum of 3 hours per week during the academic year). Attendance at staff development opportunities, as well as participation in department and school-wide meetings, is expected. The qualified candidate must perform additional service to the College, University, and community. This role includes spearheading program specific-professional development initiatives for undergraduate students. Undergraduate scholar mentorship is encouraged. Opportunities are available for faculty development and travel awards. Lehman College and CUNY internal funding is available through competitive grants for scholarship and professional development support.
  
  
**Qualifications**
Ph.D., EdD., DNS degree with experience in Nursing or related discipline or a related academic field is required on commencement of the appointment. Demonstrated scholarship and dissemination of scholarship through publications and/or, presentations, etc. Ability to cooperate with others for the good of the institution. Active involvement in professional organizations and sincere commitment to student success.
  
  
**Preferred Qualifications**

* Clinical expertise and recent practice experience in adult health/medical-surgical nursing.
* College or university teaching experience in undergraduate and/or graduate nursing education.
* Experience with simulation, technology-enhanced learning, online/hybrid education, and/or innovative teaching strategies.

Salaries are commensurate with education and relevant experience and are subject to the Professional Staff Congress-CUNY salary schedule (http://www.psc-cuny.org/contract/psc-cuny-contract-salary-schedule).
  
  
CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. CUNY also provides mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of a commitment to ongoing faculty professional development.

**Job:**

Assistant Professor of Cognitive Science and Computer Science

**Job Description:**

Barnard seeks to hire a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Cognitive Science and Computer Science to begin July 1, 2027. The area of focus is at the intersection of Human Cognition and Artificial Intelligence. The faculty member's primary affiliation and tenure line will be in the Department of Computer Science, with responsibilities split between the Computer Science Department and the Cognitive Science Program at Barnard. We are seeking candidates who work at the intersection of human cognition and artificial intelligence. The ideal candidate will pursue research and teaching that advances both our understanding of how the mind works and the development of new cognitively inspired and ethically designed AI systems. A successful hire will further the aims and vision of the Cognitive Science Program and Computer Science Department at Barnard.

Barnard is a premier liberal arts undergraduate college for women in New York City affiliated with Columbia University. Barnard faculty are expected to engage in teaching, research, curriculum and program development, undergraduate advising, and mentoring of undergraduate research. There are also opportunities to collaborate with faculty and students across Barnard College and Columbia University, including Columbia’s NSF AI Institute for Artificial and Natural Intelligence (https://arni-institute.org/).

The Program in Cognitive Science at Barnard (https://barnard.edu/cogsci) is a relatively new program that brings together faculty across several departments, including Psychology, Philosophy, Neuroscience and Behavior, Computer Science, and Economics.

  

Barnard’s Computer Science (CS) Department (https://cs.barnard.edu/) has faculty with expertise in Security and Privacy, Natural Language Processing, Computer Graphics, Augmented Reality, AI and Law, Human-Computer Interaction, and Programming Synthesis. The Barnard Computer Science Department works closely with the Vagelos Computational Science Center and with the Columbia CS Department (https://www.cs.columbia.edu/).

**Skills, Qualifications & Requirements:**

**Required Qualifications**

Candidates must have a PhD in Computer Science, Cognitive Science or a related discipline, and should have a promising research agenda and record of scholarship, as well as a demonstrated commitment to undergraduate teaching, mentoring, and increasing participation in cognitive science and/or computer science.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate/Full Professor in Architectural Engineering
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**
---------------------

The University of Kansas (KU) Department of Civil, Environmental and Architectural Engineering (CEAE) seeks outstanding candidates for two tenured or tenure-track faculty positions, one at the rank of Assistant Professor and a second position at the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor in architectural engineering. The focus areas for these positions are in building electrical power systems and the broader energy areas described below. The successful candidates are expected to contribute to the continued development of academic and research programs in architectural engineering and to the broader research community.
  
  
For the building electrical power systems position, relevant expertise may include building electrical power distribution and utilization; electrical system design for commercial and institutional buildings; power quality, reliability, and resilience; emergency and standby power systems; distributed energy resources and microgrids; grid modernization; smart building electrical systems; and advanced sensing, monitoring, and controls for building power systems. The successful candidate in this area will strengthen the program's research and teaching capacity in building electrical and power systems and contribute to engagement with industry and the profession.
  
  
The broader energy areas of interest include integrated building or district energy systems; building-to-grid integration and grid-interactive buildings; distributed energy resource management; building energy resilience; building energy efficiency and decarbonization; environmentally sustainable buildings; renewable energy systems for buildings and communities; grid reliability and energy infrastructure; and net-zero-energy buildings.
  
  
Successful candidates must have an earned doctorate in architectural, mechanical, electrical, or civil engineering or a closely related discipline by the time of appointment. Candidates must demonstrate the potential to develop collaborative, externally funded research programs and to design and teach high-quality undergraduate and graduate courses. The anticipated starting date is August 18, 2027. Successful candidates must be eligible to work in the U.S. prior to the start of the position.
  
  
These positions are subject to a collective bargaining agreement between the University of Kansas and the United Academics of KU, the exclusive representative for the bargaining unit. Faculty have the right to be a member or not be a member of UAKU without fear of personal or professional repercussions.
  
  
The University of Kansas School of Engineering (http://engr.ku.edu/) has undergone a significant expansion while taking explicit care to maintain and improve the high-quality student programs the university is known for. The effort involved a multifaceted approach aimed at growing our facilities, faculty, leadership, and research and, most importantly, supporting students. It also helps industry partners find the new talent, designs, and techniques they need to fuel economic growth and business success.
  
  
The CEAE Department (https://ceae.ku.edu/) currently has 26 tenured/tenure-track faculty, four teaching professors and professors of practice, one research professor, and approximately 360 undergraduate students and 140 graduate students, with programs leading to bachelor’s, master's, and doctoral degrees. The department has a strong history of conducting impactful research while focusing on the success of students at all levels. KU's ABET-accredited architectural engineering program benefits from the university's close proximity to the Kansas City metro area, which is home to one of the nation’s largest concentrations of architectural, engineering, and construction firms. This location provides rich opportunities for industry engagement, research partnerships, and student learning.

**Job Description**
-------------------

The University of Kansas is the state’s flagship university, an R-1 institution and one of just 71 invited members of the prestigious Association of American Universities. Our university consistently earns high rankings for academics and recognition as a premier research university (engaging in $611 million of research in fiscal year 2025). KU offers more than 8,000 courses, 460 degree and certificate programs, and more than 200 fields of study. As of Fall 2025, student enrollment for the Lawrence-Edwards campus was 27,212 representing all 50 states and 115 countries.
  
  
KU’s excellence is a result of the rich tapestry of experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds of our faculty, staff, students, and colleagues from across our nation and the globe. At KU, we invest in continuous learning and growth by creating a climate where people engage in respectful dialogue and debate and support each other’s success. We foster a culture of care where each person is seen, heard and valued. When people feel a true sense of belonging, we believe they are better able to reach their full potential and achieve remarkable things. The successful candidate must be eligible to work in the U.S. by the effective date of the appointment.
  
  
**Job Description:**  
  
40% Teaching
  
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in architectural engineering. Develop courses and participate in curriculum development. Supervise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students throughout the course of their studies.
  
  
40% Research
  
Develop and conduct an innovative research program in building electrical power systems or one of the broader energy areas associated with the positions. Relevant areas include building electrical power systems; integrated building or district energy systems; building-to-grid integration and grid-interactive buildings; distributed energy resource management; grid modernization; building energy resilience; building energy efficiency and decarbonization; environmentally sustainable buildings; renewable energy systems for buildings and communities; grid reliability and energy infrastructure; and net-zero-energy buildings. Establish a strong research agenda leading to external grant support and publication in recognized refereed journals, and participate in local, national, and international professional conferences and other activities appropriate to the discipline. Supervise M.S. and Ph.D. studies.
  
  
20% Service
  
Perform service activities normally expected of university faculty commensurate with rank, including committee service to the Department, School, and University. Also includes national and international service to the profession.

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

**All ranks:**

* Earned doctorate in architectural, mechanical, electrical, or civil engineering or a closely-related discipline by the time of appointment.

* Demonstrable expertise in one or more of the following areas: building electrical power systems; integrated building or district energy systems; building-to-grid integration and grid-interactive buildings; distributed energy resource management; grid modernization; building energy resilience; building energy efficiency and decarbonization; environmentally sustainable buildings; renewable energy systems for buildings and communities; grid reliability and energy infrastructure; or net-zero-energy buildings. Candidates considered for the building electrical power systems position must demonstrate expertise in that area and the ability to contribute to architectural engineering coursework in building electrical systems and power engineering.

* Ability to communicate ideas effectively and work well with others as demonstrated through application materials and interview.

* Demonstrated potential to develop an externally-funded research program and to design and teach high-quality undergraduate and graduate courses.

  
**At the rank of Associate Professor:**

* Sustained record of scholarship and research;

* Evidence of national recognition in the field;

* Demonstrated experience in leading multidisciplinary teams;

* A minimum of five years of post-Ph.D. professional experience in a faculty role or an equivalent combination of academic and relevant industry/practice experience.

  
**At the rank of Professor:**

* Sustained record of scholarship and research;

* Evidence of national and international recognition in the field;

* Demonstrated experience in leading multidisciplinary teams;

* A minimum of ten years of post-Ph.D. professional experience in a faculty role or an equivalent combination of academic and relevant industry/practice experience, with a sustained record of leadership.

**Additional Candidate Instructions**
-------------------------------------

A complete online application includes the following materials: (1) cover letter, including an indication of the position or positions for which the applicant wishes to be considered (2) curriculum vitae; (3) research agenda (2-page limit); (4) teaching philosophy statement (2-page limit); and (5) the names and contact information, including email addresses, for three professional references.

**Required Documents:**

* University application

jobs.title: Reference Librarian - Open Rank Professor
jobs.description:
The University of Nebraska College of Law invites applications for the position of Reference Librarian (Open Rank Professor) at the Schmid Law Library. This 12-month, tenure-track law library faculty position offers an opportunity to support student learning and faculty scholarship while contributing to the mission and values of the College of Law.
  
  
As a valued member of the law library faculty, the Reference Librarian/Law Library Professor will:

* Provide expert research assistance and reference services to a diverse community, including faculty, law students, graduate and undergraduate students, and the public.
* Teach in the first-year legal research program.
* Lead and participate in instructional and outreach initiatives.
* Demonstrate initiative in developing and implementing law library resources, such as creating Libguides and bibliographies that enhance research and learning.
* Take on evolving responsibilities within a modern law library, based on institutional priorities and an individual’s expertise and interests.
* Conduct or contribute to research, scholarship, and other significant creative activity.
* Promote a positive, collaborative, inclusive, and innovative work environment within the law library and the College of Law.
  

This role offers an exciting opportunity to contribute meaningfully to legal education, research, and law library services in a dynamic academic setting. Members of the law library faculty participate in faculty governance at the College of Law and may apply for faculty development fellowships (sabbatical). Initial appointment and rank will be commensurate with experience.

Law library faculty will participate in the University’s generous benefits package. Please find the full range of benefits at **https://hr.unl.edu/health-benefits/**. General information about the Law College is available at **https://law.unl.edu/**.

Minimum Required Qualifications

* A Juris Doctor (J.D.) from an ABA-accredited law school and a Master’s Degree in Library and Information Science or equivalent degree from an ALA-accredited master’s program by the start of employment.

**OR**

  

* A Juris Doctor (J.D.) from an ABA-accredited law school and current enrollment in a Master’s degree program in Library and Information Science from an ALA-accredited institution, or an equivalent graduate degree in library or information science, with completion required within 18 months of hire; or current enrollment in a joint degree program, with completion of both the J.D. and the Master’s degree within six months of hire.

**OR**

  

* A Master’s Degree in Library and Information Science or equivalent degree from an ALA-accredited master’s program AND substantial professional experience as a law librarian demonstrating qualifications comparable to those described above.

The title of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor will be based on the successful candidate’s qualifications.

Click “Apply for this Job” and complete the faculty information form. Attach the following required documents.

For questions about the application process, please contact Rich Leiter, Direcor of the Schmid Law Library, University of Nebraska College of Law, Lincoln, NE 68583-0902 at **rich.leiter@unl.edu**.

**FACULTY VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT**
The Department of Nursing at Lehman College, City University of New York, invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Adult Health/Medical-Surgical Nursing beginning Spring 2027. Candidates must demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in nursing education at the undergraduate and graduate levels and an active or developing program of research and scholarship consistent with their area of expertise.
  
  

* Teach undergraduate and graduate nursing courses in multiple modalities, including in-person, hybrid, and online formats.
* Teaching assignments may include daytime, evening, weekend and online courses based on departmental needs.
* Advise and mentor undergraduate, master's, and doctoral students.
* Maintain an active program of scholarship and dissemination appropriate to a tenure-track faculty appointment.
* Participate in curriculum development, program evaluation, and continuous quality improvement.
* Provide service to the Department, College, University, profession, and community.

The Department of Nursing and is currently housed in the School of Health Sciences, Human Services and Nursing (HS2N). The School of Health Sciences, Human Services and Nursing currently includes six departments: Exercise Science and Recreation; Health Promotion and Nutrition Sciences; Health Equity, Administration & Technology; Social Work; Speech, Language and Hearing Sciences, and Nursing. The school is also home to the CUNY Institute for Health Equity. Departments in the School actively engage with community and government partners to support evidence-based practices and health equity, with a special emphasis on urban populations. The faculty are also strongly committed to high-quality teaching and preparation of ethical and skilled health and human service professionals.
  
  
CAMPUS SPECIFIC POSITION DETAILS
  
  
The Lehman College campus is located in the Bronx, New York and is a Senior College within the City University of New York (CUNY) system. Lehman is the only four-year public college in the Bronx and is recognized as a Hispanic-serving Institution. The college serves mainly undergraduate students preparing them for employment, the professions and further study. The Department of Nursing provides education for nursing students at the undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral levels. The teaching load is 18 credit hours over a 9-month appointment. Student advisement is required, (minimum of 3 hours per week during the academic year). Attendance at staff development opportunities, as well as participation in department and school-wide meetings, is expected. The qualified candidate must perform additional service to the College, University, and community. This role includes spearheading program specific-professional development initiatives for undergraduate students. Undergraduate scholar mentorship is encouraged. Opportunities are available for faculty development and travel awards. Lehman College and CUNY internal funding is available through competitive grants for scholarship and professional development support.
  
  
**Qualifications**
Ph.D., EdD., DNS degree with experience in Nursing or related discipline or a related academic field is required on commencement of the appointment. Must have a baccalaureate and master degree in nursing. Must be licensed or eligible for licensure in New York State at time of appointment. Strong evidence of successful teaching in adult health nursing. Demonstrated scholarship and dissemination of scholarship through publications and/or, presentations, etc. Ability to cooperate with others for the good of the institution. Active involvement in professional organizations and sincere commitment to student success.
  
  
**Preferred Qualifications**

* Clinical expertise and recent practice experience in adult health/medical-surgical nursing.
* College or university teaching experience in undergraduate and/or graduate nursing education.
* Experience with simulation, technology-enhanced learning, online/hybrid education, and/or innovative teaching strategies.
* Evidence of, or potential for, a sustained program of scholarship and dissemination.
* Experience with curriculum development, program evaluation, nursing accreditation, and/or continuous quality improvement.
* Experience mentoring students in scholarly, research, or evidence-based practice activities.
* Evidence of nurse leadership in accreditation, faculty professional development in leading nurse research teams

**Compensation**
Assistant Professor $109,025-$112,841.
  
  
Salaries are commensurate with education and relevant experience and are subject to the Professional Staff Congress-CUNY salary schedule (http://www.psc-cuny.org/contract/psc-cuny-contract-salary-schedule).
  
  
CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. CUNY also provides mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of a commitment to ongoing faculty professional development.
  
  
**How To Apply**
Visit www.cuny.edu, access the employment page, log in or create a new user account, and search for this vacancy using the Job ID or Title. Select "Apply Now" and provide the requested information.
  
  
Candidates must attach a resume, cover letter, writing sample, and three professional references (name, title, organization, and contact information).
  
  
**For Technical Issues**
Contact the service desk by email: service.desk@cuny.edu. If you can, provide screenshots. Please do not provide your User Account password; it is not needed to investigate any issue.
  
  
**For Other Questions**
For questions about the content of any job posting, please contact the Human Resources department: human.resources@lehman.cuny.edu.
  
  
**CLOSING DATE**
Review of CVs will begin on October 30th for spring 2027 and continue until a candidate has been identified.

Applicants and employees will not be discriminated against on the basis of any legally protected category, including sexual orientation or gender identity. EEO/AA/Vet/Disability Employer.

The College of Business & Information Systems at Dakota State University invites applications for a full-time (9-month) tenure-track Assistant Professor or Associate Professor position in economics and statistics. Qualified individuals will contribute to DSU’s graduate and undergraduate business programs through excellence in teaching, research and scholarship, and service, as well as a willingness to collaborate in all phases of academic life. The successful candidate may be assigned to teach courses at both the graduate and undergraduate levels in business areas including economics and statistics. Additional courses from the business administration curriculum may be assigned based on their academic credentials. Courses will be taught on campus in Madison, SD, and online as needed.  
  
Academic rank will be at the Assistant or Associate Professor level, determined by the candidate’s qualifications and experience. The start date of this position is Fall 2027.

* Pensacola - Main Campus, Florida, United States

#### **POSITION DETAILS**

**Employment based visa sponsorship will be considered for this position.**

**Position Number:** 105770
  
**Classification Title:** Assistant Professor
  
**Working Title:** Assistant Professor of Museum Studies
  
  
**Department:** Dept of Art and Design
  
**FLSA Status:** Exempt
  
**Salary Range:** Commensurate with education and experience
  
**Pay Basis:** Annually

#### **POSITION OVERVIEW**

##### **JOB SUMMARY:**

The University of West Florida Department of Art & Design invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Museum Studies. This position will play a central role in developing the new interdisciplinary Minor in Museum Studies and expanding the Art History Major into Museum Studies, both designed to provide students with foundational knowledge and hands-on experience in museums, galleries, collections management, exhibition production, interpretation, preparatorship, and public-facing cultural work. The salary for this position will be commensurate with education and experience.
  
  
This initiative supports the university’s area of expertise in Public Archaeology and Community Heritage and is intended to serve undergraduate and graduate students in Art, Art History, History, Archaeology, Anthropology, Public History, Graphic Design, Arts Administration, and related disciplines. The program will leverage the University’s unique partnerships and resources, including TAG, The Art Gallery at UWF, the Pensacola Museum of Art, the Pensacola Museum of History, the Pensacola Children’s Museum, the UWF Historic Trust, the UWF Archaeology Institute, and the Florida Public Archaeology Network (FPAN).
  
  
The successful candidate will contribute to the development and growth of the Museum Studies Minor and Art History and Museum Studies Major while also helping to guide The Art Gallery at UWF (TAG) as a teaching gallery, exhibition space, and experiential learning site. The position emphasizes interdisciplinary learning, applied museum practice, and student-centered professional development through coursework, internships, exhibitions, collections work, public programming, and collaborative cultural projects.
  
  
The faculty member will be housed in the Department of Art & Design in the College of Arts, Social Sciences and Humanities at the University of West Florida. The Department is strongly committed to fostering a welcoming, collaborative, and student-centered learning environment grounded in interdisciplinary practice, experiential learning, and community engagement.
  
  
Position Responsibilities:
  
  
This is a full-time, tenure-earning position with benefits. The successful candidate will contribute to developing an interdisciplinary Museum Studies Minor and an Art History and Museum Studies Major, teaching courses across museum studies, curatorial practice, gallery operations, collections management, museum education, public history, and audience engagement.
  
  
Teaching responsibilities may include undergraduate courses within the Department of Art & Design, as well as courses that support interdisciplinary connections with History, Public History, Archaeology, Anthropology, Art Administration and related majors and programs. Depending on the candidate’s expertise, courses may address topics such as:
  
  

* Museum Studies
* Exhibition Practices
* Curatorial Methods
* Collections Management
* Museum Education and Interpretation
* Gallery Operations
* Preparatorship and Exhibition Installation
* Public History and Community Heritage
* Museum Writing and Audience Engagement
* Digital Interpretation and Public-Facing Cultural Work
* Art History
* Architectural History

  
The successful candidate should demonstrate the ability to curate exhibitions and develop exhibition-related learning opportunities in collaboration with TAG, the Pensacola Museum of Art, the UWF Historic Trust, the UWF Archaeology Institute, FPAN, and other regional museums, galleries, archives, archaeological organizations, and cultural institutions.
  
  
Experiential Learning & Museum and Gallery Engagement:
  
  
The position connects classroom learning directly to applied gallery and museum practice by guiding exhibitions as teaching opportunities and experiential learning sites, coordinating exhibition and experiential learning opportunities through partnerships with TAG, The Art Gallery at UWF, the Pensacola Museum of Art, the Pensacola Museum of History, the Pensacola Children’s Museum, the UWF Historic Trust, the UWF Archaeology Institute, and the Florida Public Archaeology Network (FPAN). The faculty member will coordinate the department's experiential learning ecosystem and provide mentorship across all stages of exhibition production. This includes leading student-centered initiatives such as exhibition and event graphic design, administrative and preparatorial operations, and an annual faculty-partnered exhibition series that connects coursework with faculty research. Together, these opportunities allow students to engage in the full lifecycle of exhibitions—from concept development and design to installation, programming, and documentation—as the Assistant Professor strengthens curricular connections and expands partnerships with regional cultural institutions.

##### **MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

Holds the highest degree appropriate in Museum Studies, Art History, Public History, Anthropology, Archaeology, Arts Administration, Exhibition Design, Curatorial Studies, or a related field, or possesses equivalent qualifications based on professional experience, and be otherwise qualified to perform assigned duties. The appointee engages in teaching, scholarship and creative projects, and/or service and other related activities.

##### **POSITION QUALIFICATIONS:**

Terminal degree, PhD, MFA, or equivalent, in Museum Studies, Art History, Public History, Anthropology, Archaeology, Arts Administration, Exhibition Design, Curatorial Studies, or a related field, completed by the start date of appointment.
  
  
Professional experience in museums, galleries, archives, collections, cultural institutions, exhibition spaces, or related organizations.
  
Teaching experience at the university level or demonstrated potential for effective undergraduate teaching.
  
  
Demonstrated ability to support gallery, museum, exhibition, collections-based, or public-facing cultural learning experiences for undergraduate students.
  
  
Demonstrated commitment to experiential learning, interdisciplinary collaboration, and student professional development.

##### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

Experience developing or teaching interdisciplinary Museum Studies coursework.
  
  
Experience directing, managing, or coordinating a museum, university gallery, exhibition space, archive, collection, cultural program, or public-facing arts initiative.
  
  
Experience with exhibition production, collections management, curatorial practice, museum education, preparatorship, archives, public programming, or cultural heritage interpretation.
  
  
Experience curating exhibitions or developing exhibition-related projects in collaboration with museums, galleries, archives, archaeological organizations, public history sites, community-based cultural institutions, or university partners.
  
  
Experience supporting experiential learning, internships, undergraduate research, project-based learning, or high-impact educational practices.
  
Experience mentoring students in applied museum, gallery, exhibition, design, archival, or public history contexts.
  
  
Ability to contribute to interdisciplinary collaboration across Art, Art History, Graphic Design, History, Archaeology, Anthropology, Public History, Arts Administration, and related fields.
  
  
Experience working with student exhibition teams, design teams, preparator teams, gallery interns, or museum education programs.
  
  
Experience teaching in multiple modalities, including in-person and online instruction.

##### **PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

* **Physical Requirements:** Regularly involves lifting, bending or other physical exertion. Often exposed to one or more disagreeable environmental factors, such as heat, cold, noise, dust, dirt, chemicals, etc., with often to the point of being objectionable.
* **Impact of Deadlines:** Routine deadlines. Usually sufficient lead time. Variance in work volume, seasonal, and predictable. Priorities can be anticipated. Some interruptions are present. Involves occasional exposure to demands/pressures from persons other than immediate sup.
* **Standing:** Daily
* **Walking:** Daily
* **Sitting:** Daily
* **Reaching with hands and arms:** Daily
* **Climbing or balancing:** Daily
* **Stooping:** Daily
* **Use of hands to handle objects:** Daily
* **Lifting up to 10lbs:** Daily
* **Lifting up to 25lbs:** Occasionally
* **Lifting over 25lbs:** Occasionally
* **Talking as express or exchange of ideas verbally:** Daily
* **Hearing as perceive sound by ear:** Daily
* **Vision as distinguish colors & depth:** Daily

**Special Requirements or Considerations of the Job:**

* This position requires a criminal background screening.

**Special Instructions to Applicants:** Candidates must apply online through the University of West Florida website: https://careers.uwf.edu. Applicants are required to attach a cv, letter of interest and contact information for three references. References will be contacted upon submission of this application. An opportunity to upload these documents will be provided during the application process. For assistance, please contact Human Resources at 850.474.2694 or email jobs@uwf.edu.
  
  
If one or more of your advanced degrees is awarded from an institution outside of the United States, UWF will require a credential evaluation and/or translation prior to onboarding. This credential evaluation should include original documents received directly from your institution so that the agency can evaluate and attest that your credential is equivalent to a similar degree earned at a US institution. If your credential is not in English, this evaluation should also include a translation to US English.
  
  
UWF does not endorse any particular approved agency; however, typically any current National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES) member agency is acceptable. You are advised to check with the agency first to make sure your educational background can be evaluated as some agencies do not evaluate all international degrees.
  
  
When necessary, these credential evaluations will be requested as part of the Offer Letter with instructions on where and to whom these documents should be submitted.

**Position Summary**

Tulane University invites applications for a full-time **Professor of Practice in Mechanical Engineering** in the Department of Physics and Engineering Physics within the School of Science and Engineering.

**About the Department**

The Department of Physics and Engineering Physics is pursuing interdisciplinary excellence through the integration of physics and core engineering disciplines and is substantially expanding its mechanical engineering programs, including the launch of a new Bachelor of Science in Engineering in Mechanical Engineering, a Minor in Mechanical Engineering, and a Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering.

The Department also offers an established Engineering Physics undergraduate major and a Materials Physics & Engineering PhD program.

**About the School of Science and Engineering at Tulane University**

The School of Science and Engineering provides exceptional opportunities for collaboration across disciplines and supports the development of cutting-edge research and educational initiatives. The School is distinctive as the only academic unit at a major research university to merge the behavioral sciences, physical sciences, life sciences, engineering, and mathematics, which provides an unusually rich environment for innovative programs and interdisciplinary research.

Tulane University is a member of the prestigious American Association of Universities (AAU), is classified by the Carnegie Foundation as an R1 (Very High Research Activity) and Community Engaged university, and is committed to research and education at the highest levels. Tulane University offers a collaborative environment for interdisciplinary interactions, a strong public service theme, and a commitment to science as a major thrust of research, scholarship, and education.

**About the Opportunity**

The successful candidate will play a central role in the development and delivery of Mechanical Engineering Studio, a sequence of hands-on, project-based courses designed to complement the traditional mechanical engineering curriculum. These courses provide students with opportunities to integrate engineering fundamentals through open-ended design, analysis, experimentation, prototyping, manufacturing, teamwork, and industry- and research-related projects.

As the mechanical engineering programs continue to grow, the successful candidate will help establish and continuously refine the Studio curriculum while also teaching additional courses within the discipline.

**Ideal Candidate Profile**

This position is particularly well suited to engineers and educators with substantial practical experience in areas such as:

* Mechanical engineering design
* Manufacturing
* Experimentation
* Product development
* Aerospace
* Robotics
* Energy systems
* Related engineering fields

Candidates with experience developing project-based, experiential, or studio-based engineering courses are especially encouraged to apply.

* Develop and teach Mechanical Engineering Studio courses.
* Design and continuously improve studio-based, experiential learning curricula.
* Contribute to the broader mechanical engineering curriculum.
* Mentor undergraduate design projects and student teams.
* Collaborate with faculty and industry partners where appropriate.
* Support the continued growth of an innovative, practice-oriented engineering program.
* Participate in departmental activities that advance teaching excellence and student success.

* Cover Letter
