Asssistant or Associate Professor - Theatre, Dance, and Multimedia Performing Arts

**FACULTY VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT**

The Department of Theatre, Dance, and Multimedia Performing Arts at Lehman College, City University of New York invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor or tenure-track / tenured Associate Professor position in Dramatic Writing beginning in the Fall of 2027.

The department presents a full mainstage season of six productions, as well as having a multimedia performing arts track that integrates live performance with digital media that focuses on student-driven work as part of its mainstage season. In addition, the department has a focus on new work for the stage and screen created by students that is presented in various

forums throughout the academic year. Full-time faculty are expected to mentor students in developing their own voices for a hybrid of stage and new media platforms.

The department is seeking candidates with specializations in dramatic writing, including but not limited to playwriting, screenwriting, digital streaming media, immersive and devised theatre, merging traditional dramatic scriptwriting with new media storytelling arts. The department is seeking candidates that can combine the pedagogy of dramatic scriptwriting with an emphasis on performance, embodiment, and somatic learning that is the signature of the department’s academic and performance work.

Candidates must demonstrate the ability to teach major courses in playwriting and screenwriting at both the introductory and advanced levels. They must also be able to teach general education courses in theatre for non-majors. Depending upon the candidate’s area of specialization, they may be asked to teach other theatre program-related courses that cover new

play development, public presentation and communication skills, business of the arts, and special topics in theatre, such as Africana Theatre and/or Latino Theatre.

Candidates must be committed to exploring innovative pedagogical techniques to promote student success. To that end, candidates must be able to address the realities of teaching dramatic writing in the age of A.I. The cognitive offloading of creative, research, and technical skills to A.I. poses pedagogical questions regarding the authenticity of the individual “voice”

and creative spirit of all students, and requires innovative teaching techniques as a result. Rather than ignoring A.I., how can pedagogy address the concerns posed by A.I. without simply saying “no” to its use? Candidates should be able to address both the drawbacks and possible uses of A.I. in their teaching with the search committee.

The starting date is August 26, 2027. The teaching load is 18 credit hours (5-6 courses) per academic year that may be taught in person or online. The successful candidate will also be expected to maintain an active creative work/research agenda in the field. For tenure-track faculty, the teaching commitment is reduced by six courses over the first five years in

order to assist with creative work/research. Tenured faculty may also receive teaching releases to assist with creative work/research. All faculty are eligible to apply for competitive internal Lehman College and CUNY grants to support their creative work/research.

Service is required for all full-time faculty, and so the successful candidate will be expected to engage in significant service activities at the departmental, college, university, professional and/or community levels, commensurate with rank. Areas of service include but are not limited to recruitment, advising, curriculum development and assessment, and production

supervision. The appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor or Associate Professor will begin Fall 2027.

Lehman College is a senior college in the City University of New York system that prides itself on its commitment to public urban higher education. Located in the Bronx, the College serves its diverse student body of more than 14,000 students by providing a liberal arts education that prepares them for employment, graduate study, and the professions. The College is a

Hispanic-Serving Institution. In 2018, Lehman College was ranked 3rd in the U.S. among four-year public institutions for economic mobility for students, and 1st in the U.S. among Hispanic-Serving Institutions with high extended upward income mobility rates.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

MFA in Dramatic Writing or PhD/DFA in Theatre by the start date of the position (August 26th, 2027).

For Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor:

Ph.D. degree in area(s) of experience or equivalent. Also required are the ability to teach successfully, demonstrated scholarship or achievement, and ability to cooperate with others for the good of the institution.

For Instructor:

Master's degree in area(s) of expertise, and/or active progress toward a Doctorate, or equivalent. Also required are the ability to teach successfully, interest in productive scholarship or achievement, and ability to cooperate with others for the good of the institution.

**COMPENSATION**

Assistant Prof: $94,017-$105,588

Associate Prof: $113,745-$125,436

CUNY offers faculty a competitive compensation and benefits package covering health insurance, pension and retirement benefits, paid parental leave, and savings programs. We also provide mentoring and support for research, scholarship, and publication as part of our commitment to ongoing faculty professional development.

**HOW TO APPLY**

For a list of all jobs available at CUNY, visit the following page: https://cuny.jobs/

Visit https://www.cuny.edu/employment/, sign in if you already have an account or register as a New User account if you do not, and search for this vacancy using the Job ID or Title. Select "Apply for Job" and provide the requested information.

Candidates must upload a Curriculum Vitae, a Cover Letter, a Dramatic Writing Sample (no more than 10,000 words), a brief Creative Work/Research Statement (1-2 pages), evidence of teaching excellence and interest in innovative pedagogy, and the names of three (3) professional references – name, title, organization, and contact information – who are familiar with the

candidate’s record of teaching and/or creative work/research. The three (3) professional references must be included in the original application to be considered. If an initial interview is requested, potential interviewees must arrange to have three (3) letters of reference submitted two weeks prior to their interview date.

For technical issues:

Contact the service desk by email: service.desk@cuny.edu. If you can, provide screenshots. Please do not provide your User Account password; it is not needed to investigate any issue.

For questions about the content of any job posting, please contact the Human Resources department: Human.Resources@lehman.cuny.edu.

**CLOSING DATE**

Please submit completed applications by November 28, 2026 for full consideration. Review of applications will begin on November 30, and continue until a candidate has been identified.

**JOB SEARCH CATEGORY**

jobs.description:
**Assistant Professor, Department of Childhood Studies**

  
  
**Rank:** Assistant Professor  
**Tenure Information:** Tenure Track  
  
**Department Summary:**  

The Department of Childhood Studies at Bridgewater State University is an inclusive, interdisciplinary community of scholars who examine the social and cultural constructions of childhood and seek evidence-based solutions to the challenges and inequities facing children and youth today. As the first interdisciplinary department and fastest-growing department at Bridgewater State University, our goals are to educate and inspire undergraduate students to think critically and to advocate for children, youth, and families locally and globally.

Our students come from diverse backgrounds and often combine Childhood Studies (CHST) with majors in fields such as Education, Criminal Justice, English, and Sociology. We emphasize engaged, inclusive teaching that helps students connect these interdisciplinary perspectives to children's lived experiences and apply their learning to advocacy and work with children, youth, and families.

We are a collaborative, and collegial department that continually reflects on assessment data to evaluate the program's impact and identify opportunities for improvement.

The department's teaching and scholarship are built around six essential concepts:

* Global challenges affecting children and childhood
* Children as active participants in research
* Childhood as a social construct
* Childism and the ways children are marginalized
* Children as beings, not “becomings”
* “Child a method” (Burman, 2018)
* Power and social justice. We support BSU's broader commitment to diversity and equity throughout all CHST coursework by identifying and addressing issues of power and privilege.

Bridgewater State University has a diverse student population, 30% students of color, 45% first-generation students, and 14% openly LGBTQ+ students. The Childhood Studies program consists predominately of female students (96%) with 22% students of color, 50% first-generation students, and 14% openly GLBTQ+.

*Bridgewater State University is an inclusive community dedicated to the lifelong success of all students; focused on the continuous improvement of its people; and is responsible for leading innovation that benefits Southeastern Massachusetts, the commonwealth, and the world. Bridgewater's accessible environment of teaching and learning stimulates critical thinking and the pursuit of new knowledge and deeper understanding. The teaching and learning environment at Bridgewater also cultivates meaningful and diverse interpersonal relationships and fosters an appreciation for global engagement aimed at transforming lives and improving the human condition. Our commitment is reflected in our* ***institutional values****, which ensure that all students are supported and succeed.*

  
  
**Essential Duties:**  

The Department of Childhood Studies (CHST) invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor. Our program serves both traditional day students and continuing studies students. The successful candidate will demonstrate a commitment to, and knowledge of teaching and learning, and supporting student well being both in-person and on-line. The position includes advising at least 30 students per semester.

You will have the opportunity to:

* Teach four Childhood Studies courses per semester, including Introduction to Childhood Studies, Service Learning in Childhood Studies, and Research Methods.
* Use innovative, learner-centered techniques and resources that support the diverse Childhood Studies student body.
* Contribute to the ongoing development, design, and enhancement of the Childhood Studies major curriculum, supporting an interdisciplinary, integrative, and inclusive approach to student learning and positive overall student experiences.

  
  
**Required Qualifications:**  

* PhD in Childhood Studies, or a related interdisciplinary field such as anthropology, cultural studies, history, geography, or a closely related interdisciplinary field
* Ability to develop and teach courses that engage critical approaches to childhood/children and youth, both face-to-face and virtually
* Evidence of an active interdisciplinary research agenda (publications, conference presentations, works in progress, or equivalent scholarly/creative activity)
* Demonstrated experience in working toward diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging in teaching, research, and/or service
* Demonstrated commitment to excellence in teaching, advising, undergraduate research mentoring, and university and community service

  
  
**Preferred Qualifications:**  

* Expertise in critical research in anthropology, history, geography, or a related field
* Experience designing and delivering online curriculum
* Experience providing academic and career advising to students
* Experience with community-engaged service and/or scholarship

jobs.title: Faculty Appointment, Religious Studies
jobs.description:
LaGrange College seeks to fill a tenure-track position at the assistant professor level in Religious Studies beginning August 1, 2027. The field of specialization is open, but preference will be given to candidates who can teach Christian ethics and broader philosophical approaches to ethics including Bioethics and possibly business ethics and the ethics of AI, as well as candidates prepared to contribute in areas such as American Christianity or world religious traditions.
  
  
A Ph.D. in religious studies or related field is required, although outstanding ABD candidates will be considered. The successful candidate must have their terminal degree completed prior to the end of their second year in the position.
  
  
The teaching load is four (4) courses per semester, including introductory courses, upper-level electives in the candidate’s field(s) of specialization, and courses that satisfy the college’s general education curriculum, known as Ethos. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to help shape the future of the major in religion and help create interdisciplinary approaches to critical analyses of American culture and society. The position includes the supervision and mentorship of undergraduate research projects in the field. Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to excellence in teaching, professional development, and institutional service, as well as an understanding of, and appreciation for, the mission of liberal arts institutions.
  
  
The religion program maintains a close relationship with the Candler School of Theology at Emory University; students interested in a future ministry career will find a direct and accelerated pathway from LaGrange College to the Candler School of Theology. Through both a solid grounding in theory and engagement in the field (via internships, collaborative undergraduate research, and other opportunities) Religious Studies students receive a thorough, intensive, and experiential education in the discipline. The program’s historic engagement in LaGrange College’s undergraduate research program affords students the opportunity to work directly with faculty on research projects that build their professional skills. The college values its relationship with the United Methodist Church and in particular its commitment to the Wesleyan ideal of service.
  
  
Interested candidates should visit https://lagrangecollege.applicantstack.com/x/openings to apply for the position and to view other positions available at the college. Required documents include:
  
  

* A letter of interest describing the alignment of the candidate’s qualifications with the position requirements
* Current curriculum vitae

* A statement of scholarly interests
* Graduate and undergraduate transcripts (copies are fine at this point)
* Contact information (only) for three professional references

Review of applications will begin Nov. 9 and will continue until the position is filled.

jobs.title: Faculty, Doctor of Executive Leadership (DEL)
jobs.description:
**Description**
**About Arkansas Colleges of Health Education**
Arkansas Colleges of Health Education (ACHE) is a private, non-profit, graduate-level health sciences institution located on over 500 acres in Fort Smith, Arkansas. ACHE’s service-driven mission is to educate and train a diverse group of competent and compassionate healthcare professionals; to create health and research support facilities; and to provide healthy living environments to improve the lives of others. Founded in 2014, ACHE has experienced rapid growth and is poised to be a leader in healthcare education for years to come. ACHE is the first and only private institution in Arkansas that is dedicated solely to healthcare and wellness, and maintains a strong commitment to the surrounding community.
  
  
**About Fort Smith And The Arkansas River Valley**
Fort Smith is a vibrant community of around 90,000, with a low cost of living and ample recreational opportunities. Located in the beautiful Arkansas River Valley at the foothills of the Ozark mountains, Fort Smith is nestled between the Ozark-St. Francis and Ouachita National Forests. The region provides hiking, mountain biking, rock climbing, hang gliding, whitewater rafting, and camping all within a short drive. In addition, the city supports a variety of cultural attractions, including museums, theaters, an award-winning symphony, and two historic entertainment districts.
  
  
**LOCATION**
This is a hybrid position. The employee will be remote the majority of the time, with the supervisor determining any residential requirements.
  
  
**Job Summary**
The Doctor of Executive Leadership (DEL) Faculty member is a collaborative educator and scholar committed to excellence in graduate education, executive leadership development, scholarship, service, and continuous program improvement.
  
  
The faculty member will contribute to the delivery and ongoing development of the Doctor of Executive Leadership program through high-quality online instruction, curriculum development, student advising and mentorship, scholarly activity, program assessment, and institutional and professional service.
  
  
The faculty member will work collaboratively with the DEL Program Director, faculty, staff, students, and institutional leadership to support the mission, vision, goals, and continued growth of the DEL program and Arkansas Colleges of Health Education (ACHE).
  
  
The faculty member will carry a teaching load as assigned based on program needs and institutional expectations and will actively contribute to the academic, scholarly, and service missions of ACHE.
  
  
**Essential Functions And Responsibilities**
**Teaching and Curriculum**

* Teach online Doctor of Executive Leadership courses within areas of demonstrated academic or professional competence.
* Provide high-quality, engaging, doctoral-level instruction appropriate for experienced working professionals and executive leaders.
* Develop, review, and revise course content, instructional materials, learning activities, and assessments.
* Ensure alignment among course learning outcomes, program learning outcomes, instructional activities, and assessments.
* Maintain current, evidence-informed course content reflecting contemporary leadership theory, organizational practice, healthcare, business, policy, and other relevant areas.
* Utilize effective online teaching methodologies and educational technologies to promote student engagement and learning.
* Provide timely, substantive, and constructive feedback on student assignments and academic performance.
* Maintain consistent course organization, communication, grading practices, and academic expectations.
* Participate in continuous curriculum review and improvement.
* Support the development of new DEL courses, concentrations, certificates, educational pathways, and other curricular initiatives as assigned.
* Maintain the security and integrity of course materials, assessments, student information, and academic records.
* Teach courses in other ACHE programs when appropriate based on expertise and institutional needs.

**Student Advising and Mentorship**

* Serve as an academic advisor and mentor to DEL students as assigned.
* Maintain appropriate availability and responsiveness to students.
* Monitor student academic progression and provide guidance when academic or professional development needs are identified.
* Provide individualized mentorship that connects doctoral education with students' professional leadership goals and organizational impact.
* Support students experiencing academic difficulty and participate in remediation activities when appropriate.
* Refer student concerns involving academic performance, professionalism, or conduct to the DEL Program Director in accordance with institutional policies.
* Support student scholarly activities, presentations, publications, professional development, and other academic opportunities.
* Promote a supportive, inclusive, professional, and academically rigorous learning environment.

**Scholarship and Research**

* Maintain an active program of scholarship appropriate to academic rank, professional expertise, and institutional expectations.
* Engage in research, applied scholarship, scholarly writing, peer-reviewed publication, professional presentations, or other recognized forms of scholarly activity.
* Pursue opportunities for collaborative scholarship with DEL faculty, ACHE faculty, students, and external partners.
* Mentor DEL students in scholarly inquiry, evidence-based leadership, research, and dissemination of scholarly work when appropriate.
* Participate in the development and evaluation of DEL program-related research and scholarly initiatives.
* Seek opportunities to translate research and professional experience into knowledge that advances executive leadership, organizational performance, healthcare, education, or other relevant fields.
* Pursue external funding, grants, or collaborative research opportunities when appropriate.
* Disseminate scholarly work at local, state, national, and international professional forums.

**Program Assessment and Continuous Improvement**

* Participate in the ongoing assessment and evaluation of the DEL curriculum and program.
* Assist with evaluation of course learning outcomes, program learning outcomes, student performance, and other measures of program effectiveness.
* Participate in the collection, analysis, and interpretation of assessment data.
* Contribute to accreditation, institutional effectiveness, and continuous quality-improvement activities as assigned.
* Participate in periodic review and revision of course materials, curriculum, academic policies, and program processes.
* Provide recommendations to the DEL Program Director regarding opportunities to improve academic quality, student outcomes, and program effectiveness.
* Maintain required academic and administrative documentation in accordance with ACHE policies and applicable accreditation standards

**Program and Institutional Service**

* Serve as a member of DEL program committees and other ACHE committees as assigned.
* Participate in faculty meetings, curriculum meetings, assessment activities, retreats, and other institutional responsibilities.
* Participate in DEL admissions activities, including applicant review, interviews, and candidate evaluation as requested.
* Support DEL orientation, information sessions, recruitment events, student activities, and other program initiatives.
* Participate in faculty governance and institutional service activities consistent with academic appointment and institutional expectations.
* Collaborate with faculty and staff across ACHE programs to advance interdisciplinary education and institutional initiatives.
* Support the mission, vision, values, and strategic priorities of ACHE.
* Participate in commencement, academic ceremonies, institutional events, and other activities requiring faculty representation as appropriate.

**Recruitment and Program Growth**

* Support recruitment and enrollment initiatives for the DEL program.
* Participate in information sessions, webinars, conferences, professional meetings, and other recruitment activities as requested.
* Engage professional networks and organizations to increase awareness of the DEL program.
* Identify opportunities for educational partnerships, professional collaborations, and student recruitment.
* Support development of relationships with healthcare systems, academic institutions, professional organizations, government agencies, military organizations, nonprofit organizations, and other potential partners when appropriate.
* Assist in identifying emerging leadership-development needs and opportunities that may inform future DEL curriculum and program growth.

**Professional and External Engagement**

* Maintain active engagement within relevant professional and academic communities.
* Represent ACHE and the DEL program professionally at conferences, meetings, educational events, and community activities.
* Participate in local, state, regional, national, or international professional service appropriate to expertise and academic role.
* Develop relationships that may contribute to educational opportunities, research, scholarship, student development, or institutional partnerships.
* Maintain professional competence and remain current within areas of academic and professional expertise.

**Faculty Responsibilities And Professional Conduct**

* Maintain professional, ethical, and collegial relationships with students, faculty, staff, institutional leadership, and external partners.
* Demonstrate reliability, accountability, professionalism, and responsiveness in fulfilling assigned responsibilities.
* Adhere to ACHE policies and procedures and applicable academic, regulatory, accreditation, and ethical standards.
* Maintain confidentiality and privacy of student, faculty, and institutional information.
* Demonstrate respect for diverse perspectives, backgrounds, professional experiences, and areas of expertise.
* Contribute to a collaborative, solutions-focused, and professional faculty environment.
* Participate in faculty development and continuing professional education as appropriate.
* Complete required institutional training and administrative responsibilities in a timely manner.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the DEL Program Director, Dean, or their designee.

**Teaching Load**

* The DEL Faculty member will carry a teaching load as determined by the DEL Program Director and institutional leadership based on program needs, faculty workload expectations, areas of expertise, and other assigned responsibilities.
* Teaching assignments may include DEL courses as well as courses in other ACHE academic programs when appropriate, based on faculty expertise and institutional needs.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the Program Director, Doctor of Executive Leadership or their designee.

**Requirements**
**QUALIFICATIONS AND CREDENTIALS**
**Education And Experience**
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Earned doctoral degree from an appropriately accredited institution in leadership, healthcare, business, education, organizational leadership, public administration, or another field relevant to the DEL curriculum.
* Credentials sufficient to qualify for academic appointment at the level of Assistant Professor or higher.
* Demonstrated experience in higher education, professional education, executive education, or a related academic environment.
* Demonstrated experience in leadership, administration, organizational management, healthcare, education, business, government, military leadership, or another area relevant to the DEL curriculum.
* Experience developing, managing, or teaching online or technology-enhanced curriculum.
* Evidence of commitment to excellence in teaching, scholarship, service, and student mentorship.
* Ability to contribute to doctoral-level education for experienced professionals and executive leaders.
* Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with faculty, staff, students, and institutional leadership.
* Strong written, verbal, interpersonal, organizational, and professional communication skills.
* Commitment to the mission, vision, and values of ACHE.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Significant progressive leadership or executive experience.
* Experience teaching at the doctoral or graduate level.
* Experience developing or delivering online doctoral education.
* Experience mentoring doctoral or graduate students.
* Record of peer-reviewed scholarship, professional presentations, applied research, or other scholarly activity.
* Experience with curriculum development, program assessment, accreditation, or institutional effectiveness.
* Experience working across disciplines or within complex organizations.
* Experience developing external partnerships, professional collaborations, or funded projects.
* Demonstrated national or international professional engagement within an area relevant to the DEL program.

**Required Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities**

* Ability to provide high-quality doctoral-level instruction in an online learning environment.
* Ability to effectively mentor and advise experienced professionals and executive-level students.
* Ability to translate theory, research, and evidence into practical leadership and organizational applications.
* Ability to critically analyze complex organizational and leadership challenges.
* Ability to design and evaluate graduate-level learning activities and assessments.
* Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple responsibilities and priorities.
* Ability to work independently while functioning effectively as part of a collaborative academic team.
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
* Ability to effectively use learning management systems, Microsoft Office, videoconferencing platforms, and other educational technologies.
* Ability to communicate and represent ACHE professionally in academic, professional, and community settings.
* Demonstrated commitment to continuous improvement, professional development, ethical leadership, and academic integrity.
* Display professionalism for the college in all communication and interactions.
* Ability to maintain confidentiality and privacy.
* Ability to prioritize and organize numerous and varied assignments.

**ABILITIES AND COMPETENCIES ESSENTIAL TO THE FUNCTION OF THE JOB**
**Communication and Comprehension**
ACHE is in full compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and does not discriminate with regard to applicants or employees with disabilities and will make reasonable accommodations when necessary. The following are essential abilities and physical requirements for all positions at the college.
  
  

* Ability to orally communicate effectively with others with strong interpersonal skills and customer service orientation.
* Ability to work cooperatively with colleagues and supervisory staff at all levels.
* Ability to understand oral and written information, using the English language, and organize thoughts and ideas into effective forms of communication.
* Ability to make decisions which range from moderate to a significant impact on the immediate work environment, as well as outside contributors.
* Possess public communication skills that allow professional representation of ACHE to a variety of business and community customers and associates.
* Strong organizational skills.

**Problem Solving**

* Intuitively able to reason, analyze information and events, and apply judgment in order to solve problems of both a routine and complex nature.
* Expertise in negotiation.

**Physical And Sensory Abilities**

* May be exposed to short, intermittent, and/or prolonged periods of sitting and/or standing in performance of job duties.
* May be required to accomplish job duties using various types of equipment/supplies to include, but not limited to pens, pencils, calculators, computer keyboards, telephone, etc.
* May be required to transport oneself to other campus offices, conference rooms, and on occasion, to off-campus sites to attend meetings, conferences, workshops, seminars, etc.
* May require significant travel or work away from campus.
* Requires attendance at events representing ACHE both within as well as outside of the college setting.
* Frequently required to work at a desk, conference table or in meetings of various configurations.
* Frequently required to see for purposes of reading matter.
* Frequently required to hear and understand speech at normal levels.
* Occasionally required to lift items in a normal office environment.
* Ability to safely lift and carry 25 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.
* Frequently required to operate office and presentation equipment.

If you need assistance in the application process because of a disability, or any other reason, please contact Vicki Broadaway, Vice President of Human Resources, at 479.308.2290 or hr@achehealth.edu.
  
  
Arkansas Colleges of Health Education is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of English and Creative Writing
jobs.description:
*Sweet Briar College* *is a liberal arts college for women with a long history of forging female leaders. Sweet Briar College is repeatedly named by* US News and World Report *as one of the most innovative liberal arts colleges in the nation. Sweet Briar College is growing rapidly, attracting students who are drawn to it for its excellent liberal arts program, coupled with distinctive programs in women's leadership, engineering, sustainability, arts, and its legendary equestrian program.*

*The College boasts a modern core curriculum focused on women's leadership in the 21st century and undergraduate programs in the arts, sciences, and humanities, as well as a Master of Arts in Teaching. It is one of only two women’s colleges in the United States with an ABET-accredited engineering degree. The* *women’s leadership core curriculum* *is innovative and energizing.*

*When students graduate, they are persuasive communicators who know how to think on their feet and bring people together. No matter* *what they study* *or where they go, Sweet Briar women are prepared to lead. The campus community is a family of faculty, staff, coaches, and alumnae who support and encourage students and each other. With a student-to-faculty ratio of 8 to 1, students lead research, ask questions, and forge supportive relationships with faculty that can last for decades.*

*As an Equal Opportunity Employer, Sweet Briar College is committed to enhancing our community and encourages applications from qualified individuals with varied backgrounds, experiences, and viewpoints who would strengthen the College.*

**Job Title**: Assistant Professor of English and Creative Writing

**Classification**: Full-time, tenure-track, benefits eligible faculty position.

**Reports To**: Arts Division Head

Sweet Briar College invites applications for a tenure-track position of Assistant Professor of English and Creative Writing, to begin teaching in Fall 2027, with a specialization in creative nonfiction. The English and Creative Writing program at Sweet Briar College employs a studio curriculum with an emphasis on project-based learning. As working writers, our faculty engage in projects that shift and develop over time and are informed by what we’re reading and what we discover as we write and by the changing world around us. English and Creative Writing courses at Sweet Briar combine the reading and discussion of classic and contemporary literature with instruction in both analytical and creative writing.

The standard teaching load is three courses per semester and includes teaching in our general education Leadership Core curriculum. The successful candidate will teach at least three sections each year of one of those Leadership Core courses, The Mindful Writer, a first-year writing course in which students receive subscriptions to the *New Yorker* magazine and use those articles as models for their own writing. Other opportunities to teach in the Leadership Core and across the curriculum are possible based on the candidate’s qualifications and interests.

Candidates ready to work with a diverse student body are especially welcome. Sweet Briar prides itself on creating a learning environment that encourages young women to fulfill their highest potential. Leadership in all walks of life is fostered by the special connections our faculty make with their students, and Sweet Briar women translate their academic experiences into interesting and important lives.

**Required Qualifications**:

jobs.description:
**Assistant Professor, Mathematics (Tenure- Track)**

  
  
**Posting Number:** F01362  
**Location:** Los Medanos College  
**Salary:**
  
  
**Description of Position:**  
Los Medanos College's Math Department has 11 full-time faculty members and is excited for a new member. With the advent of AB705/1705 the number of students enrolling in first-level transfer courses has increased. The Math department seeks faculty who are familiar with instructional techniques, institutional resources, and can direct students to the appropriate resources to support the diverse first-level transfer students. Recently, the LMC Math department has been remodeling the coursework pathways and designing new courses such as Quantitative Reasoning and even Calculus Support. This position can teach a wide variety of courses in the Math department, including transfer-level coursework and major/STEM level coursework. Other department duties will involve working with teams in meeting their goals of strategically remodeling and design to increase the quality of teaching and learning and equitable outcomes for all students taking math at LMC. Our department is committed to increasing the success and retention rates in math classes for Black students at LMC. We are also improving our curriculum to be more culturally responsive. We are looking for instructors who share a strong commitment to pedagogies that close equity gaps.  
  
**Inquiries:**  
Email Nicole Acosta at nacosta@losmedanos.edu if you have a question.
  
  
**Position Status:** Tenure- Track  
**EEO Job Category:** Faculty & Other Instructional Staff  
**Employee Group:** Full-Time Faculty  
**Department:** L5009-Mathematics  
  
**Duties and Responsibilities:**  
In addition to contractual duties, all full-time faculty are expected to participate actively in their disciplines, department activities, and the general intellectual life and governance of the college. Part of the teaching assignment may be in the evening and/or online. Duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:
  
1. advancing equitable student learning through dedicated, exemplary instruction in accordance with established course outlines;
  
2. participating in the assessment of student learning outcomes for courses and programs; developing and implementing student learning outcomes assessment processes for courses and programs;
  
3. collaborating in the development and revision of curriculum and in program review;
  
4. engaging in department program improvement initiatives;
  
5. participating in department, division, and college committees;
  
6. participating in professional development activities, both departmental and college-wide;
  
7. maintaining current knowledge in the subject matter area and effective teaching/ learning strategies;
  
8. maintaining appropriate standards of professional conduct and ethics;
  
9. informing students of course requirements, evaluation procedures and attendance requirements;
  
10. preparing and grading class assignments and examinations and informing students of their academic progress;
  
11. maintaining attendance, scholastic, and personnel records and submitting them according to published deadlines;
  
12. posting and holding sufficient and regular office hours in accordance with prevailing policy;
  
13. participating in College's shared governance processes.  
  
**Minimum Qualification-Education/Experience:**  
Master's in mathematics or applied mathematics OR Bachelor's in either of the above AND Master's in statistics, physics or mathematics education OR the equivalent. If you do not possess the listed degree, you can apply for an equivalency. You can upload a master's degree equivalency form in the attachment section of the application to explain how you possess the equivalent background.  
  
Understanding of and sensitivity to the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, sexual orientation and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, staff and faculty.  
  
**Desirable Qualifications:**  
#1: Ability and willingness to support students in various mathematics courses including courses with support, i.e., Statistics with support, Precalculus with Support, and Applied Calculus with support, Calculus, Differential Equations, Linear Algebra, and/or Discrete Mathematics. Furthermore, willingness to provide adequate support to students in order to promote success and retention.
  
  
#2: Ability to facilitate effective mathematical learning in the classroom of various teaching modalities (online synchronous, online asynchronous, face-to-face, or hybrid). Several strategies may include experience in utilizing innovative class discussions, facilitating student collaboration /group work, tutoring, discovery learning, and designing lab activities/ just-in-time support.
  
#3: Ability and willingness to integrate new and existing technology and Software/ Tools into the curriculum. These include Desmos or any calculator suite, Statcrunch, R, Geogebra, OER, etc.  
  
#4: Demonstrate experience and/or willingness to participate as a team member or leader in committees. Some examples are as follows: Math Path To Transfer, Math Teaching Communities, and Various Math Cohorts (Puente, UMOJA, Honors, etc.).  
  
#5: Have sensitivity and understanding of diverse academic socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, including those with physical or learning disabilities.

**Job Close Date:** 11/13/2026  
**Open Until Filled:** No  
**Employment Begins:** Fall 2027  
**# of Months:** 12

**Job Title**

Assistant Professor - Mathematics

**Agency**

East Texas A&M University

**Department**

Mathematics

**Proposed Minimum Salary**

Commensurate

**Job Location**

Commerce, Texas

**Job Type**

Faculty

**Job Description**

**INSTRUCTIONS TO APPLICANT****:**

During the application process the *“My Experience*” page has a section provided “*Attachments (Resume/CV, References, Cover letter, etc.)*” to upload required documents.

* Use the Upload button to add each document.
* You will be able to upload up to 5 documents. Be aware that the maximum size allowed for any one document is 5MB.
* All documents must be electronically submitted through the Texas A&M Online Employment Services website to be considered.
* Incomplete or improperly submitted applications may be excluded from consideration.
* Please do not withdraw your application in an attempt to upload a missing document, instead please email HR for help.

**Please provide the following documents**:

* Cover Letter
* Resume/CV
* Statement of Teaching Philosophy
* Statement of Research Interests
* Three professional references with complete contact information *(Unsolicited letters of recommendation will not be considered).*
* Transcripts (Unofficial will be accepted with application. Official transcripts are required upon acceptance of verbal offer).  
  *If transcripts are from an international institution, it is the responsibility of the prospective faculty member to have the transcripts translated and evaluated by an approved credential evaluator.*

If you need assistance, please contact us at HR.Hiring@etamu.edu

***A Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025. Please be advised that Texas A&M University will NOT pay this fee. Therefore, if you need immigration sponsorship for your employment, we recommend that you consult with your private immigration counsel at your own expense to ascertain whether your current immigration status would make a potential offer of employment from Texas A&M University subject to this fee.***

***In addition, on January 27, 2026, Texas Governor Abbot issued a moratorium on the filing of any new H-1B unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate.***

**SUMMARY:**

The Department of Mathematics at East Texas A&M University invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position beginning in Fall 2027. We seek a candidate with expertise in Statistics, Data Science, Machine Learning, or a closely related area. Candidates whose research connects mathematics and statistics with interdisciplinary applications, such as mathematical biology, biostatistics, artificial intelligence, computational science, or related fields, are especially encouraged to apply.

The successful candidate will be expected to teach undergraduate and graduate courses, maintain an active research agenda, mentor students, and contribute to the service mission of the department, college, university, and profession. The department is particularly interested in candidates who can support and further develop programs in Statistics and Data Science.

**DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in Mathematics, Statistics, and Data Science in face-to-face, hybrid, and online formats.
* Contribute to the development and expansion of courses and curricula in Statistics, Data Science, Machine Learning, and related areas.
* Maintain an active scholarly research program that leads to publications in peer-reviewed scholarly publications, professional presentations, and pursuit of external funding opportunities.
* Engage undergraduate and graduate students in research and mentorship.
* Advise and mentor students in academic and professional development.
* Provide service to the Department, College, University, community, and profession.
* Maintain effective, professional, and collegial relationships with faculty, students, staff, alumni, and external partners.
* Maintain on-campus office hours and participate in departmental activities.
* Serve on departmental, college, and university committees as assigned.

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:**

* **Education:** An earned Ph.D. in Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field (degree must be completed prior to the start date).
* **Experience / Knowledge / Skills:** Evidence of potential for excellence in university-level teaching. Demonstrated potential to establish and sustain a productive research program.

* **Ability to:** Ability to interact with students, staff, and faculty in a professional, collegial, and collaborative manner.
* **Licensing/Professional** **Certifications:** N/A
* **Physical Requirements:** N/A
* **Other Requirements:** NA

**PREFERRED EDUCATION / SKILLS/ EXPERIENCE:**

* Research expertise in Statistics, Data Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Computational Mathematics, or related disciplines.
* Experience teaching Statistics, Data Science, Machine Learning, or related courses at the undergraduate and/or graduate level.
* Evidence of interdisciplinary collaboration.
* Demonstrated record of scholarly publications and professional presentations.
* Success in obtaining, or strong potential to obtain, external research funding.
* Commitment to student success, mentoring, and academic excellence.

**SUPERVISION OF OTHERS:**

NA

**APPLICATION MATERIALS:**

Please submit the following at our Employment website, https://www.etamu.edu/human-resources/employment/:

* Cover Letter
* Curriculum Vitae
* Statement of Teaching Philosophy
* Statement of Research Interests
* Three professional references with complete contact information (unsolicited letters of recommendation will not be considered)
* Transcripts (unofficial transcripts will be accepted with the application; official transcripts are required upon verbal offer)

All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other information required by the institution’s procedures, including the completion of the criminal history check.

Equal Opportunity/Veterans/Disability Employer.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of English
jobs.description:
Young Harris College invites applications for a full-time, tenure track Assistant Professor of English beginning August 1, 2027. A Ph.D. in English with a specialization in Eighteenth or Nineteenth-Century British Literature and Culture is required by the time of appointment; ABD candidates nearing completion will be considered. The successful candidate will teach a range of courses, including composition, surveys of British and/or World literature, Romanticism, Victorian literature, history of the novel, and other courses related to their specialty. Young Harris College is a teaching-focused liberal arts institution that values both effective instruction and vibrant scholarly engagement. Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to undergraduate teaching, an active research agenda, and the ability to mentor students in guided research experiences.
  
  
Applications should include a two-page cover letter, an updated CV, and contact information for three professional references. Additional materials, including unofficial transcripts, statements of teaching philosophy, and sample syllabi may be requested later in the hiring process. Review of applications will begin in January 2027 and will continue until the position is filled. The selected candidate must successfully pass a background check prior to the appointment.
  
  
Young Harris College is a private baccalaureate and master’s degree-granting institution located in the beautiful mountains of North Georgia. Founded in 1886 and historically affiliated with The United Methodist Church. Young Harris College educates, inspires, and empowers students through an education that purposefully integrates the liberal arts and professional studies. Approximately 1,400 students are enrolled in its residential and Early College programs. The College is an active member of the NCAA Division II and remains a fierce competitor in the prestigious Conference Carolinas. For more information, visit yhc.edu
  
  
Young Harris College is proud of its Wesleyan heritage and commitment. The College was founded by a Methodist circuit-rider, and its namesake and sustainer during the institution’s formative years was one of the state’s outstanding Methodist laypeople. For several years, all Presidents of the College were ordained Methodist ministers, with Young Harris later appointing professional educators who were active lay leaders in the Methodist Church to the presidency.
  
  
Today, Young Harris is a member of the North American Association of Methodist Schools, Colleges, and Universities (NAAMSCU), a voluntary association of over 100 private schools, colleges, universities, and seminaries in the United States that cooperate to advance the common good of member institutions and to address issues of mutual concern to the church and the academy. Young Harris is also a member of the University Senate of the UMC’s General Board of Higher Education and Ministry (GBHEM), making the institution eligible for funding from UMC agencies. Young Harris supports the UMC’s commitment to “open hearts, open minds, and open doors.” For more information about the College’s affiliation with GBEHM, follow this link: GBHEM.
  
  
Young Harris College does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex , age, disability, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. EOE M/F/D/V local laws.
  
  
Young Harris College is committed to providing an inclusive and accessible application process for all applicants. If you need a reasonable accommodation at any point during the application or hiring process, we encourage you to contact Human Resources at hr@yhc.edu.

Faculty - Human Engineering Research Laboratories

Med-Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation - Pennsylvania-Pittsburgh - (26005723)

**The Department of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation is currently accepting applications for full-time doctoral-level faculty researchers to work within the Human Engineering Research Laboratories (HERL) at the rank of Assistant Professor, non-tenure stream.** A PhD, MD, DO, or equivalent degree in Engineering, Sciences or Medicine is required. Compensation package will be commensurate with experience and accomplishment.

Responsibilities will include:

* Secure peer-reviewed funding and collaborate in the conduct of research and development.
* Create, design, and participate in research protocols, data collection and analysis.
* Dissemination of research and development through peer-reviewed publications and presentations.
* Advise and mentor students and post-docs who are working on research and development projects.
* Serve on HERL and other committees as approved by the HERL Director.
* Engage in scholarly activity and participate as part of an interdisciplinary team to conduct and support an externally funded peer-reviewed research and development program.
* Participate in professional development activities and demonstrate leadership or leadership potential within profession.
* Represent HERL through service on university-level committees and in the broader community.

Qualifications: Candidates should have skills to be an effective faculty member. Should be an effective mentor and leader with strong interpersonal, written, oral communication skills and the ability to interact effectively with all stakeholder groups, including students, research participants, faculty, staff, and administration, as well as professional, governmental, and community partners.

The ideal candidate will:

* Possess PhD in Rehabilitation Science, Engineering, Computer Science or a closely related field.

Job Description
  
  
The Department of Engineering in The College of Science, Engineering, and Technology at Norfolk State University invites applications for a 9-month tenure-track Assistant/Associate professor in Electrical and Electronics Engineering at the Assistant/Associate Professor level to begin Fall 2027. Review of applications will begin on November 30, 2026, and continue until the position is filled. Please note that this position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.  
  
  
  
  
Responsibilities
  
  
The successful candidate will join a cohesive faculty group in Electrical and Electronics Engineering and be responsible for full participation in the management and oversight of undergraduate and graduate research and education program offerings. Faculty responsibilities include graduate and undergraduate course instruction; advising/mentoring undergraduate and graduate students; and participation in departmental activities related to the future growth and direction of Engineering Department programs. Candidates must be prepared to manage a faculty-directed research effort in support of the technical objectives of the Engineering Department.
  
  
TO APPLY AND BE CONSIDERED FOR THIS ROLE, YOU MUST APPLY USING WORKDAY: https://nsu.wd501.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/nsu/details/Assistant-Associate-Professor\_JR100420?q=electrical
  
  
Overview of the Department
  
  
Norfolk State has an emergent focus on semiconductor electronics, artificial intelligence/machine learning, bioengineering, and engineered materials with applications in areas such as biomedicine, advanced signal processing, and space-based technologies. These activities are carried out by interdisciplinary teams that include Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and Computer Science faculty. Academic degree programs supported by the Engineering Department include bachelor and master of science degree programs in Electrical and Electronics Engineering, master of science and doctoral degree programs in Materials Science and Engineering, and a bachelor of science degree program in Optical Engineering.
  
  
NSU Teaching Philosophy for Underrepresented Populations
  
  
Norfolk State University is particularly interested in candidates who have experience working with students from diverse backgrounds and a demonstrated commitment to improving access to higher education for all students regardless of background. Candidates must include a statement that reflects their philosophy and experience working with initiatives or with students and communities from underrepresented populations.  
  
  
  
Norfolk State University
  
  
Norfolk State University is a comprehensive urban public, doctoral granting institution committed to transforming students’ lives through exemplary teaching, research and service. The University is a top ranked and largest in the Commonwealth of Virginia, Historically Black College and University (HBCU) with nationally recognized STEM programs and enrolls 6,000 students in over thirty undergraduate and nineteen on-line & in-person graduate programs. Norfolk State University garners over $20M in annual grant acquisitions, has as an NCAA Division I athletic program with fifteen sports that boasts three regular season MEAC conference championships in men’s basketball, and a coveted marching band as winners of the 2024 Circle City Classic Battle of the Bands.  
  
  
  
About the City of Norfolk
  
  
Norfolk is one of seven cities that make up the Hampton Roads Region. With a population of about two million, Hampton Roads is the 33rd largest Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA) in the nation, the 8th largest metro area in the Southeast, and the 2nd largest between Atlanta and Washington, DC. It is home to the world's largest naval base, the Port of Virginia, one of the world's leading maritime gateways, and NATO’s only North American headquarters (NATO Supreme Allied Commander Transformation). By virtue of its strategic location, it is a cosmopolitan area with many minority groups from every corner of the world. Norfolk has big city amenities and attractions of arts and culture, as well as cuisines of the Eastern Seaboard and is a home port for Carnival Cruise Lines year-round with other cruise lines using Norfolk as a port-of-call. In addition, the region boasts accessible parks, riverfronts, beaches, and numerous festivals, all favorable for weekend getaways.

Portland State University is a public research university located in the heart of one of America’s most dynamic cities. Public impact research is at the heart of Portland State University’s mission as **Oregon’s Urban Research University**. PSU research prioritizes solving real-world problems that directly affect communities—whether it’s improving transportation systems, advancing sustainable urban development, or addressing pressing social and environmental challenges. By collaborating with public agencies, nonprofits, and industry partners, we ensure that PSU research doesn’t remain theoretical but instead drives meaningful change.

At Portland State University’s **Maseeh College** curiosity meets impact. Our research tackles global challenges with solutions that are inspired and developed here in the Pacific Northwest. **Job Summary:**
----------------

The Department of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Wisconsin-Madison invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Quantum Cryogenics, Thermal Management for Quantum Systems, and Quantum Infrastructure.

  
  

We seek candidates with a vision to address the engineering challenges of cooling, operating, and scaling quantum systems and to strengthen, broaden and deepen related research in the Department of Mechanical Engineering. Interests include but are not limited to: sub-kelvin refrigeration and cryocoolers; low-temperature heat and mass transfer; thermal management of quantum devices and systems; cryogenic materials, components, and instrumentation; and the integration, reliability, and scaling of quantum infrastructure.

  
  

While both theoretical and applied research is of interest, we are particularly interested in candidates that can articulate a clear vision of how their research will translate from research to practice in the broad context of Mechanical Engineering applications. Research in these areas is anticipated to enable advances in quantum computing, sensing, and communication, where cooling capacity, thermal loads, wiring, vibration, and system reliability present significant engineering challenges. We also welcome research with applications to other cryogenic technologies, including superconducting systems for fusion, space, and medicine.

  
  

The UW Mechanical Engineering Department has a longstanding strength in cryogenic engineering, grounded in experimental research on refrigeration cycles, low-temperature heat transfer, and thermal systems design. Current work includes sub-kelvin cooling, helium-3/helium-4 mixtures, superfluid transport, magnetic refrigeration, and thermal-management technologies. This expertise is complemented by broader departmental strengths in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, materials, and system integration. The successful candidate will be able to build an independent research program while collaborating with colleagues across engineering and the physical sciences, including through the Wisconsin Quantum Institute, on the infrastructure needed to operate and make https://engineering.wisc.edu/research/moonshots/>.

  
  

The department welcomes candidates who transcend the traditional boundaries of Mechanical Engineering and can incorporate insights from Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Industrial and Systems Engineering, Materials Engineering or related disciplines to holistically address high impact societal problems related to the areas described above. Candidates should articulate how their research will engage and attract Mechanical Engineering students from all backgrounds.

  
  

The Department of Mechanical Engineering advances the mission of the College of Engineering to foster a respectful and inclusive environment for all members of our community.

  
  

Additional Information:

The Department of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Wisconsin-Madison is rapidly expanding, with growing student enrollment and a dynamic wave of faculty hires, making it one of the university’s most vibrant and fast-evolving departments. The Department offers and fosters a transdisciplinary research and educational environment and provides the infrastructure to address grand technological challenges. The Department also strives to create a culture of belonging for all members of our growing department. Candidates who can contribute to these priorities are encouraged to identify their strengths and experiences in these areas in their cover letter, research statement, and/or teaching statement. Current research areas in the ME Department include aerospace, energy systems and storage, electrochemical systems, and sustainability; robotics, bio robotics, sensing and autonomous systems; computer-aided engineering, data-driven approaches, AI/ML and design; fluid and solid mechanics; renewable energy, aerodynamics, extreme mechanics, biomechanics; and advanced materials design and manufacturing. New research directions will continue to be launched and nurtured to facilitate creative solutions to transformative technical challenges.

Teaching and developing inclusive undergraduate and graduate courses for a diverse student body in the Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, and Engineering Mechanics degree programs, mentoring graduate students and supervising their research; developing and directing a successful, extramurally funded research program; participating in departmental and university faculty governance; and contributing to professional and public service.

The School of Life Sciences (SOLS) invites applications for a full-time, benefits-eligible, non-tenure-eligible Assistant Teaching Professor position with an anticipated start date of August 16, 2027. This includes supervising coursework for Applied Projects and Capstones for the Biology MS program. Responsibilities will include supervising graduate teaching assistants and updating/developing course materials with other faculty & staff. This person will also provide service within the school, college, and university in capacities appropriate for the position.

With more than 100 full-time faculty members and excellent undergraduate and graduate training programs, the School of Life Sciences (SOLS) (https://sols.asu.edu/about/mission-vision) has wide-ranging expertise across the biological sciences. SOLS supports and encourages multiple interdisciplinary research initiatives. Within The College, our faculty engage with a large, curious student body, guiding them as they grow into socially aware, critical thinkers and writers able to succeed in a wide range of careers and to address the challenges of the twenty-first century. Advancing the success of our students remains our top priority. To learn more about The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, please visit https://thecollege.asu.edu.

ASU exemplifies a new prototype for the American public research university. As articulated in the ASU Charter, ASU is a comprehensive public research university, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural, and overall health of the communities it serves.

* Supervise graduate teaching assistants

------------

Georgia College & State University (GCSU) is the state's designated public liberal arts university, where students learn the essential skills to compete in a fast-paced and technology-driven global society. The university prepares students for successful careers, leadership in communities, problem solving and life-long learning through personalized attention in a residential setting with opportunities for a variety of transformational experiences through its award-winning, high-impact practices. One of only three selective universities within the University System of Georgia and a top 10 ranked public university in the Southeast, GCSU offers undergraduate degrees in more than 40 majors, more than 30 graduate programs, doctorates in education and nursing, professional certificates, and continuing education programs.

As a member of the prestigious Council of Public Liberal Arts Colleges (COPLAC), GCSU is committed to fostering a liberal arts environment that values academic preeminence, interdisciplinary inquiry and an inclusive learning community. GCSU enjoys a strong reputation for academic excellence and nationally ranked programs according to US News & World Report, The Princeton Review and Colleges of Distinction - among other ranking sources.
  
Georgia College & State University takes great pride in combining the educational experience of a private liberal arts college with the affordability of a public university. Faculty and staff are dedicated to student engagement and experiential learning through high-impact practices such as internships, service- and community-based learning, leadership development, study abroad opportunities, mentored undergraduate research and a capstone project that fosters intellectual curiosity, reasoned inquiry and critical thinking.

The university's beautiful and historic campus is located downtown in Milledgeville, Georgia, a charming college town of approximately 19,000 residents in Central Georgia, and only 90 miles southeast of Atlanta. Milledgeville is also the home of noted American author and alumna, Flannery O'Connor, '45, and the college community enjoys many exciting literary arts programs at O'Connor's former home, Andalusia, a National Historic Landmark owned by the university. Milledgeville is located on the banks of beautiful Lake Sinclair and Lake Oconee, allowing faculty, staff and students to take full advantage of the environmental and recreational benefits of being part of a lake community. For cultural, educational and leisure opportunities beyond Milledgeville - Macon and Atlanta are located within easy driving distances.

Georgia College & State University is dedicated to protecting academic freedom in addition to supporting freedom of expression as outlined in the University System of Georgia's Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom policy and its Ethics Code of Conduct. For more information, visit us online at gcsu.edu.

**Job Summary:**
----------------

The Department of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Wisconsin-Madison invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position in aerospace structures, dynamics, and resilience. Priority areas include nonlinear structural dynamics, aircraft design and multidisciplinary optimization, aeroelasticity and flutter, stability, noise and vibration suppression, reduced-order and high-fidelity modeling, and structural health monitoring for next-generation aircraft, rotorcraft, and space vehicles, addressing emerging challenges in sustainable aviation, high-speed flight, and space exploration. We seek faculty who can bridge computational methods, experimentation, and data-driven approaches, enabling advances in lightweight aerospace structures, morphing systems, and robust dynamic response prediction under uncertainty. Successful candidates will be able to contribute to teaching and research efforts of the new Aerospace Engineering program within the Department of Mechanical Engineering.

  
  

The department welcomes candidates who transcend the traditional boundaries of Mechanical Engineering and can incorporate insights from Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Industrial and Systems Engineering, Materials Engineering or related disciplines to holistically address high impact societal problems related to the areas described above. Candidates should articulate how their research will engage and attract Mechanical Engineering students from all backgrounds.

  
  

The Department of Mechanical Engineering advances the mission of the College of Engineering to foster a respectful and inclusive environment for all members of our community.

  
  

Additional Information:

The Department of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Wisconsin-Madison is rapidly expanding, with growing student enrollment and a dynamic wave of faculty hires, making it one of the university’s most vibrant and fast-evolving departments. The Department offers and fosters a transdisciplinary research and educational environment and provides the infrastructure to address grand technological challenges. The Department also strives to create a culture of belonging for all members of our growing department. Candidates who can contribute to these priorities are encouraged to identify their strengths and experiences in these areas in their cover letter, research statement, and/or teaching statement. Current research areas in the ME Department include aerospace, energy systems and storage, electrochemical systems, and sustainability; robotics, bio robotics, sensing and autonomous systems; computer-aided engineering, data-driven approaches, AI/ML and design; fluid and solid mechanics; renewable energy, aerodynamics, extreme mechanics, biomechanics; and advanced materials design and manufacturing. New research directions will continue to be launched and nurtured to facilitate creative solutions to transformative technical challenges.

Teaching and developing inclusive undergraduate and graduate courses for a diverse student body in the Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, and Engineering Mechanics degree programs, mentoring graduate students and supervising their research; developing and directing a successful, extramurally funded research program; participating in departmental and university faculty governance; and contributing to professional and public service.

The Jindal School of Management at The University of Texas at Dallas is seeking to fill a tenure system position in accounting. Candidates will be required to conduct high-quality research and publish in top journals in the Accounting area, and to develop and teach Accounting courses at undergraduate and graduate levels.

The appointment commences for the fall 2027 semester.

**Qualifications**

Candidates are expected to demonstrate the ability to work effectively in a highly collaborative, engaging, and dynamic environment comprised of individuals with a range of backgrounds, skills, and perspectives. We are seeking candidates able to produce research and scholarly or creative achievements that enhance the program and the discipline, with the ability to deliver high-quality teaching using evidence-based practices to effectively engage students from a range of backgrounds and experiences.

Preferred Education and Experience: A minimum of three years of work experience is preferred. Candidates seeking Associate and Full Professor appointments are expected to have experience and qualifications commensurate with those positions, including well-established records of research and teaching. A record of publications in top-tier accounting journals is required.

**The** **Jindal School of Management**

The Jindal School of Management (JSOM) is the largest school in UT Dallas with an enrollment of almost 10,000 students. The successful candidate will contribute to the excellence of the academic community at JSOM and UT Dallas through collaborative, engaging, and dynamic teaching, research, and service. Based on publications in 24 top journals tracked by the UT Dallas Top 100 Business School Research RankingsTM, JSOM ranks 2nd in research productivity in North America and 2nd worldwide. We offer programs that are ranked as high as in the top 10 by *Bloomberg BusinessWeek, The Princeton Review* and *U.S. News & World Report.* Our Full-Time MBA program is ranked #12 (tied) and our Part-Time MBA program is ranked #8 (tied) among public schools by *U.S. News & World Report.* The accounting department at JSOM is committed to pursuing the mission of the school, focusing on high-quality research while providing first rate education to our students preparing them for their successful and meaningful careers.

The University promotes a welcoming environment through programs and initiatives designed to support engagement and success for members of the campus community. Employee benefits include a range of physical and mental wellness resources, competitive insurance and retirement plan options, lactation facilities located throughout the campus, and Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) comprised of individuals who share common interests to help build community among UT Dallas faculty and staff (e.g., Universal Access ERG, Military and Veteran ERG, UT Dallas Young Professionals). jobs.title: Tenure-Track: Assistant Professor of Theatrical Production Management and Research
jobs.description:
##### **Description**

The Texas A&M University College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts (PVFA) invites applications for a full-time, 9-month tenure-track position in Theatrical Production Management and Research at the rank of Assistant Professor in the Dance, Music, and Theatre Performance section. The anticipated start date is August 1, 2027.

Candidates should demonstrate strong potential for scholarly achievement and an ability to establish a nationally and internationally recognized agenda for research and creative work focused on producing and researching structures that make interdisciplinary, virtual/hybrid, media-integrated, and devised performance possible. Areas of expertise may include, but are not limited to:

* Digital Transformation and Technology

* producing and scheduling systems for media-integrated and technology-driven performance

* live streaming, virtual and hybrid producing models

* data analytics for production planning, budgeting, and audience/venue operations

* Collaborative and Non-hierarchical Producing Models

* producing structures for devised and collectively created work, where authorship and decision-making are distributed rather than script-first

* Sound and Media Design as Producing Practice

* sound design, projection/media design, and live media integration as both creative and infrastructural components of production

* Interdisciplinary Partnerships

* producing collaborations across the theatre, dance, music, and visualization programs

* engaging with emerging technology across PVFA

This position supports the College's Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre, a practice-based, devised-theatre program established in Fall 2024, and complements the program's existing technical design faculty. Successful candidates will teach Stage Management and Producing Theatre and other courses as assigned that fall within their expertise. Preference will be given to candidates who also have experience in sound and/or new media design and an interest in advancing those design dimensions of the program.

The successful candidate will be expected to:

* Establish an active, nationally and internationally visible program of research and/or creative practice investigating production management as a discipline of its own — including its digital, collaborative, and technological dimensions

* Pursue external funding to support this agenda (e.g., NEA, NEH, foundation, or industry-partnered support for producing technology, digital infrastructure, or interdisciplinary production research)

* Disseminate work through exhibitions, performances, publications, presentations, software systems, patents, or other recognized scholarly outcomes

* Contribute production-management expertise to PVFA's theatre curriculum and season, and possibly sound and/or new media design expertise, as a site for applied research and graduate/undergraduate mentorship

* Build interdisciplinary partnerships that extend production-management research into visualization, data science, or technology domains represented elsewhere in the College

* Contribute to section, college, and university service

About the College

The College of Performance, Visualization & Fine Arts was formed in 2022 at Texas A&M University, bringing together the Department of Visualization, the Department of Performance Studies, and the Dance Science Program. PVFA is built without departments. Faculty sections and academic programs sit at the college level, which places musicians, composers, actors, directors, choreographers, dancers, painters, cinematographers, technical artists, level designers, spatial audio engineers, tools programmers, ethnomusicologists, art historians, UI/UX designers, and virtual set designers in one structure rather than in separate units. The College places a heavy emphasis on collaboration and interdisciplinary work in both scholarly and creative research.

The College offers the BS, MS, and MFA in Visualization, a PhD in Visual Computing and Interactive Media, and degree programs in music, dance, and theatre. We are particularly interested in candidates whose creative and scholarly work explores generative systems, machine learning, creative coding, computational creativity, and emerging forms of AI-enabled artistic and design production.

We seek candidates whose work investigates the creative, cultural, aesthetic, and critical possibilities of machine learning, generative AI, algorithmic systems, computational visualization, procedural design, and related computational approaches to art and design.

The Section welcomes research and creative practice across areas including:

* Artificial Intelligence and Creative Practice
    
  Creative applications of intelligent systems and machine learning, human-AI collaboration, computational creativity, and emerging approaches to artistic and design production.
