  Algorithmic design, creative coding, procedural systems, computational visualization, generative workflows, and computational methods for design innovation.

  Research and creative work, including publications, that examines the cultural, social, ethical, and aesthetic implications of AI and computational technologies.

Across these areas, we are interested in how computation functions not simply as a tool, but as a medium for artistic inquiry, design research, experimentation, and creative production. We are particularly interested in candidates who demonstrate how intelligent systems, generative methodologies, and computational design function as conceptual, aesthetic, and material frameworks for contemporary artistic and design practice.

**Job Summary**

Seeking applications for a new faculty position – Assistant Professor of Educational Leadership
  
  
Area of focus: Educational policy and leadership in US K-12 education.
  
  
The University of Massachusetts Amherst is seeking qualified candidates for a new tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Educational Leadership to join the dedicated and accomplished community of faculty, students, and staff in the Department of Educational Policy, Research, and Administration (EPRA) within the College of Education.
  
  
The Department of Educational Policy, Research, and Administration (EPRA) is home to the Center for Education Policy, which houses the Massachusetts Consortium for Innovative Education Assessment and the Annual Massachusetts Educator Survey. These and other initiatives position us as active partners with school districts throughout Massachusetts and beyond. Our district partnerships are grounded in the real, articulated needs of schools, with particular emphasis on sustained, job-embedded professional learning for school leaders in areas such as instructional leadership, equity-centered practice, and organizational change.
  
  
Ideal candidates will demonstrate expertise in education policy and leadership in US K-12 education, with a research agenda that examines pressing problems of K-12 policy, leadership, and practice. We seek scholars whose work generates scholarship that not only advances theory but also informs actionable improvements in educational systems. Candidates should be prepared to contribute to interdisciplinary collaborations and leverage district partnerships to ensure programming is responsive to workforce needs and grounded in practice.

**Essential Functions**

Tenure track faculty at the University of Massachusetts are employed for 9-month contracts with opportunities to engage in additional teaching, research, and community service during summer months and intersessions.
  
  
Tenure track faculty are expected to teach two courses each semester (undergraduate and/or graduate level, in-person and/or online), maintain a robust student advising caseload, have an active research and scholarship agenda that includes procuring external funding, and provide service related to their expertise to the college, university, and community.

**Minimum Qualifications**

Successful applicants will have earned a doctorate in Education, Public Policy, or a relevant social science field. They will have broad expertise in education policy and leadership in US K-12 education, with a research agenda that examines pressing problems of K-12 policy, leadership, and/or practice and the ways these issues shape public education.
  
  
Regardless of their research focus areas, candidates must have experience working on externally funded projects and demonstrate potential to secure external funding. In addition to their research, candidates must demonstrate the ability to teach classes across multiple program levels. Specific teaching responsibilities will include relevant courses in the multi-campus undergraduate certificate in Education Policy, Research, and Leadership; the M.Ed. in Education Policy, Research, and Leadership; and the Ph.D. in Educational Leadership.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* A track record of publication in recognized outlets, with a clear research trajectory.
* Success in procuring external funding for research initiatives.
* An emphasis on educational equity and access, particularly related to underrepresented populations in educational leadership.
* Experience with program development and curriculum design at multiple educational levels.
* Experience designing or teaching in online or hybrid educational programs.
* Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across departments and with community partners.
* A record of effective mentoring and supervision of graduate students and early-career scholars.
* Experience with principal licensure programming, including familiarity with licensure requirements and pathways.

**Additional Details**

Located in the beautiful Pioneer Valley of Western Massachusetts, the University of Massachusetts Amherst is a leading center of public higher education in the Northeast. Our campus-wide strategic plan calls for our campus community to engage in work “for the common good,” and the College of Education is dedicated to advancing “education for a socially just world.” As the flagship public land-grant university of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, our mission is to expand educational access, fuel innovation and creativity, and share and use our knowledge for the betterment of society.

This position is subject to final budgetary and administrative approval.

**Working Conditions**

Work is performed in a standard office or indoor university environment and involves minimal physical exertion.

**Work Schedule and Work Arrangement**

This full-time tenure-track position starts on September 1, 2027.

**Salary Information**

The University expects to pay within an approximate range between $79,350 and $127,397.
  
  
Please note: The low end of this range is based on the minimum salary for the rank included in the collective bargaining agreement between the University and the Massachusetts Society of Professors, UMass Amherst/MTA/NEA. The high-end of the pay range reflects an increase above the median salaries at this rank within the department for faculty who may have multiple years of faculty experience. The specific pay for this position will be determined by the University based on consideration of all relevant factors, including faculty rank and required relevant certifications, when and if it decides to extend an offer of employment.

**Special Instructions for Applicants**

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. To ensure consideration for a Winter/Spring interview, we encourage you to apply no later than December 1, 2026.
  
  
Candidates must provide the following in their application package:
  
1) Cover letter that lays out your interest in this position and why you are a good fit.
  
2) Current curriculum vitae.
  
3) Statement of research outlining your accomplishments briefly, focusing on your future plans and potential fit at UMass Amherst.
  
4) Statement of teaching, including your teaching philosophy and potential courses you might offer at the undergraduate and graduate levels.
  
5) Contact information for three professional references.
  
  
Current and previous UMass employees applying for this position should expect that their past teaching, advising, and service contributions will be reviewed as part of their application. This includes, but is not limited to, review of SRTI scores and comments for each course that was taught. Individuals who have previous experience teaching at another university are strongly encouraged to provide relevant course feedback scores and comments for review by the search committee.

*This position will remain open for the time period required by any applicable collective bargaining agreement and will continue until a suitable candidate pool is identified. Interested applicants are strongly encouraged to apply early.*

jobs.description:
Req Id: 44435

Job Title: Assistant/Associate Professor in Energy Innovation - Engineering

City: West Lafayette

**Job Summary**
---------------

Purdue Engineering invites applications for multiple tenure/tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor positions as part of a cluster hire in energy innovation at our West Lafayette location, led by Purdue’s Institute for Energy Innovation (IEI) . IEI brings together faculty, students, industry, government, and community partners to develop industry-driven energy solutions. IEI seeks to ensure the availability of abundant, reliable, and affordable energy; advance U.S. energy leadership and domestic supply-chain resilience; and accelerate the translation of research into technologies that are technically sound, commercially viable, and economically scalable. Its activities are organized around five major initiatives: Grid of Tomorrow, Nuclear Energy, Battery and Energy Storage, Geothermal and Natural Gas, and Critical Materials.

  

Through this cluster hire, Purdue Engineering seeks exceptional candidates whose research interests and expertise align with one or more of the following initiatives or the crosscutting research themes described below. Research topics include, but are not limited to, the examples below:

  

1. **Grid of Tomorrow** : Power systems research to modernize the electrical grid, including grid planning and operations with large data center and industrial loads; grid data analytics and artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML); grid flexibility; large-scale integration of distributed energy resources and storage; power electronics; protection; and power system dynamics.

2. **Nuclear Energy** : Nuclear power technologies, including small modular reactors and microreactors for distributed energy generation and industrial applications; advanced reactor technologies, nuclear materials, and the nuclear fuel cycle; fusion and plasma engineering; tritium production, handling, and management; and integration of nuclear energy with electrical grids and industrial energy systems.

3. **Battery and Energy Storage** : Resilient and sustainable energy-storage architectures; next-generation battery chemistries, including those using earth-abundant materials; and storage solutions for electrified mobility, aviation, defense, and the electrical grid. Across these areas, topics of interest include novel metrology, characterization, analytics, predictive modeling, safety, recycling, and scalable manufacturing.

4. **Geothermal and Natural Gas** : Technologies that provide reliable and abundant sources of electricity, industrial heat, and fuels, including geothermal resource development and energy systems; efficient utilization and catalytic conversion of natural gas and light hydrocarbons; carbon management; and engines and combined heat and power.

5. **Critical Materials** : Materials innovation and resilient domestic supply chains for energy technologies, including the discovery, design, synthesis, characterization, recovery, separation, purification, recycling, and scalable manufacturing of critical materials used in batteries, magnets, semiconductors, nuclear systems, and other energy technologies, as well as alternatives that reduce dependence on scarce materials.

  

Across these initiatives, we welcome research on **Energy Utilization** , including heat pumps and industrial efficiency. Examples include technologies that improve energy efficiency in chemical, cement, and steel processing. We also welcome research on energy systems integration and engineering approaches that incorporate techno-economic analysis, energy markets, supply chains, and deployment. Opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and industry engagement are central to IEI’s mission.

**Qualifications**
------------------

Applicants must hold a Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a closely related discipline by the start of employment. Early-career applicants should show evidence of initiating independent research, while mid-career applicants should demonstrate a sustained record of independent research within academic or industrial organizations, and contributions to education and/or mentoring. Successful candidates will be expected to conduct original research, attract external research support, advise graduate students, teach undergraduate and graduate courses, and contribute service to their academic unit, the College of Engineering, Purdue University, and the broader profession.

  

Appointments will be made in the academic school within Purdue’s College of Engineering that most closely aligns with each candidate’s background and research expertise. Applicants interested in a position in any of Purdue’s engineering schools are welcome to apply. Successful candidates will also engage with IEI and collaborate across disciplines to develop research and education programs and partnerships in energy innovation.

**Institute and College**
-------------------------

The Institute for Energy Innovation connects Purdue’s strengths in engineering and science with expertise in business, economics, and policy. Through interdisciplinary research, hands-on education, and partnerships with industry, government, and national laboratories, IEI helps faculty translate fundamental discoveries into practical energy technologies. Its industry engagement brings research needs and deployment challenges into academic collaborations and prepares students to contribute to the energy workforce. Purdue Engineering is renowned for top-notch faculty and students, unique research facilities and innovations, and a culture of collegiality and persistent pursuit of preeminence. As one of the top ranked and largest engineering colleges in the nation, we are the first among U.S. engineering colleges in annual graduates and market demand, and have 8 degree programs ranked in the top 10 nationally. Purdue Engineering is a top-ranked college for patents and translation of our research activities to practice in the state, nation, and world. More than 70 Purdue Engineering faculty and alumni are National Academy of Engineering members, and we look to continue bringing outstanding faculty to campus, remaining the leader in affordable excellence at scale by guiding strategic growth through investment in people, exciting initiatives , and facilities .

**Application Process**
-----------------------

Applicants should submit the following materials to this site:

  

1. A cover letter identifying the IEI initiative or initiatives, or crosscutting research themes, most closely aligned with the applicant’s expertise and the engineering school of primary interest;

2. A complete curriculum vitae;

3. A research statement (maximum two pages, excluding references) describing the applicant’s research accomplishments and future plans, including their alignment with IEI and opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and technology translation;

4. A teaching statement (maximum two pages, excluding references) describing the applicant’s interests and approach to undergraduate and graduate education and student mentoring; and

5. The names and contact information of at least four references.

  

Review of applications will begin on November 9, 2026 and will continue until the positions are filled. Questions regarding the positions or application process may be directed to Purdue Engineering Academic Affairs, coeacademicaffairs@purdue.edu . A background check is required for employment in these positions.

  

Purdue University and the College of Engineering offer a Concierge Program that provides dual-career assistance and relocation services.

  

*Purdue University is an equal opportunity/equal access university.*

jobs.description:
PCN 2094

**Position Overview:**

The Girard School of Business at Merrimack College invites applications for a full-time, open-rank, Non-Tenure Track (NTT) faculty position in Marketing beginning in Fall 2027.

The Girard School is seeking a faculty member who can help build a distinctive model of business education and applied scholarship at the intersection of marketing, analytics, artificial intelligence, technology, and the future of work. We are particularly interested in candidates who combine meaningful professional or industry experience with a strong commitment to teaching, scholarship, and external engagement.

This position is part of a broader strategic investment in faculty, research, experiential learning, and industry engagement within the Girard School. The successful candidate will have an opportunity to play a formative role in the development of the School's emerging Center for the Future of Work, an interdisciplinary research and engagement platform focused on understanding how technological, economic, demographic, and other forces are reshaping work and organizations.

Located in the Merrimack Valley, the School is particularly interested in leveraging the region's concentration of companies, industries, communities, and organizations as a setting for applied inquiry and partnership, while building relationships that extend nationally and globally.

The Center will seek to bridge academic inquiry and industry practice by working directly with organizations to identify consequential challenges, conduct applied research, engage students in real-world problem solving, and translate insights into scholarship, teaching, and broader thought leadership. The Center's work will be complemented by Applied Industry Labs that bring faculty, students, and industry partners together around real-world organizational and industry challenges.

**Responsibilities**

* Teach undergraduate and graduate Marketing courses consistent with the candidate's expertise and the needs of the Girard School, including courses related to marketing analytics and/or emerging technologies;
* Maintain an active program of applied scholarship and thought leadership focused on consequential problems facing organizations and industries. Relevant outputs may include applied research, white papers, industry reports, case studies, conference presentations, practitioner publications, and other work that advances knowledge and informs practice; ;
* Develop relationships with companies and other external organizations that can support research, experiential learning, and student engagement;
* Translate industry challenges and organizational data into opportunities for faculty research, student projects, cases, simulations, and other forms of applied learning;
* Contribute to the development of the Center for the Future of Work, related Applied Industry Labs, and the Girard School's broader capabilities in analytics and data-informed decision-making;
* Mentor undergraduate and graduate students and engage students meaningfully in research and applied projects;
* Contribute to the intellectual life, service, and strategic development of the Girard School and Merrimack College.

**Qualifications**

We are especially interested in candidates who are comfortable operating across academic and industry environments—individuals who can engage executives and organizational leaders, identify important questions emerging from practice, study those questions rigorously, and bring the resulting insights into the classroom and scholarly community.

The Girard School welcomes candidates whose careers have crossed traditional boundaries between industry and academia, including accomplished executives and senior practitioners who have developed or are developing a substantive scholarly and teaching agenda.

Relevant areas of scholarly and professional interest may include, but are not limited to:

* marketing analytics and data-driven decision-making;
* artificial intelligence and marketing;
* consumer analytics and customer insights;
* digital marketing and emerging technologies;
* marketing technology and automation;
* customer experience and personalization;
* AI-enabled communication and content creation;
* human-AI collaboration in marketing decision-making;
* responsible use of AI, data, and algorithms in markets; and
* the changing role and skills of marketing professionals.

Candidates need not specialize in all—or any particular combination—of these areas. Of greater importance is an intellectual agenda that addresses consequential problems facing contemporary organizations and lends itself to meaningful engagement with industry.

**Required Qualifications**

* A doctorate or appropriate terminal degree in Marketing, Business Administration, Analytics, or a closely related field by the time of appointment.
* Demonstrated ability or strong potential to teach effectively at the undergraduate and graduate levels.
* Evidence of an active or emerging scholarly agenda, appropriate to the candidate's career stage, with interest in producing applied scholarship that addresses consequential organizational, market, or industry challenges.
* Demonstrated interest in engaging organizations and translating real-world challenges into scholarship and/or student learning.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Significant professional or industry experience in marketing, analytics, consumer insights, technology, consulting, digital strategy, or related areas.
* Experience applying analytics, artificial intelligence, or marketing technologies to organizational problems and decision-making.
* A record of applied research, thought leadership, industry presentations, or other work that bridges scholarship and practice.
* Experience developing relationships across industry, academia, or regional economic ecosystems.
* Interest in building new programs, research initiatives, partnerships, or experiential-learning models.
* Evidence of the ability to engage students from varied academic and professional backgrounds.

**Application Materials Should Include:**

* Curriculum vitae
* Cover letter stating motivation and interest in the position, citing experience relevant to the qualifications and experience associated with key responsibilities for the position including teaching philosophy and evaluations.
* Contact information for three professional references (name, title, address, phone number, email address). References will be contacted only at a later stage of the search process.

**Compensation**

The expected 9-month base salary range for the Assistant Professor or Assistant Professor of Practice rank is $80,000-$110,000; for the Associate Professor or Associate Professor of Practice $110,000,000-$130,000; for the Professor or Professor of Practice $130,000-$150,000. The actual pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as, but not limited to, candidate qualifications and prior experience, scope of responsibilities, internal equity, and market considerations.

**Work Location**

This is an on-campus position as employees are essential in order to provide a fully on-campus,

residential college experience for our students and the community.

This position is subject to the successful completion of a criminal background check.

**Statement on Our Mission**

Merrimack College is a Catholic Augustinian institution of higher education committed to building an accepting and respectful community. Our mission is to enlighten minds, engage hearts and empower lives and is inspired by our Catholic faith and the Augustinian tradition of seeking truth through inquiry and dialogue.

Merrimack College seeks candidates who understand, respect, and can contribute to Merrimack’s Catholic and Augustinian mission. All candidates should describe in their application how they will foster a culture that supports our mission.

**About Merrimack College**

The only Catholic, Augustinian institution of higher education in New England, Merrimack College is a private, independent, coeducational institution with more than 4,100 undergraduate, 2,500 graduate students and 50 doctoral students from 48 states and 63 countries. The College features more than 160 career-focused undergraduate, professional and graduate programs, all taught by exceptional faculty who are passionate about their subject and student success. The College has six schools: arts and sciences, engineering and computational sciences, nursing and health sciences, education and social policy, the Girard school of business and the graduate school of counseling and social work. The College’s suburban 220-acre campus is just north of Boston in North Andover, Massachusetts. Merrimack is a Master’s Colleges and Universities/Larger Programs (M1) institution in the Carnegie Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. Merrimack is one of the fastest growing educational institutions in the country and has steadily climbed up in the U.S. News & World Report’s ranking of Best Colleges, ranking 38th in the Regional Universities North category in 2026. Merrimack is a NCAA Division I athletic institution.

**About Us - Values Overview**

Welcome to the University of North Texas System. The UNT System includes the University of North Texas in Denton and Frisco, the University of North Texas at Dallas and UNT Dallas College of Law, and University of North Texas Health Fort Worth. We are the only university system based exclusively in the robust Dallas-Fort Worth region. We are growing with the North Texas region, employing more than 14,000 employees, educating a record 49,000+ students across our system, and awarding nearly 12,000 degrees each year.

We are one team comprised of individuals who are committed to excellence, curiosity and innovation. We are transforming lives and creating economic opportunity through education. We champion a people-first values-based culture where We Care about each other and those we serve. We believe that we are Better Together because we foster an environment of respect, belonging, and access for all. We demonstrate Courageous Integrity through setting exceptional standards and acting in the best interest of our communities. We are encouraged to Be Curious about opportunities for learning, creating, discovering, and innovating, and are encouraged to learn from failure. Show Your Fire by joining our team and exhibiting your passion and pride in your work as part of our UNT System team.

Learn more about the UNT System and how we live our values at www.UNTSystem.edu.

  

**Department Summary**

The University of North Texas is a Carnegie R1 research university located in Denton, Texas, within the vibrant and rapidly growing Dallas–Fort Worth metropolitan area. The G. Brint Ryan College of Business is accredited by AACSB International and offers undergraduate, master’s, doctoral, and professional programs designed to prepare students for leadership in an increasingly complex global economy.  
  
The Department of Supply Chain Management is an academic department within the G. Brint Ryan College of Business at the University of North Texas. The department’s mission is to advance supply chain knowledge and practice through impactful research, innovative education, meaningful industry engagement, and the development of students who are prepared to lead in complex and rapidly changing organizations.  
  
The department offers academic programs at the bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral levels. Its undergraduate portfolio includes the Bachelor of Science in Supply Chain Management with concentrations in Logistics, Operations Management, Aviation Logistics, Purchasing, and Supply Chain Analytics. The department also supports the Bachelor of Science in Industrial Distribution.  
  
UNT’s supply chain programs are distinguished by innovative curricula, experiential learning, strong employer relationships, and extensive engagement with the Dallas–Fort Worth business community. The undergraduate supply chain program was ranked No. 4 in Gartner’s 2024 Supply Chain University Top 25, reflecting its academic quality, industry relevance, and commitment to preparing students for successful careers.  
  
Department faculty conduct basic and applied research across a broad range of supply chain topics, including logistics, sourcing and procurement, operations management, transportation, supply chain analytics, technology, resilience, risk, sustainability, and complex systems. Faculty members publish in leading academic journals, collaborate with industry and government partners, mentor doctoral students, and contribute leadership to major professional and scholarly organizations.  
  
The department benefits from its relationship with the Center for Logistics & Supply Chain Management and the Center for Strategic Sourcing. These partnerships support student development, industry engagement, applied research, executive education, scholarships, internships, and collaboration with organizations throughout the Dallas–Fort Worth region and beyond. UNT’s location in one of North America’s most important logistics and distribution hubs provides exceptional opportunities for research, teaching, and industry collaboration.  
  
UNT has a highly diverse campus with a wide range of languages spoken in addition to English. We welcome candidates who have experience with HSI/MSIs and/or who speak Spanish, Vietnamese, American Sign Language, Chinese (Cantonese, Mandarin and other variations), Arabic, Tagalog, Farsi, French, or/and Yoruba.

**Position Overview**

The Department of Supply Chain Management in the University of North Texas G. Brint Ryan College of Business invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor of Supply Chain Management. The anticipated appointment will begin Fall 2027 and will be based primarily on the UNT Denton campus.
  
  
The successful candidate will maintain an active program of high-quality research with the potential for publication in leading supply chain management, logistics, operations management, or related business journals. The candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate courses, contribute to the department’s academic programs, mentor students, and participate in service activities appropriate to rank.  
  
The department welcomes candidates whose research and teaching interests fall within supply chain management. Areas of particular interest may include:  

* Logistics and transportation
* Sourcing, procurement, and supplier management
* Operations and process management
* Supply chain analytics and artificial intelligence
* Supply chain technology and digital transformation
* Sustainability and circular supply chains
* Aviation logistics
* Humanitarian, healthcare, public-sector, or defense supply chains

  
Candidates with complementary expertise that strengthens or expands the department’s existing capabilities are also encouraged to apply.  
  
The successful candidate will be expected to:  

* Develop and sustain a productive, high-quality research program with the potential for publication in leading peer-reviewed journals.
* Teach supply chain management and related courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels.
* Deliver courses in face-to-face, online, hybrid, or other formats consistent with departmental needs.
* Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of departmental curricula and academic programs.
* Mentor undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral students.
* Collaborate with faculty members on research, teaching, and program initiatives.
* Pursue external research funding or industry-supported research when appropriate.
* Engage constructively with the department’s industry partners, centers, alumni, and professional communities.
* Participate in departmental, college, university, and professional service.
* Support the university’s commitment to student success and an inclusive learning and working environment.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* A doctoral degree in supply chain management, logistics, operations management, purchasing, transportation, industrial engineering, or a closely related field from an AACSB-accredited institution by the time of appointment, or have equivalent applied experience in accordance with faculty credentialing guidelines
* Evidence of the ability or potential to conduct high-quality scholarly research.
* Evidence of the ability or potential to publish in respected peer-reviewed journals.
* Evidence of the ability or potential to provide effective university-level instruction.
* Strong communication skills.
* Candidates who are ABD will be considered, provided that all doctoral degree requirements are completed before the appointment begins.

  
Employees in this job may be responsible for conducting research on, working on, or having the ability to access critical organizational infrastructure and they must be able to maintain the security and integrity of the infrastructure related to this role.

**Preferred Qualifications**

Preference may be given to candidates who demonstrate:  

* A clearly defined research agenda with strong potential for publication in leading journals.
* Publications or manuscripts under advanced review in recognized supply chain management, logistics, operations, or related journals.
* Expertise that complements the department’s existing research and teaching strengths.
* Experience teaching supply chain management or related courses.
* The ability to teach across multiple levels and instructional formats.
* Experience working with doctoral students or participating in doctoral education.
* Potential to secure external research support.
* Interest in interdisciplinary, industry-engaged, or applied research.
* Experience developing relationships with companies, government agencies, professional associations, or other external organizations.
* A record of collegiality and the ability to collaborate effectively with faculty, staff, students, and external partners.

**Position Summary**
Albany College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences invites applications for a full-time non-tenure track Principal Faculty position within our emergent Master of Physician Assistant Studies program (ARC-PA site visit scheduled for January 2027). This 12-month position is an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic, engaged individual to help shape an innovative PA program and prepare aspiring PAs for transformative health careers to solve problems that change the world. The Principal Faculty member will be primarily responsible for teaching and assessment of various professional and clinical topics throughout the didactic and clinical curriculum. The individual will work closely with the Program Director and other faculty members to ensure that students achieve the required program learning outcomes and entry level PA professional competencies. The individual will also be actively involved with student advising, admissions, new student orientation, faculty meetings and committees, and accreditation. Academic rank and salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. All applicants must be available to report in person at the campus in Albany, NY.
  
  
Albany College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences (ACPHS) is a private institution with a 140+ year tradition located in Albany, NY. ACPHS offers a comprehensive benefits package and competitive salary. The Albany area is a central hub in upstate New York—the Adirondacks, Boston, Montreal, and New York City are all within 3 hours driving distance. Additional information about ACPHS and the working environment can be found at https://www.acphs.edu . Applications consisting of a letter of interest, curriculum vitae, statement of teaching philosophy, and contact information of three references should be submitted at https://employment.acphs.edu. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. ACPHS is an equal opportunity employer.
  
  
**Major Duties & Responsibilities**

* Provide student instruction in a broad range of clinical topics within the classroom, in small groups and in the Physical Exam laboratory.
* Evaluate student performance in assigned courses and identify student learning deficiencies.
* Provide remedial instruction in assigned courses.
* Coordinate/direct instruction in assigned courses including preparation of course syllabus, course LMS site, exam creation and administration, reporting of student performance, and analysis of assessments.
* Perform student advisement and academic counseling.
* Assist the program director, medical director and clinical coordinator in clinical site recruitment, evaluation and maintenance.
* Assists in the development, implementation, and continuous review of the program's curriculum.
* Assist the program director with program self-assessment, and accreditation maintenance.
* Participate in student recruitment, admissions and selection processes.
* Provide service to the department, college, community, and profession.
* Other duties as assigned by the program director, chair of the Department of Allied Health Sciences, and dean of the School of Health Sciences.

**Knowledge, Skills And Abilities**

* Demonstrate the ability to work independently with little direction and work confidentially with discretion.
* Demonstrate dedication to the mission of the department and the College.
* Demonstrate attention to detail.
* Demonstrate excellent organizational skills.
* Demonstrate excellent oral and written communication skills.
* Demonstrates a positive attitude and work ethic.
* Interact professionally and effectively with all members of the College community.
* Demonstrate efficiency by observing schedules and meeting assignment deadlines.
* Demonstrate willingness to proactively identify and pursue relevant learning and professional development opportunities, and apply new knowledge, insights, and skills to enhance work results.

**Education And Experience**

* Doctoral degree in a scientific or medical field.
* A minimum of three years of experience in higher education
* Experience in PA education preferred

**Physical Demands**
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; and talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, and the ability to adjust focus. Please note that this posting is not all-inclusive of the job responsibilities or qualifications of the position. The essential functions of the job may or may not have been fully described for purposes of ADA reasonable accommodation. All accommodation requests will be reviewed and evaluated on a case-by-case basis.
  
  
**Work Environment**
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is not substantially exposed to adverse environmental conditions.
  
  
**Additional Information**
This position is based in Albany, NY. The duties and responsibilities of this particular role require the need for consistent, in-person collaboration and/or interaction with our community, requiring all work to be performed full-time on-site. Standard work hours are from 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM EST, Monday through Friday. Additional details pertaining to this position will be discussed during the interview process.
  
  
**Benefits**
Albany College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences (ACPHS) offers a comprehensive benefits package for full-time employees including medical, dental and vision benefits, free life insurance and disability programs, tuition assistance programs, retirement plan with employer match and contribution, and generous time off including 20 paid holidays plus paid sick and vacation time. Additional perks include wellness rewards, free gym access, free parking, identity theft protection and many others. Please note, benefits and benefits eligibility can vary by position, and exclusions may apply for some roles.
  
  
ACPHS is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate against any protected class of job applicant or employee in our hiring and employment practices.

jobs.description:
How to Apply
  
  
The confidential review of applications will occur as they are received and will continue until the position is filled. A cover letter, attached as the first page of your Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded online via the http://careers.umich.edu/ (U-M Careers website) for this Job ID 283050.
  
  
**Additional Required Materials (submitted Via Email)**
In addition to applying online, applicants are requested to send the following materials to the UMSN Office of Human Resources via email to [email protected] - please put in the subject line that you are applying for the Mary Lou Willard French Endowed Chair opportunity.
  
  

* Teaching and Mentorship Statement (2 pages maximum):

Describe your philosophy, accomplishments, and impact as an educator and mentor in oncology nursing. Highlight contributions that have advanced the development of the oncology nursing workforce and improved learning outcomes across educational settings.
  
  

* Scholarship and Research Statement (2 pages maximum):

Describe the body of scholarship that best represents your contributions to oncology nursing and cancer care. Discuss three to five representative scholarly works within the narrative, emphasizing their scientific, clinical educational, or policy impact and their influence on the field.
  
  

* Leadership, Service, and Professional Impact Statement (1-2 pages maximum):

Describe your leadership and service contributions to oncology nursing, health care organizations, professional societies, and communities. Highlight activities demonstrating sustained impact on the profession, cancer care delivery, advocacy, health equity, or patient and family outcomes.
  
  
If selected to move forward in the process, applicants will be asked to submit additional materials as noted in the School of Nursing Faculty Handbook, including professional letters of recommendation, transcripts of your highest degrees, and complete compliance requirements. For further information regarding these positions, please contact [email protected].
  
  
Responsibilities\*
  
  
The University of Michigan School of Nursing (UMSN) invites distinguished nurse scientists to apply for the Mary Lou Willard French Endowed Chair. Appointment will be at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor with tenure, commensurate with the successful candidate's qualifications and experience. Candidates should demonstrate excellence in funded research, oncology nursing, interdisciplinary team science, and the mentorship of emerging investigators. They should also have a sustained record of scholarly productivity and impact, as well as experience integrating research and scholarship with teaching and service in undergraduate and/or graduate programs.
  
  
The recipient of the Mary Lou Willard French Endowed Chair will advance a nationally or internationally recognized program of research focused on nursing care for people living with cancer and their families. The recipient will have opportunities to collaborate closely with faculty across the UMSN, Michigan Medicine, and the University of Michigan Rogel Cancer Center, as well as with national and international partners and funding organizations. Michigan Medicine and the Rogel Cancer Center offer an outstanding environment for interdisciplinary research, education, clinical innovation, and patient care, providing a strong foundation for scholarship that improves outcomes for the cancer population.
  
  
The UMSN is a vibrant community of scholars, educators, clinicians, and innovators embedded within one of the world's leading public research universities. Consistently ranked among the nation's top nursing schools, we are committed to advancing health and health equity through research, education, leadership, and service. Our faculty generate knowledge that improves lives, informs policy, strengthens healthcare delivery, and addresses pressing local and global health challenges.
  
  
UMSN faculty benefit from exceptional opportunities to collaborate across nursing, medicine, public health, engineering, data science, and the social sciences. Supported by a premier academic health system and a robust culture of mentorship and faculty development, our researchers are positioned to advance bold ideas, foster meaningful partnerships, and create solutions that improve the health and well-being of individuals, families, and communities.
  
  
The successful candidate will advance oncology nursing science, lead interdisciplinary investigative teams, mentor the next generation of nurse scientists, and contribute to the school's education, leadership, and service missions.
  
  
The University of Michigan is a world-class research institution offering an exceptional environment for education, patient care, and research. Learn more about the University of Michigan School of Nursing, Michigan Medicine, and the Rogel Cancer Center.
  
  
This position is anticipated to be filled during the 2027-2028 academic year. All qualified candidates, including individuals from groups underrepresented in nursing, are encouraged to apply.
  
  
Required Qualifications\*
  
  

* Demonstrated expertise in oncology nursing
* Earned PhD in Nursing with scholarly credential commensurate with appointment at senior rank (Associate Professor or Professor)
* Current Michigan nursing license is required or eligibility for a nursing license in the State of Michigan
* Sustained record of first-authored and/or last-author, database, peer-reviewed publications, and presentations
* Excellent communication, networking, and relationship-building skills
* Sustained record of excellence in teaching, including mentoring experience with advanced students and early career faculty
* Sustained and growing record of scholarly eminence, which advances the frontier of knowledge
* A national, and preferably internationally, reputation for outstanding and continuing achievements in the field of oncology nursing
* A reputation, supported by documented external evaluation, which recognizes the presence of leadership and the quality of research activities, publications, and contributions to the profession in comparison with other professors
* A continuing record of recognized accomplishments in academic, professional and community service
* Prior to start date must be in compliance with all health requirements, including standard precautions such as Basic Life Support (BLS) certification, orientations, licenses/certifications, policies and procedures both internal and external to the University for your assigned classroom(s) and/or clinical site(s) and/or research site(s)
